ld.name: The Lincoln Hotel in Biddeford
ld.description: A beautiful red-brick industrial building from the early 1900s is the raw material for the Lincoln Hotel, a 33-room luxury boutique hotel that is, by a considerable distance, the most attractive lodging in the riverside town of Biddeford, Maine. This old textile mill retains many of its original, well-worn architectural features, and they’re complemented by an eclectic array of interventions, some clean-lined and modern, others elegantly Art Deco or whimsically postmodern. The rooms benefit from warehouse-style high ceilings; there’s a rooftop pool, a café, a lobby bar, and a restaurant, Batson River Brewing and Distilling.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Tower at The Boca Raton in Boca Raton
ld.description: The century-old Boca Raton Resort is the sort of multi-hotel mega-complex rarely seen this side of Vegas, and its most luxurious lodging is luxurious indeed — the ultra-luxe Tower was thoroughly renovated in 2022 by the Rockwell Group, one of the big names in American luxury hospitality design. The result is on a level with anything in South Florida: chic and contemporary yet imbued with a strong sense of place, and equipped with top-flight comforts. Resort amenities include a beach club, multiple pools, an expansive spa, and a long list of upscale dining and drinking venues.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Beach Plum Farm Cottages in Cape May
ld.description: The southernmost point on the Jersey Shore, Cape May has little in common with the resort towns to its north. The town’s Victorian mansions are authentic examples of the form, and a mile to the west of town, Beach Plum Farm occupies 62 bucolic acres of verdant agricultural land. To the working farm have been added six guest houses, some renovated, some new: three barns and a three cottages, to be precise.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ivey's Hotel in Charlotte
ld.description: The Ivey’s Hotel stands in Uptown Charlotte on the site of the historic department store that gave it its name; though it’s rooted in local history, this is no retro affair, but a thoroughly modern luxury boutique hotel, and one of the top lodgings in town. With just 47 rooms and suites it feels rather more intimate than you’d expect from a former department store, and the accommodations themselves are swanky and more than a little bit residential in aspect. There’s a Church and Union steakhouse on the ground floor, and the rest of Uptown Charlotte is chock full of bars and restaurants.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fairmont Hotel Macdonald in Edmonton
ld.description: There’s still nothing else in North America quite like Canada’s string of grand railway hotels; the MacDonald, formally known as the Fairmont Hotel Macdonald, is an incongruously old-fashioned structure, a storybook French Renaissance castle standing by the banks of the North Saskatchewan River. What’s inside, however, is a perfectly contemporary luxury hotel, in classic Fairmont style, featuring handsome and well-equipped rooms and suites, and, at the top end, lavish suites named for Winston Churchill, King Edward VIII, and Queen Elizabeth II. No surprise, then, that among the MacDonald’s culinary offerings is a highly regarded afternoon tea.
ld.petsAllowed: We adore our VIPs (Very Important Pets)! Your furry companions are warmly welcome to join you for a daily fee of $35 CAD + GST per pet, which includes a $5 CAD donation to the Canadian Guide Dogs for the Blind.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Prospect Berkshires in Egremont
ld.description: Tucked into a quiet corner of North Egremont, Prospect is more than just a retreat, it is a reawakening. The lake does most of the talking, catching the light at all hours, while a chorus of rustling maples and wind chimes fills the gaps. This is a place shaped by intention, from the hand-built Scandinavian-style cabins and restored wetlands to the Cliff House’s suspended porch and knockout views of the Taconic Range. Come for the lake. Stay for the reminder that you don't need much to feel full.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Harbor House Inn in Elk
ld.description: Perched on a craggy cliff overlooking the Pacific Ocean, the Harbor House Inn enjoys a prime location in one of the most scenic stretches of northern California. Far from a hot spot with a buzzy scene, this corner of the state, most of the way to Mendocino, is where guests come to unwind from the pressure of the modern world. Indeed, with cell signals often cutting out as guests make their way along the wild coastline, it’s a place that’s remarkably free from distractions.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed at Harbor House Inn, however, per ADA guidelines,  Service Animals are permitted.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: El Cielo Resort Valle de Guadalupe

address.streetAddress: Carretera El Tigre-El Porvenir Km 7.5 Parcela 117, El Porvenir, Valle de Guadalupe

ld.name: El Cielo Resort Valle de Guadalupe in Ensenada
ld.description: Imitation is a form of flattery in the Valle de Guadalupe, where many luxury hotels and wineries are Mediterranean in style, with ideal grape-growing conditions — sunny days and cool nights — to match. One example is El Cielo Resort, with Tuscan-inspired villas set amid picturesque vineyards and olive groves. Yet there’s plenty of Mexican character to the interiors outfitted in native wood and stone, not to mention inside its excellent restaurant specializing in Baja-Yucatán fusion cuisine.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Armstrong Hotel in Fort Collins
ld.description: Fort Collins, Colorado is a college town, home to Colorado State University; it’s also an adventure town, located at the foot of the Rockies, an hour north of Denver. It’s also, of course, a classic Old West town, and by the standards of Old Town Fort Collins, the 1923-vintage Armstrong Hotel is a relative newcomer. In advance of its 100th birthday it’s been thoroughly updated, brought up to modern boutique-hotel standards, with swanky, stylish rooms and a pair of highly regarded dining and drinking venues: the underground Ace Gillett’s Lounge and the street-level Ace Café, as well as the sunny Mugs Coffee Lounge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Elizabeth Hotel, Autograph Collection in Fort Collins
ld.description: It’s a sign of how far Fort Collins has come that Colorado’s second university town should have a hotel in Marriott’s Autograph Collection of luxury boutique hotels. The Elizabeth is set in the vibrant Old Town district, and makes music its focus — not only are there record players in every room, there’s a selection of (really quite good) guitars and other stringed instruments for lending. Rooms and suites are contemporary in concept and comforts, though influenced by the city’s 19th-century heritage; restaurants include an American brasserie, an indoor rooftop lounge, and Magic Rat, an unpretentiously stylish live music venue.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bowie House, Auberge Collection in Fort Worth
ld.description: It just might be the most stylish building in Fort Worth, Texas; it’s surely the city’s most extraordinary luxury hotel. Bowie House, Auberge Collection is indeed a member of the same hotel group responsible for some of California’s most desirable stays, and while it’s consistent with the brand’s high standards for design and comfort, you certainly can’t say it hasn’t been painstakingly localized, from cowhide armchairs in the lobby to the local artworks and upscale Texan cuisine. The rooms and suites are spectacular, as is the pool terrace, and the rest of Bowie House’s common spaces are as inviting as they are impressive.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Drover, Autograph Collection in Fort Worth
ld.description: In most cases we take care to tell you how modern this city is, but Fort Worth’s historic Stockyards district is a well-preserved monument to the cattle-driving industry, and the inspiration for Hotel Drover, a hotel that seeks a balance between Old West character and contemporary boutique-hotel style. It’s surprisingly successful — unmistakably Texan but without crossing too far into kitsch, and sophisticated enough to balance out the broad rustic gestures. There’s a backyard featuring a swimming pool, a hot tub, and plenty of lounge space and outdoor games; restaurants include the upscale 97 West.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Quercus in Gay
ld.description: Quercus takes its name from the oak, fitting for a retreat set on 3,800 acres of forest, pasture, and river in rural Georgia. What started as a return to regenerative farming soon evolved into a project that unites land, food, and hospitality. The result is four cottage-style suites furnished with botanical tones and heirlooms from the Visconti collection, while wide porches and fireplaces turn the outdoors into living space. Dining, guided by a biodynamic garden, shapes every stay: from picnic-style lunches to refined dinners, the experience is inseparable from the land that sustains it.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Reynolds, Lake Oconee in Greensboro
ld.description: A little over an hour to the east of Atlanta, the Ritz-Carlton Reynolds, Lake Oconee is hidden away on its own little peninsula, surrounded by miles and miles of winding lakeshore. Aesthetically, it’s something unusual for the brand, in a throwback Craftsman style that’s perfectly suited to its environment. The rooms and suites are joined by lakeside cottages for larger traveling parties, and all the Ritz-Carlton signatures are here, from the expansive spa to the multiple upscale dining and drinking venues; guests also have access to a nearby tennis club and no fewer than five championship golf courses.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Muir, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Halifax

ld.name: Muir, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Halifax in Halifax
ld.description: The Queen’s Marque district, where the city center meets the waterfront, is the center of Halifax’s recent revitalization, and it’s where you’ll find Muir, the first hotel of its kind in this maritime city: a proper luxury hotel with boutique good looks and a wealth of details that are tailored to the locale. The rooms and suites are handsome and understated, their seafaring vibe never crossing over into kitsch; local crafts and artworks keep them firmly rooted in their place. An expansive spa and wellness center, a highly regarded restaurant, a stylish bar, and a serious art gallery cement Muir’s status as a local landmark.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Dallas, Las Colinas in Irving
ld.description: Spread across a former cattle ranch in the Las Colinas hills, just minutes from DFW Airport, The Ritz-Carlton Dallas, Las Colinas forgoes the urban tower format for a low-rise resort with genuine space between buildings. The 427 rooms, suites, and villas take their palette from the surrounding landscape: tan leather, dark walnut, and blue accents that echo the TPC Las Colinas fairways visible from most balconies. Five dining options, a 14,000-square-foot spa, championship tennis and pickleball courts, aerial yoga, and three pools give it the density of programming that justifies a proper stay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fogo Island Inn in Joe Batt's Arm
ld.description: Perhaps the only thing stopping the Fogo Island Inn from becoming the most famous high-design luxury hotel in the world is its out-of-the-way location, on a tiny and sparsely populated island off the coast of Newfoundland. Of course, this air of remoteness is key to its appeal, along with its design, an ultra-modern reinterpretation of traditional, utilitarian Maritimes architecture. Here you’ll find 29 luxe rooms with spectacular views, an impressive high-end locavore restaurant, and excursions that range from whale-watching to iceberg tours and beyond. It’s a voyage that’s well worth the effort, and it’s closer than it may seem to the East Coasts of the US and Canada.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: The Dunlin, Auberge Collection in Johns Island
ld.description: The Dunlin, Auberge Collection, offers a laid-back take on Southern luxury, set along the Kiawah River on Johns Island. Its 72 rooms and suites, along with 19 villas, reflect classic Sea Island design: gabled roofs, screened porches, and long marsh views. Days unfold over oyster-laced shorelines, dolphin sightings, and slow hikes through 2,000 acres of biodiverse Lowcountry terrain. Charleston is a 40-minute drive, but the real draw is right outside: river paths, open sky, and the natural pace of the Lowcountry.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: White Barn Inn, Auberge Collection in Kennebunk
ld.description: White Barn Inn is one of America's finest country house hotels, a rustic and intimate inn (and now, a cottage compound) down by the waterfront in the Atlantic coast town of Kennebunkport, Maine. This is a town perhaps best known outside of the Northeast as a presidential summer home, but long before the elder Bush first arrived, it was a popular hideout for the Yankee aristocracy.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets: Pets are not permitted in the Main Inn unless registered as service animals. Dogs are not permitted on houseboats unless registered as service animals.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Belden House & Mews in Litchfield
ld.description: Belden House & Mews brings full-scale hospitality back to Litchfield’s center, more than a century after the town’s original grand hotel was lost to fire. Built in 1888 by Dr. Charles O. Belden, the main house has been redesigned by Champalimaud Design, with Victorian staircases, original fireplaces, and subtle updates that preserve the building’s character. Behind it, a 1959 mews holds 31 light-filled rooms with custom furniture and and garden access. The village green is just around the corner, but the atmosphere here feels worlds apart.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: One&Only Mandarina in Lo de Marcos
ld.description: An hour or so up the coast from crowded Puerto Vallarta, the spectacular One&Only Mandarina combines eco-lodge sensitivity, boutique-hotel good looks, and luxury-hotel comforts and facilities, all in a tranquil setting amid 80 acres of coastal rainforest. The treehouses and villas are stunning, inside and out, and come with every conceivable luxury, from plunge pools to butler service. The three restaurants draw on some high-caliber culinary talent, and the diversions include anything from humble nature walks to various seafaring and whale-watching adventures and the genteel pursuits on offer at the Mandarina Polo & Equestrian Club.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed (Pet fees may apply).

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Dove Mountain in Marana
ld.description: A short drive from Tucson sits a luxury retreat that’ll have you channeling your inner Wyatt Earp. The generously proportioned suites and bedrooms blend seamlessly into the foothills of the Tortolita Mountains in the Sonoran Desert and provide views that’ll be hard to forget. The Jack Nicklaus-designed golf course will keep you busy during the day, while the impressive selection of restaurants and bars means you’ll never have to leave the resort at night.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Atticus Hotel in McMinnville
ld.description: Roughly halfway between Portland and the coast is McMinnville, Oregon, a small city with a touch of Old West atmosphere owing to its Oregon Trail roots. The Atticus Hotel is one part country charm, one part urban sophistication, a contemporary boutique-style hotel in a town where you wouldn’t necessarily expect such a thing. Rooms range from crash-pad-sized Micro Studios to a proper penthouse suite, and Cypress at the Atticus, the restaurant, draws on Mediterranean and Northwestern flavors. This town is plenty walkable, and to expand your range the Atticus keeps a fleet of stylish cruiser bikes on hand.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Salamander Middleburg in Middleburg
ld.description: You don’t have to go very far beyond the upscale western suburbs of Washington, D.C. to find yourself in some of Virginia’s most scenic countryside; here, on a 340-acre estate in the Blue Ridge foothills, is the spectacular Salamander Middleburg. One of too few Black-owned hotels, it’s the work of Sheila C. Johnson, the co-founder of the B.E.T. television network, and an accomplished hotelier, on the evidence provided here. It’s a full-spectrum luxury resort with an emphasis on equestrian sports — the stables and horse trails are as much an attraction as the vast spa and the multitude of restaurants.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Albatross in Ocean Grove
ld.description: One town south of Asbury Park on the famous Jersey Shore is Ocean Grove, a remarkably dense little Victorian village that’s set apart from its neighbors not only by its historic architecture but by its status as a dry town, with alcohol sales prohibited within its limits. It turns out this constraint is just the thing to nudge the local hospitality scene towards something a little more grown up; the result is the stylish and unusually refined Hotel Albatross.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pendry Natirar in Peapack
ld.description: An hour from Manhattan, Pendry Natirar reimagines a 500-acre Somerset County estate once owned by Moroccan royalty. At its core is a 1912 Tudor-style mansion, now joined by sleek guest wings, a spa, tennis courts, and an organic farm that supplies the property’s restaurants, including the acclaimed Ninety Acres. Rooms mix classic materials with contemporary finishes: think dark wood, marble, brass, and deep-green accents. With a cooking school, private club, and panoramic views, it is a rare mix of scale, setting, and substance in the Northeast.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Merrill House in Picton
ld.description: The lovely little town of Picton, in Ontario’s Prince Edward County, is maybe the most likely setting in all of Canada for a hotel like Merrill House. This red brick Gothic Revival mansion stands just off Main Street, a block from Picton Harbour, but feels quiet and quasi-rural all the same. And the style is unforgettable. Both inside and out, Merrill House is anglophilic even by Canadian standards — its owners live part-time in London, and the house’s décor wouldn’t look a whisker out of place there.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Royal Hotel in Picton
ld.description: 150 years ago Picton, Ontario was important enough to merit a rather grand railroad hotel, but prior to its recent redevelopment, the splendid red-brick Royal Hotel was on the way to demolition. Now, with wine-country tourism on a major upswing, there is again a need for a stylish and luxurious lodging on the Royal’s level. Today it mixes heritage glamour with contemporary cool, filling the rooms with high-end modern comforts and adding enticements like a spa, a sauna, and a seasonal outdoor pool. Farm-to-table cooking is a major point of emphasis, as are Prince Edward County’s local wines.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed for an additional fee and must not be left alone at any time.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Fearrington House Inn in Pittsboro
ld.description: Midway between Washington, D.C. and Charleston, The Fearrington House Inn transforms a onetime dairy farm into a beautiful property with a distinctly Southern cadence. Pastures are still home to the rare Belted Galloway cows, while the surrounding village hums with gardens, boutiques, and seasonal gatherings. Built in the 1980s, the inn retains an intimate scale: individually designed rooms, fresh flowers from the grounds, and a restaurant that fuses European traditions with local flavors. It balances the character of the Carolina countryside with the standards of a European grande dame.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Sea Ranch Lodge in Sea Ranch
ld.description: The Sea Ranch has long been one of coastal California’s most unusual places — a planned community, established in the 1960s, where a number of prominent midcentury architects built a variety of low-profile, low-impact timber-frame houses. It’s here, in a weathered redwood building that’s still home to the community’s general store and post office, that you’ll find The Sea Ranch Lodge, a 17-room hotel that combines modern Californian luxury with the utopian spirit of the project’s original founding. Alongside its impressive accommodations, guests enjoy the presence of an excellent restaurant and bar, as well as access to mile after mile of sublimely rocky coastline.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Edgewood Tahoe in Stateline
ld.description: We aren’t here to cast aspersions on the rest of the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe, but we think it’s absolutely safe to say there’s never been anything here quite like the Edgewood Tahoe. In a hotel scene that’s rife with refurbishments and repurposings, it’s that rare sight: a brand-new, purpose-built, LEED Silver–certified luxury lodge. And to its front-row view of the lake it adds a golf course by George Fazio and a shuttle service to Heavenly Mountain, one of the region’s best-loved ski areas.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel 1928 in Waco
ld.description: Hotel 1928 occupies the former Grand Karem Shrine Temple, a 1928 Moorish Revival landmark reimagined with Art Deco flair and Southern warmth. Original details remain: painted beams, arched windows, hardwood floors, layered now with plush lounges, patterned textiles, and the sparkle of chandeliers in the grand ballroom. The 33 rooms are intimate yet stylish, while public spaces include a café, two restaurants, a library, and tucked-away sitting rooms. Ten minutes from the Silos, the hotel is both a tribute to Waco’s past and a gathering place for its present.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Quoin in Wilmington
ld.description: Wilmington, Delaware flies under the radar for a number of reasons, but boutique-hotel aficionados have at least one reason to keep it on the list: the Quoin, a Romanesque bank building in the historic downtown center, now renovated by the Philadelphia-based Method Co. and Stokes Architecture + Design into a warm, livable, and richly detailed boutique hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sage Lodge in Yellowstone National Park
ld.description: There’s much more to Yellowstone than Old Faithful, and though most of the park lies within Wyoming, the neighboring portion of Montana is no less impressive. It’s here, by the park’s northern entrance, that you’ll find Sage Lodge, along the banks of the Yellowstone River in the aptly named Paradise Valley. The style is modern-rustic and the comforts are as plush as the landscape is rugged; there’s no end of opportunity for outdoor adventure, plus a luxe spa and a pair of restaurants serving menus centered around meats and produce sourced from local ranches and farms.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

address.streetAddress: Blvd. Cabo Marqués, Lote 1, Col. Punta Diamente

ld.name: Banyan Tree Cabo Marqués in Acapulco
ld.description: Banyan Tree specializes in bringing a polished sheen to beachfront eco-resorts with a practiced ease that always feels individually tailored. The private pool-villa concept works tremendously well in a place like Acapulco, where it serves as a welcome alternative to the faded glitz of the high-rises looming over the bay. Masterfully secluded at the tip of Punta Diamante, Banyan Tree Cabo Marques ensures that its guests’ experience with those mega-hotels begins and ends with a view of their twinkling lights across the water.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Adelphi Hotel in Adirondack Mountains
ld.description: Saratoga Springs, like many mid-century resort towns, is having a renaissance, which is the perfect occasion for the Adelphi’s second act. This classic Victorian hotel, right on Broadway in the heart of town, has been renovated from head to toe, resulting in a contemporary boutique hotel that’s worthy of its glamorous façade. The oversized rooms back up their classic good looks with luxe touches like ultra-modern bathrooms with radiant-heated floors. This stretch of Broadway is lively at night, but the Adelphi gives you reasons to stay in: there’s a cocktail bar called Morrissey’s as well as two restaurants, the Blue Hen and Salt & Char.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Mirror Lake Inn Resort and Spa

ld.name: The Mirror Lake Inn Resort and Spa in Adirondack Mountains
ld.description: As travelers once again return to destinations closer to home, places like Lake Placid, in New York’s Adirondack Mountains, are more relevant than they’ve been in decades. Of course Mirror Lake Inn Resort and Spa has been here the whole time, family-owned for 85 years. And while its atmosphere remains delightfully timeless, its comforts have been subtly upgraded — gas fireplaces replace wood, for example, and the spa includes a salt-therapy room and a 60-foot indoor pool. The View is the higher-end of the two restaurants, while the Cottage does a fine après-ski — this one-time Winter Olympics site excels at snow sports, but the Adirondacks are magical year-round.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Whiteface Lodge in Adirondack Mountains
ld.description: These days Lake Placid is perhaps better known as a Winter Olympics venue (and as the site of a certain Cold War–era hockey game) than as a holiday destination. Which is unfortunate — the same sublime geography that makes it so well-suited to winter sports means it’s none too shabby in the summer either. Not to mention that they’ve got a certain body of water there that’s, well, none too rough apparently. And now they’ve got the Whiteface Lodge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Los Poblanos Historic Inn & Organic Farm

ld.name: Los Poblanos Historic Inn & Organic Farm in Albuquerque
ld.description: Organic shampoo, hand-milled honey soap, complimentary earplugs. Wait, what? Don’t worry, it’s not the pulsing beats of a nightclub below that might interrupt your sleep — it’s the peacocks. The fabulously decorative birds, infamous for their early morning call, are just some of the exotic creatures that wander the grounds of Los Poblanos Historic Inn & Organic Farm.
ld.petsAllowed: Los Poblanos is a working farm with live animals and a certified wildlife habitat. We have a firm no-pets policy and adhere strictly to ADA guidelines regarding service animals. Service dogs in training and Emotional Support animals are not protected under the ADA Laws and are not considered service animals. We will gladly recommend boarding arrangements with a nearby kennel.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Asbury Ocean Club Hotel in Asbury Park
ld.description: As short-haul travel once again becomes the norm, places close to New York City are experiencing a renaissance — among them Asbury Park, New Jersey, a beach town that’s right in the heart of the Jersey Shore. A hotel like the Asbury Ocean Club would have been unthinkable a decade or two earlier, but today it’s a breath of fresh air, a light and stylish luxury hotel that’s set right on Ocean Avenue, steps from the boardwalk and the beach.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Blind Tiger Asheville in Asheville
ld.description: Whether it’s a hidden gem or simply a gem is up for debate, but Asheville, North Carolina is one of the most pleasant destinations in the American South — known for its modest size, its artistic and creative culture, and its spectacular natural surroundings. The same things that attract travelers presumably attracted Lark Hotels, the Northeastern boutique-hotel group behind the Blind Tiger guest houses. And Blind Tiger Asheville is true to form: a beautifully restored 19th-century Queen Anne–style house in Chestnut Hill, a few blocks to the north of downtown, transformed into a stylish 14-room guest house that makes a point of blending in to the local community.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Jerome, Auberge Collection in Aspen
ld.description: It’s been a long journey for Aspen, from rough-and-tumble Old West outpost to upscale ski resort and playground to the stars. It was arguably the Hotel Jerome itself that kick-started that long upward ride during the silver boom of the late 1800s, when Macy’s co-owner Jerome Wheeler started investing in the town’s properties — starting with what would quickly become the most luxurious hotel in town.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mollie Aspen in Aspen
ld.description: There’s no rule that says a modern Colorado ski hotel has to look like a national park lodge or an Alpine chalet. And in these days of “quiet luxury,” there’s nothing more quietly luxurious than the sort of Bauhaus-meets-Japanese-Scandinavian modernism on display here. The Mollie Aspen stands just off Main Street, a quick shuttle ride from Aspen Mountain’s lifts. But in its style and atmosphere it’s a world apart from even the most fashionable ski hotels, none of which can match it in terms of architecture and design — much less a hip bar and restaurant, the latter featuring a variety of vegan options.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Little Nell in Aspen
ld.description: The Little Nell’s unassuming name can’t hide the fact that it might just be the finest ski hotel in the United States. Even in Aspen, a city that’s no stranger to slopeside luxury, this is, for many of its guests, the only game in town. It helps that its location, at the foot of the Silver Queen Gondola, is the very definition of ski-in/ski-out. And while it’s been an A-list favorite for more than a generation, it’s never content to rest on its laurels — the most recent renovation, by the New York studio Champalimaud Design, leaves it looking like the very picture of modern mountain luxury.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: FORTH Hotel Atlanta in Atlanta
ld.description: Atlanta’s historic Old Fourth Ward is more of a culinary hotspot than a place to stay the night; most of the city’s luxury hotels are located in Downtown or Midtown. A notable exception, the hip Forth Hotel, is a creation of the same team that converted the nearby Ponce City Market from an old Sears building into a vibrant food hall.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Clermont  in Atlanta
ld.description: Not all that long ago, Atlanta’s Clermont Hotel was famous for two things: the landmark sign on its rooftop radio tower, and the Clermont Lounge, a legendary slice of nightlife in the basement. Both of those features still exist, but what’s in between them — a 1920s red-brick edifice that’s seen good times and bad — has been thoroughly renovated, and reinvented as a 94-room boutique hotel, complete with a hip restaurant by a celebrated local chef and a couple of in-demand nightspots (that’s in addition to the basement’s attractions).
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are welcome with a $75 per pet per stay fee, max 2 pets. Cats are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Nobu Hotel Atlanta in Atlanta
ld.description: The upscale Atlanta district of Buckhead has long been a hotbed of hotel luxury, but Nobu Hotel Atlanta expands the scene in a new direction. What originally seemed like a one-off — an unlikely collaboration between the restaurateur Nobu Matsuhisa and the actor Robert De Niro — is now a global luxury-boutique phenomenon, whose signature cocktail of sharp, modernist-inspired design and Japanese-Peruvian cuisine is a welcome addition to the unofficial capital of the American South.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Stonehurst Place Atlanta in Atlanta
ld.description: We’ve nothing against bed and breakfasts per se; they’re not simply small hotels, but something else entirely. Occasionally, though, we come across one that’s extraordinary enough that we’re forced to take notice, and this is one of those times. Atlanta in general does oversized nouveau riche as well as anyone, but Stonehurst Place is proof that they’ve still got a flair for the classic as well.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Atlanta in Atlanta
ld.description: Ritz-Carlton and Downtown Atlanta were made for each other — it’s hard to think of another American city where the brand’s classic elegance is so well appreciated. And there’s nothing particularly sedate about it — there’s contemporary art, live music, and an outpost of the beloved Athens-based Jittery Joe’s coffee shop. The rooms and suites are lavish and subtly high-tech, with classic comforts like marble bathrooms, rain showers, and Nespresso machines. The fitness center is particularly well-equipped, with Peloton bikes and personalized programs, and the high-end modern steakhouse and opulent cocktail bar are local favorites.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The St. Regis Atlanta in Atlanta
ld.description: Positioned directly across from Buckhead Village's luxury retail corridor, the St. Regis Atlanta is all hardwood floors, twin curved staircases, and chandelier-lit rooms that feel more private club than hotel. Macassar ebony beds, white marble bathrooms, and Juliette balconies run throughout; the Empire Suite stretches to 3,000 square feet with its own kitchen, media room, and Peloton gym. Atlas, the Michelin-starred restaurant, displays original Picassos and Van Goghs from owner Joe Lewis' personal collection. The nightly champagne sabrage in the Grand Hallway, a Napoleonic ritual the hotel takes seriously, is worth being back for at six.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: ARRIVE Austin in Austin
ld.description: Austin, Texas has changed an awful lot in recent years, as the Texan capital has also become a tech capital, and ARRIVE Austin stands as a perfect emblem of that evolution. The east side of town has long been the city’s less polished, more creative side, and it still is — though it’d be a stretch to call this brand-new contemporary structure unpolished, its industrial-inspired interiors and its sociable, communal atmosphere remain true to the spirit of the neighborhood.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Austin Proper Hotel in Austin
ld.description: There’s no sense in denying that Austin has changed a lot in recent years, and while the advent of the Austin Proper Hotel will likely be an occasion for some grumbling about Californian imports, it’s a fine example of a city embracing change with open arms. While many Austin boutique hotels emphasize their down-home roots, the Proper Hotel is unapologetically urban, and architecturally, it’s as contemporary as they come. The design is by the same Kelly Wearstler who’s responsible for the mini-chain’s California installments, and the vibe, for all its style, isn’t shy about tending a bit upscale.
ld.petsAllowed: Dogs are allowed for a fee of USD 100 per stay, per pet. Up to 2 dogs (sorry no cats) are allowed, not to exceed 35 lbs. per pet.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Commodore Perry Estate, Auberge Collection in Austin
ld.description: California’s Auberge Collection, now a global family, are known for their tasteful luxury and for their variety — and the Commodore Perry Estate, set on ten acres of land in urban Austin, Texas, is unique by any standard. It’s a Twenties mansion and satellite buildings in Italianate and Spanish Revival styles, and it’s all been brought entirely up to date by the expert hospitality designer Ken Fulk. The result sacrifices none of the estate’s throwback atmosphere, but brings it up to a 21st-century standard; like everything Auberge touches, it’s the very picture of modern boutique luxury.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Fairmont Austin Gold Experience in Austin
ld.description: As you may gather from the unorthodox name, the Fairmont Austin Gold Experience isn’t an ordinary hotel, but rather a hotel within a hotel — four private floors within the relatively staid Fairmont Austin, within which is offered an experience that’s a cut above the already luxe Fairmont norm. It’s got its own reception desk, its own private lounge, and access to all the rest of the hotel’s facilities and services, including the pan-global Revue, the wood-fired Garrison, and the Latin-flavored Rules & Regs — and the downtown setting places most of what’s special about Austin within easy enough reach.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Austin in Austin
ld.description: Though it’s been open since the 1980s, the Four Seasons Hotel Austin is arguably more relevant than it’s ever been. Austin is, after all, the state capital — but it’s also the tech capital of Texas, and these days the Four Seasons is as likely to host investors and entrepreneurs as it is government officials. And it certainly doesn’t hurt that, like so many of the brand’s hotels, this Four Seasons has seen an update that leaves it looking more stylish than most luxury hotels of its stature.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Saint Cecilia in Austin
ld.description: For a while now Austin has been one of the United States’ best-kept secrets: a little enclave of progressive thought, high-tech savvy, and hipster culture, cleverly hidden in Texas, which is not the first place you’d look — and it’s disguised as the state capital, no less. But until recently its hotel situation lagged a bit behind the times — one new and notable exception being the Hotel Saint Cecilia.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel ZaZa Austin in Austin
ld.description: Austin, now that it’s booming, is home to a hotel from just about every boutique and luxury chain under the sun. But the Texas-based ZaZa group took its time. Long a familiar name in Dallas and Houston, ZaZa hits the state’s capital city at a moment when it takes more than just a quirky design sense to stand out. Fortunately for everyone involved, Hotel ZaZa Austin is very much up to the task.
ld.petsAllowed: Hotel ZaZa is a pet-friendly facility. A one-time, non-refundable deposit of $150 per pet is required at check-in.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Soho House Austin in Austin
ld.description: The original Soho House was set in the London neighborhood of the same name, a place that’s no stranger to members’ clubs with a hospitality element and a creative-class focus. Since then they’ve expanded to settings as far-flung as Mumbai and Mykonos — and for their first location in the southern United States they chose Austin, Texas, a picture-perfect example of a city whose recent boom is largely fueled by the blossoming of its local creative industries.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Frances Modern Inn in Austin
ld.description: Named after the founder's grandmother, Frances Faust, whose instinct for hospitality became the guiding principle behind the whole operation, this Central East Austin property is in a neighborhood where small businesses have held ground since the 1900s. The smallest rooms are cozy singles with reading nooks and East Austin views; the largest stretch to two-story loft suites with clawfoot tubs and half-kitchens. Siti, the in-house restaurant recognized in the 2025 Michelin Guide, builds its menu around the culinary traditions of Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and the Philippines, an unexpectedly specific kitchen for a boutique inn.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Heywood Hotel in Austin
ld.description: If a hotelier is going to be a little obsessive about keeping things local, it helps to be in a town with as much creative talent as Austin. The Heywood Hotel is certainly handsome enough, with its mid-century Danish armchairs and its warmly lit polished-concrete courtyard. But behind its stylish good looks is a whole village of dynamic, creative locals, from the hotel’s architects and designers to the management and guest services staff to the artists whose works hang on the walls. (The majority of whom, not incidentally, are women, from the ownership on down to the proprietors of the various businesses that supply the hotel.)

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Boca de Agua Bacalar in Bacalar
ld.description: There’s visiting the Yucatán, and then there’s fully immersing yourself in it. Boca de Agua Bacalar offers an experience that falls firmly in the latter camp, plopping you right on the banks of the Bacalar lagoon and its outrageously clear turquoise waters. Rooms come treehouse style, lifted on stilts to minimize their footprint while also affording sweeping vistas of the jungle — and, if you’re lucky, a spider monkey or an iguana. It’s a winning recipe: a tranquil hideaway, central to a rich selection of nature excursions, neighbors with Mayan ruins, all mercifully free of the spring-break set. Your hardest choice will be: swim some more or snooze in the hammock?

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Av. 3 Corner Calle 32, Col. Mario Villanueva

ld.name: Casa Hormiga in Bacalar
ld.description: The so-called Riviera Maya may grab the headlines, but it’s worth venturing a little farther, to the southern reaches of the Yucatán Peninsula, for a truly transformative experience. Here, close to the border with Belize, is the town of Bacalar, along the shores of the impossibly clear blue lake of the same name; and it’s in this town that you’ll find the beautifully tranquil Casa Hormiga Hotel & Rituales.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Our Habitas Bacalar in Bacalar
ld.description: The Yucatán is prized by travelers for its engagement with nature, but even here there are degrees; just a few miles from the border with Belize, Bacalar is so wild as to make Tulum look like Los Angeles by comparison. The spectacularly colorful lagoon is the main natural attraction, and as luxurious as Habitas Bacalar may be, its tented A-frames are extraordinarily environmentally friendly, built using traditional low-impact methods, on raised platforms to protect the local flora and fauna.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Le Germain Charlevoix Hotel & Spa in Baie-St-Paul
ld.description: Though Le Germain Charlevoix Hotel & Spa is set on a working farm and runs its own farmers’ market during the summer months, the hotel itself is as modern as they come, proof that today’s travelers don’t see any contradiction between comfort and contemporary design. Much more than an updated farmhouse, it’s essentially a small village, its 145 rooms spread between five farm-inspired modern buildings. It’s forward-thinking enough to have its own train station, so you can walk on in Quebec City and walk off right at the hotel, no car required.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pendry Baltimore in Baltimore
ld.description: A bit of poolside lounging might not be the first thing that comes to mind when you imagine a Baltimore boutique hotel, but the Pendry Baltimore is anything but typical. The harborside neighborhood of Fell’s Point isn’t just the city’s liveliest corner, with the highest concentration of restaurants and bars, it’s also home to the historic Recreation Pier — on which, above the waters of the harbor, stands the Pendry, a renovation of a grand century-old building (whose façade might be familiar from Baltimore’s own Homicide television series).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ivy Hotel in Baltimore
ld.description: Although distinctly Baltimorean in its red-brick beauty, the Ivy Hotel serves up a brand of luxury hospitality that’ll be familiar to travelers the world over. This restored 19th-century mansion is set in Mount Vernon, just to the north of the Inner Harbor, and is one of just a few Black-owned boutique hotels in America. Its rooms are outfitted with lush fabrics, four-poster beds, and gas fireplaces, and its bathrooms feature heated limestone floors and, in some cases, soaking tubs. There’s a small-but-lovely spa, a verdant courtyard for breakfast, afternoon tea, or drinks, and a highly regarded local restaurant, Magdalena, helmed by chef Ülfet Ralph.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Fairmont Banff Springs in Banff
ld.description: Canada’s grand railway hotels now fly the Fairmont flag, and while all of them are unusually historic and luxurious, there’s no other quite like the Fairmont Banff Springs. The “Castle in the Rockies” is set right in the heart of Banff National Park, and its vast structure contains 724 rooms and suites, all updated in a subdued contemporary style that aims to complement, rather than distract from, the views of the park outside. And on top of the spa, the handful of restaurants, and the year-round roster of activities, there’s the truly spectacular Fairmont Banff Springs Golf Course.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Twin Farms in Barnard
ld.description: Surrounded by 300 acres of farmland and wilderness, Twin Farms might be as secluded as you can get without leaving the Northeast. It also might be the region’s most luxurious resort. In some places that might mean a modern hotel complex, but in Vermont it means a few rooms in Sinclair Lewis’s old farmhouse, surrounded by a handful of cottages, all with interiors by the 20th-century eclectic traditionalist Jed Johnson (and, as of late, five more cottages sporting a more contemporary look by Thad Hayes).

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Goodwin in Beloit
ld.description: We said we wouldn’t rest until there was a proper independent boutique hotel in every city in America. And while we’re not there just yet, the addition of Beloit, Wisconsin is definitely the right kind of progress. Hotel Goodwin may take its inspiration — and its name — from a 19th-century Beloit landmark, but in its current incarnation it’s every bit a 21st-century boutique hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Canyon Ranch Lenox in Berkshires
ld.description: The sequel to the original Tucson, Arizona installment, Canyon Ranch Lenox necessarily differs when it comes to local details. The setting, obviously, is not the Sonoran desert but the Berkshires of western Massachusetts; guests arrive to an opulent 19th-century mansion, formerly a Jesuit seminary. And the clientele, though global, is more likely to hail from New York and Boston than Los Angeles and Phoenix.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Granville House in Berkshires
ld.description: The picturesque Western Massachusetts town of Great Barrington, a few miles to the south of Lenox, is home to Granville House, a bed and breakfast owned and operated by a couple of veterans of the New York restaurant scene, and named for George Bailey’s house in Frank Capra’s “It’s a Wonderful Life.” The five rooms retain plenty of historical charm, though they’ve been updated with some modernist furniture and an eclectic collection of artworks and antiques. Beyond breakfast, there’s a sitting room and a music room, as well as a billiards parlor; for lunch and dinner you’ll want to explore Great Barrington and the surrounding Berkshires towns.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Tourists in Berkshires
ld.description: In far northwestern Massachusetts, roughly equidistant from Boston and New York, the Berkshires are undergoing the sort of revival that travel trend pieces are made of. Thanks in part to the redevelopment that’s accompanied MASS MoCA, the contemporary art museum, the formerly industrial town of North Adams is living a second life as a booming cultural destination. Outside the town center, on the road to neighborhing Williamstown, you’ll find another piece of reclaimed Berkshires heritage: TOURISTS, a Sixties motor lodge reborn as a very modern, very hip little country boutique hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: \n PET tourists also welcome at 45 USD per night - with a limit of 2 dogs per room.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Montage Big Sky in Big Sky
ld.description: Montage Big Sky is another hotel where the constituent parts of the name tell more or less the whole story — the Californian purveyor of lavish high-design resort experiences meets the rugged Rocky Mountain wilderness of southwestern Montana. This isn’t Jackson Hole or Aspen; until now, Big Sky hasn’t seen high-end hospitality on Montage’s level. And, likewise, it’s a long way from Laguna Beach; the untamed wilderness is close at hand, as is some of North America’s finest skiing.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: One&Only Moonlight Basin in Big Sky
ld.description: Compared to names like Aspen or Jackson Hole, Big Sky, Montana is perhaps a more rugged and down-to-earth destination than you might expect for the One&Only group’s first mountain resort. One&Only Moonlight Basin features serious modern-luxe architecture by the Northwest’s own Olson Kundig, and while its situation is more secluded than the typical slopeside ski hotel, it’s directly connected to Big Sky Mountain’s lift system via a private gondola. And while winter is its most dramatic season, it’s a credible year-round escape, with an expansive spa and wellness program and access to no end of outdoor recreation.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Alila Ventana Big Sur in Big Sur
ld.description: Big Sur is the jewel of the California coast, one of the most spectacular places in North America, and Alila Ventana Big Sur is Big Sur’s original luxury resort, founded by writer Lawrence A. Spector, using profits from the film Easy Rider. Clearly it doesn’t get much more California than that.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Post Ranch Inn in Big Sur
ld.description: Post Ranch Inn is blessed with one of the most extraordinary locations on the face of the earth, a place of such breathtaking beauty it’s hard to believe it’s even accessible by mere automobile-driving mortals. Big Sur is the most scenic destination along California’s most scenic drive, Highway 1, which links Los Angeles with San Francisco and features such curiosities as Hearst Castle and Steinbeck’s Monterey along the way.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Montage Palmetto Bluff in Bluffton
ld.description: The Inn at Palmetto Bluff may be the first East Coast hotel from the California-based Montage Resorts, but it would take a keen eye indeed to notice much Laguna Beach influence here — this place, though brand new, is absolutely authentic, its fifty clapboard cottages built in the local Low Country style of the South Carolina coast. This is the old South, make no mistake: you're midway between Hilton Head and Savannah, Georgia, and that famed Southern hospitality is on display from the moment you check in.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Boston in Boston
ld.description: Four Seasons Hotel Boston was built in the Eighties, though to its credit it feels considerably older — and the views over the Public Garden lend it a certain timelessness. At the same time, a thorough recent renovation has left the interiors looking as sharp as ever, with a refreshing absence of old New England stylistic clichés. The rooms and suites are classic in style and they’re pleasing to all senses: the Four Seasons signature bed is phenomenally comfortable, and the marble-clad bathroom is practically a private spa.
ld.petsAllowed: \n The hotel is prepared to accommodate your cat or dog, with the understanding that your pet is less than 25 pounds (11.5 kgs), fully trained, vaccinated, always appropriately restrained and compliant with local legislation requirements.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Hotel One Dalton Street, Boston

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel One Dalton Street, Boston in Boston
ld.description: Boston’s second Four Seasons hotel is unusual both for the town and the brand: set in a Henry Cobb skyscraper that was completed in 2019, the Four Seasons One Dalton Street is contemporary to the core. In classic Four Seasons style, however, it’s still eminently palatable — there’s nothing here that would alienate a traditionalist, aside from the unusual bird’s-eye-view of this generally low-rise city. Every luxury is accounted for, including a spa and a spectacular indoor pool, and dining options include Zuma, the globally renowned izakaya-style Japanese restaurant, and LPM, a newly opened venue inspired by French cuisine.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pet must weigh no more than 25 lbs and must not be left unattended. Pets are not allowed in any food and beverage outlets and wellness floor. Guests are responsible for cleaning up after their pet on hotel property and in the neighborhood. Any disturbances such as barking must be curtailed to ensure other guests are not inconvenienced. A charge may be applied to guests bill in the event of a disturbance to other guests. Guests are responsible for all property damages and/or personal injuries resulting from their pet.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Raffles Boston in Boston
ld.description: Raffles may be based in Singapore, but there’s arguably no city better suited than Boston to the task of hosting the brand’s first American hotel. Raffles is all about classic elegance, after all, and so is Boston’s Back Bay. And while both are occasionally overshadowed by bolder and brasher competitors, there’s a quiet stylishness about them that goes deeper than trends.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Langham Boston in Boston
ld.description: It takes something special to make a historic impression in Boston, a serious contender for America’s most founder-centric metropolis. Fitting, then, that Langham should make an entrance here via the 1922 Federal Reserve Bank. They’ve shrewdly retained the stolid grandeur of its exteriors for effect while dramatically transforming the interiors to present-day standards of luxury. Here, if nowhere else, the Brits maintain an elegant foothold in the Financial District, tempering the neighborhood’s elite pedigree with age-softened British elegance.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Newbury Boston in Boston
ld.description: After nearly a century in service, and after a thorough renovation, including guest rooms by the celebrated designer Alexandra Champalimaud — this Back Bay icon is back in business under its own name: the Newbury Boston. This is top-tier luxury by any name, made more desirable by its inimitable location, its impressive art collection, and its close-up views of the Boston Public Garden.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Whitney Hotel Boston in Boston
ld.description: A brand-new hotel in Beacon Hill sounds almost like a contradiction in terms — this is the old side of Boston, where buildings’ ages are measured out in centuries. But at the foot of the Longfellow Bridge, a brand-new luxury boutique hotel is exactly what you’ll find. The Whitney Hotel fits perfectly into its red-brick surroundings, and inside you’ll find interiors that perfectly thread a stylistic needle — classic enough for the bluest blueblood, and contemporary enough to clearly declare its modern boutique bona fides.
ld.petsAllowed: \n The Whitney Hotel welcomes two pets for an additional fee of $125.00 per stay per guest room. Each pet should weigh 50 lb. or less. Pets cannot be left unattended at any time.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: XV Beacon in Boston
ld.description: The name is the address: 15 Beacon Street, a block from Boston Common, at one end of the city’s posh Beacon Hill neighborhood. What’s behind the cast-iron façade of this turn-of-the-century Beaux Arts building could easily have been a perfectly uptight, perfectly conventional New England luxury hotel — instead it’s possessed of a certain dark elegance, and an atmosphere that’s both romantic and a little bit Romantic.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge in Brooklyn
ld.description: The Manhattan iteration of the 1 Hotels brand may have come first, but that doesn’t mean the Brooklyn edition is an afterthought. 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge stands at the edge of Brooklyn Bridge Park, looking across the East River at the Lower Manhattan skyline, a view that’s unique among New York hotels. There’s no more fitting location for 1 Hotels’ eco-luxe aesthetic, with its salvaged materials, stylish design, and low-impact construction than here in Brooklyn, alongside the lush green park that’s been reclaimed from the city’s post-industrial waterfront.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Wythe Hotel in Brooklyn
ld.description: It’s rare for a hotel to so completely exemplify the character of the neighborhood it calls home. Here, at Williamsburg’s Wythe Hotel, that means a location between McCarren Park and the gentrifying waterfront, in a 1901-vintage factory building that’s been lovingly (but not too thoroughly) renovated. And in the kitchen, it means a bit of Brooklyn culinary royalty: Aidan O’Neal and Jake Leiber, of the beloved Chez Ma Tante, are the chefs behind Le Crocodile, a neighborhood brasserie serving earnest French fare in a setting inspired by their Parisian and New York favorites. (They’re also responsible for Bar Blondeau, the 6th-floor bar with an unobstructed view of the Manhattan skyline.)

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Blind Tiger Burlington in Burlington
ld.description: The Northeastern hoteliers Lark Hotels are well known across the region for their stylish and smart boutique hotels; among their offerings are a number of small-scale, residential-style guest houses, under the Blind Tiger banner. Blind Tiger Burlington exemplifies the form: a private home dating to the late 19th century, lovingly restored and updated with 14 bedrooms, each one unique, all of them combining period architecture with unique vintage details and original contemporary artworks.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Dorian, Autograph Collection in Calgary
ld.description: The Dorian, Autograph Collection is just about as modern and as stylish as Calgary hotels get. The name is indeed a nod to Oscar Wilde’s Picture of Dorian Gray; presumably there’s an image of a far less attractive hotel locked away somewhere on the premises. The style is an eclectic blend of Deco-inspired elegance and flourishes of Victoriana, plus knowing references to Wilde himself; the in-room comforts, meanwhile, are state-of-the-art. In keeping with the local tradition, the Dorian’s restaurants feature plenty of Alberta-raised beef, alongside French-inspired cooking and plenty of lighter fare.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Camden Harbour Inn in Camden
ld.description: A 19th-century mansion with a view of Camden, Maine’s picturesque harbor might sound like a recipe for a trip back in time. But the Camden Harbour Inn is owned not by the descendants of its original owners, but a pair of Dutchmen who’ve adopted Camden as their second home — and adapted this beautiful old house to its new use as a very modern boutique-style bed and breakfast.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Norumbega Inn in Camden
ld.description: The Norumbega Inn seems pulled straight from a master painting. Set right on Route 1 overlooking Penobscot Bay in Midcoast Maine’s charming Camden, this castle promises a singular stay. Step inside one of the 11 guest rooms and suites and the hotel’s former life as a grand private residence (dating to 1887) will come as no surprise. Some rooms feature fireplaces while others open to terraces or frame stunning ocean views, but all sport a distinctive style with unique charm. Revel in the slow pace here and explore the grounds or savor a cocktail and snack at the bar.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: NIZUC Resort & Spa in Cancun
ld.description: With nearly 300 suites and an address in Cancún’s Zona Hotelera, NIZUC Resort & Spa is no pocket-sized boutique. But nor is it the typical Cancún resort. This corner of the coast is actually pretty spectacular, and it’s ever so slightly removed from the string of resorts lining the shore just to the north. Indeed Punta Nizuc, a mangrove-shaded piece of land that juts out into the Caribbean, faces one of the world’s largest barrier reefs, and reportedly served as a favorite stargazing spot for ancient Mayan astronomers. With a little concentration it’s possible to feel a bit like you’re on a private island, rather than on an extension of Mexico’s mega-resort zone.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria Riviera Maya in Cancun
ld.description: The down sides of Cancún — in short, that it’s crowded, tacky, and overbuilt — don’t seem to apply when you’re within the expansive perimeter of this luxe 173-room resort. It’s relatively secluded, sharing a substantial parcel of land with the nearby Hilton Cancun, and it’s nothing if not tasteful. Rooms and suites are spacious and stylish, without a hint of tropical kitsch, and they’re exceedingly well furnished, easily the equal of any urban luxury hotel. The spa is inspired by Maya culture and rituals, the restaurants by authentic Mexican flavors, and the brand’s signature service is on display throughout.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cliff House Maine in Cape Neddick
ld.description: On the picturesque coast of Southern Maine, at the edge of Cape Neddick, sits the iconic Cliff House, serving up spectacular ocean views since 1872. On the heels of a thorough transformation — and a significant expansion since the 19th century — this is now a totally modern luxury hotel, and not a small one. Each of its 226 rooms and suites opens onto a private terrace with a dramatic coastal view, and its grounds, sprawling over 70 acres of rough shoreline, contain outdoor swimming pools, a spa and wellness center, an enormous amount of events space, and, for larger parties, an outlying 3.5-bedroom cottage.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Bungalows & Casitas de las Flores in Careyes

ld.name: Bungalows & Casitas de las Flores in Careyes in Careyes
ld.description: Was it Walt Whitman or the nation of Mexico that said “I am large, I contain multitudes”? It was the poet, of course, but it’s equally true of Mexico — whether your picture of it is the ruined pyramids of the Yucatán or the hip nightspots of the Distrito Federal, you can bet there’s another side of Mexico you’re not considering. In the case of Costa Careyes, it’s the exclusive, relatively undeveloped, upscale yet unpretentious side.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bernardus Lodge & Spa in Carmel / Monterey
ld.description: The location alone would be enough to make Bernardus Lodge an attractive resort getaway. Tucked into the pines and oaks of Carmel Valley, the Lodge is remote enough to provide a measure of seclusion, yet still just minutes from the picturesque town of Carmel-by-the-Sea, and a short (and scenic) drive from Big Sur.
ld.petsAllowed: \n A $200 USD cleaning fee per pet per stay applies.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Villa Mara Carmel in Carmel / Monterey
ld.description: Lucky for visitors, Carmel-By-The-Sea hasn’t lost its boho-beachy beating heart, thanks in large part to eclectic boutiques the likes of Villa Mara Carmel. It’s an easy shout from both the beach and downtown, but sequestered enough to guarantee true peace for its 16 adults-only guestrooms. The decor skews upscale residential with plenty of handsome wooden furnishings and polished stone to go around. A full cocktail bar invites cozy nights in, as do the rambling grounds’ gardens and firepits.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Seminary Hill Orchard & Cidery in Catskills & Hudson Valley
ld.description: It’s been fifty years or more since the Catskills were so popular a destination, and the hotel scene, correspondingly, is booming. Seminary Hill Orchard & Cidery, on the outskirts of Callicoon, New York, has drawn attention for its modern cidery structure, which takes the traditional barn-style silhouette in a modern and extremely sustainable direction. Just down the road, however, in a pair of houses renovated by local hospitality experts Homestedt, is what brings us to Seminary Hill: the Boarding House, a 17-room boutique hotel in a Shaker-inspired contemporary-classic style.
ld.petsAllowed: Dogs under 50lbs are welcome for an additional fee of $100 per stay. Larger dogs and other pets cannot be accommodated at the property.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Six Bells Countryside Inn in Catskills & Hudson Valley
ld.description: Other New Yorkers have indulged country-house fantasies in the Hudson Valley, but none as intricately detailed and meticulously plotted as this. The Six Bells Countryside Inn is the work of entrepreneur Audrey Gelman, known first for a line of women-only co-working spaces and later for the Six Bells home goods shop in Brookyln’s Cobble Hill. There’s a whole fictional backstory and cast of characters involved in the Inn’s creation, but for guests, what matters most is that its eleven rooms (and its inviting public spaces) are as quietly luxurious as they are filled with visual interest.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Maker Hotel in Catskills & Hudson Valley
ld.description: The founders of the natural skincare brand Fresh were trailblazers in the “clean beauty” business. Their latest venture, a bohemian-chic boutique hotel in downtown Hudson, is a few hours away from their flagship shop in New York City, but the two have plenty in common: period charm, attention to detail, and, of course, first-rate bath products — the Maker features its own gender-inclusive fragrance.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Troutbeck in Catskills & Hudson Valley
ld.description: Troutbeck didn’t just wake up one morning and decide to style itself a creative retreat — it’s been walking the walk for well over a century, having welcomed naturalist John Burrows, author and civil rights activist W.E.B. Du Bois, writers Langston Hughes and Zora Neale Hurston and many others along the way. And while this estate, in Amenia, two hours from Manhattan, has seen some changes over the years — Benton Cottage dates back to 1760, while the 17th-century Manor House was rebuilt in 1919 — it’s perhaps most remarkable for its continuity.
ld.petsAllowed: Pet Policy: Are allowed only in our Benton House and Garden House Rooms. There is a $100 fee per stay that is charged at check out. Informing the hotel in advance of stay is required if your pet will be coming along for the reservation.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Wildflower Farms, Auberge Collection in Catskills & Hudson Valley
ld.description: Auberge was born in Napa Valley, but the brand’s expertise in luxe rural living is adaptable all over the world — from the California wine country to New York’s Hudson Valley. Wildflower Farms, Auberge Collection finds itself in Gardiner, on a working farm that’s more properly secluded than many Hudson Valley resorts. Alongside its 65 luxurious and surprisingly stylish cabins are the expansive Thistle Spa, and outdoor spaces encompass the whole of this working farm — whose produce, not incidentally, provides some of the ingredients for Clay, a restaurant singularly focused on Hudson Valley flavors and a wine selection that’s truly global.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: 86 Cannon Charleston in Charleston
ld.description: 86 Cannon Historic Inn is just about everything you could ask from a boutique hotel in Charleston, South Carolina: a well-preserved 1860s house updated with impeccably chic contemporary interiors (and a bit of a French accent), with a genteel residential calm that’s only fortified by its adults-only policy. The result is a lodging with all the amiable charm of a classic bed and breakfast and all the style of a proper luxury boutique hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Bennett Charleston in Charleston
ld.description: Charleston at its best is pure Southern elegance in Technicolor, and so is the Bennett, from its rotunda, bedecked with murals, to its salmon-pink Champagne lounge and its spectacular sky-blue rooftop bar. It’s a new build, though its style is a perfect match for its setting, right on Marion Square in the heart of town. The rooms dial down the saturation — they’re as heavenly as clouds, and just about as soft. From here, all the best of Charleston is right at your feet, though some of it is inside the hotel: the self-explanatory La Pâtisserie and the French-influenced Gabrielle restaurant are among the highlights.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Post House in Charleston
ld.description: A hotelier in Charleston — or, in the Post House’s case, the impossibly picturesque neighboring community of Mount Pleasant — can’t help but lean in to the region’s trademark genteel charm. That’s certainly the Post House’s strength; this well-preserved 19th-century house has been refashioned as a boutique inn, perhaps most properly understood as a very fine restaurant with a handful of beautifully crafted guest rooms. The style feels inevitable but at the same time studiously avoids cliché, which is no easy feat; the result is unique and memorable, which is for us more or less the whole ball game.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Dewberry in Charleston
ld.description: The downtown Charleston landmark formerly known as the L. Mendel Rivers Federal Building now bears the name of John Dewberry, the Atlanta developer who spent the better part of a decade transforming the structure. He didn’t just reimagine the building’s plain red brick facade, he commissioned local artisans to apply a custom-made gray limewash to the exterior. He didn’t just perk up the flowerbeds, he built a romantic walled garden evocative of old-world Charleston, then modeled the design of the hotel’s spa on his personal carriage house — and, along the way, assembled a dream team of architects, lighting specialists, and landscape designers, collaborating closely with a Brooklyn-based design firm and tapping a Charleston Preservation Designer to consult on the lavish marble and brass-fitted bathrooms.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Loutrel in Charleston
ld.description: Charleston, South Carolina’s French Quarter might not be the nation’s most famous, but it may very well be its finest — especially now that it’s home to the chic and luxurious Loutrel. This 50-room luxury boutique hotel is a new build, but one that does justice to the historical architecture that surrounds it; the interiors, too, are a mix of throwback elegance and 21st-century boutique-hotel style, and the rooms combine antique good looks with subtly high-tech modern comforts. Not to be missed: the Veranda Lounge, with its creative small-plates menu and botanical craft cocktails.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Nickel Hotel in Charleston
ld.description: The proprietors of downtown Charleston’s The Pinch chose Upper King Street, in Cannonborough, for the sequel. The Nickel Hotel is twice as large — a still boutique-sized 50 rooms and suites — and announces itself with just a touch more fanfare, thanks to a building by Morris Adjmi Architects whose façade, though unmistakably contemporary, pays tribute to the melting pot of historical styles that is Charleston. Once you’re in the central courtyard, though, ringed by three stories of wrought-iron balconies, you’ll likely do a double-take at the thoroughly immersive Victorian atmosphere.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Pinch Charleston in Charleston
ld.description: Just off King and George, in the very heart of Charleston, South Carolina, two historic Victorian-era structures and one contemporary one have been joined together to create the Pinch, a 25-room luxury boutique hotel that’s as stylish as anything in town — and possibly more comfortable. The interiors take some of their cues from the Victorian inspiration granted by the buildings’ heritage — from bold patterned wallpapers to period architectural ornaments — and update them with a modern color sense and an eclectic taste in furnishings and artworks.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Spectator Hotel in Charleston
ld.description: See and be seen, the Spectator Hotel’s name proclaims, and who are we to argue? This is Charleston, seat of the South’s historic capital, and a quick look at the hotel’s environs — where the French Quarter and Market Street districts come together — proves as much with a series of stately, pastel, pillared façades. Tradition counts, in other words, though not always in the high-Antebellum sense; here, you step lightly past varicolored brickwork, clean Modernist awnings, period lanterns, and a neat battalion of glossy windows into a four-story structure with a debonair, avuncular bearing. With a little renovation, the Roaring Twenties are in fine fettle for a victory lap in the Twenty-Twenties.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Hotel Chalet in Chattanooga
ld.description: Chattanooga’s Terminal Station was once a symbol of the golden age of rail travel. But the stately Beaux Arts–style building, home of the famous Chattanooga Choo Choo, barely escaped demolition in the 1970s. Newly protected as a historic site, it functioned as a Hilton hotel for decades. In its latest iteration as the Hotel Chalet, the landmark’s original grandeur has been fully restored — sunshine pours through dome-like skylights, classic cocktails are served through the window of a refurbished caboose, and the interiors, illuminated by antique lamps, exude old-world charm.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Chicago Athletic Association in Chicago
ld.description: Chicago’s architectural story began before modernism — this Venetian Gothic landmark, previously a private club for the city’s (male) movers and shakers, dates back to the final decade of the 19th century. But now, after a renovation by architects Hartshorne Plunkard and an interior redesign by hospitality wizards Roman and Williams, the Chicago Athletic Association, part of The Unbound Collection by Hyatt, is a thoroughly up-to-date boutique hotel, in that retro-modern, luxury-boutique sort of way.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Chicago in Chicago
ld.description: One of just a few hotels that sets the standard for the high end of the local luxury hotel scene, the Four Seasons Hotel Chicago towers above the Magnificent Mile, and looks straight out over Lake Michigan from its east-facing windows. A fairly recent renovation by Rottet Studio leaves it looking crisp and stylish, in a soothingly understated way. An impressive spa and indoor pool strike a tranquil note, while the hotel’s restaurant and bars mix guests with Chicago locals; just downstairs is Bloomingdale’s, and many of the city’s finest shops and restaurants are right at your feet.
ld.petsAllowed: \n One pet up to 15 pounds allowed per room for $100 cleaning fee.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Park Hyatt Chicago in Chicago
ld.description: The first Park Hyatt in the world opened on Chicago’s Magnificent Mile in 1980 — and several decades and multiple rounds of renovations later, it’s still a standout in the brand’s wide-ranging collection. The latest iteration is art-focused, a nod to the hotel’s location across the street from the Museum of Contemporary Art, and the best rooms come with impressive views of the dazzling expanse of Lake Michigan.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Your four-legged family member is welcome at Park Hyatt Chicago. For dogs weighing up to 50 pounds, a pet fee of $150 per stay is added with a stay for up to five nights. Stays of 6–30 nights include an additional $150 deep-cleaning fee. All dogs must be kept on a leash when walking through the hotel. Guests with disabilities traveling with their service animals are welcome. Service animals are not pets and are not subject to this pet policy. For more information, please contact customer service.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pendry Chicago  in Chicago
