ld.description: New York certainly has its architectural charms, but only in Chicago can a hotelier reasonably hope to set up shop in a masterwork like the 1929 Art Deco Carbide & Carbon Building, with its stately dark stone and immaculate gold trim. It’s a perfect fit for Pendry, the urban luxury-boutique cousin to the Montage resorts; Pendry Chicago combines contemporary boutique-hotel good looks with upscale comforts and impressive views of the distinctive Loop cityscape.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Gwen, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Michigan Avenue Chicago

ld.name: The Gwen, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Michigan Avenue Chicago in Chicago
ld.description: The Gwen doesn’t just echo the aesthetics of Twenties and Thirties Chicago, it’s an authentic piece of history — its façade comes from the 1929 McGraw-Hill building, and it’s named for the sculptor Gwen Lux, whose work still adorns it today. Inside it’s a thoroughly contemporary boutique-style luxury hotel, with Art Deco accents and 21st-century comforts. There’s an open-air rooftop bar (complete with firepits) and a weekend “Tipsy Tea” served in the hotel’s lounge; an ideal prelude to an afternoon in what might be one of Chicago’s finest shopping districts.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Langham Chicago in Chicago
ld.description: There was a time when Chicago’s hotel scene, on the whole, lagged far behind those of coastal capitals like New York and Los Angeles. Today, though, its best hotels are more than worthy of its status as a world-class city. A hotel like the Langham, Chicago, then, is a sign of the times, and a remarkably complete package as well: contemporary design, state-of-the-art comforts, thoughtful, professional service, and a link to the city’s urban history, embodied in its location: 330 North Wabash, formerly known as IBM Plaza, the last work of the modernist master architect Ludwig Mies Van der Rohe.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Peninsula Chicago in Chicago
ld.description: In the middle of Chicago’s Magnificent Mile of department stores and designer boutiques is the Peninsula Hotel, only the third in America. The Peninsula’s brand of Hong Kong luxury has fared well in New York and LA, but in the heartland?

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Viceroy Chicago in Chicago
ld.description: The Viceroy hotels exist at the intersection of luxury-hotel extravagance and boutique-hotel tastefulness, and the brand-new Viceroy Chicago is no different. The building, a gently undulating glass tower, is pure luxe modernity, but the lower floors blend effortlessly into Chicago’s Gold Coast, thanks to the meticulously preserved façade of the 1920s-vintage Cedar Hotel, which was reassembled brick by brick once the tower was complete.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago in Chicago
ld.description: Even in a city with some truly monumental architecture, the Waldorf Astoria Chicago feels like a remarkably grand hotel. One look at the huge English courtyard, or the museum-like marble lobby, and it’s clear that this is a full-scale luxury hotel all the way — especially since all this black, white, and polish gives off a dazzling Art Deco vibe. Fortunately the hotel undercuts its potentially chilly elegance with outstanding service, for which no staff person is allowed to accept a tip — or maybe that’s just good old Midwestern friendliness.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Central Hotel Boutique in Chihuahua City
ld.description: It would be hard to imagine a more distinguished setting for a hotel in Chihuahua than this, right in the heart of the historic city center, next to the Plaza de Armas and the 18th-century cathedral. And the Central Hotel Boutique makes its home in a distinguished building as well: Casa Trías dates back to 1845, and is the city’s oldest estate-style courtyard house. And today, after more than two decades under its present ownership, it’s attained some distinction as a hotel: this is by a considerable distance the most stylish and most luxurious lodging in town.
ld.petsAllowed: No pets allowed

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Chablé Yucatan in Chocholá
ld.description: Buried deep in the Yucatán jungle, tucked among Mayan ruins and sacred sites, is a more modern sort of temple, the kind built for relaxation. Chablé isn’t just a luxury hotel — it’s a wellness resort that’s worthy of the name. When you arrive, the staff will work with you to devise a personal program based on your particular relaxation needs: you might be prescribed yoga, biking, meditation, or Mayan-inspired healing techniques. You’ll almost certainly plan to spend some time in the excellent spa, which is built around a natural cenote, a swimming hole with healing waters, sacred to the ancient Maya.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Cleveland's Fidelity Hotel in Cleveland
ld.description: In the restored 1920s Fidelity Mortgage Building, this 97-room newcomer channels Cleveland’s past with fresh intent. Once surrounded by jazz joints and whiskey bars, the hotel now sits at the edge of what was Short Vincent, back when the city partied like New York. Inside, the design is rich, tactile, and confidently nostalgic: pour-over coffee, Bellino linens, sculptural lighting, and deep colors in all the right places. Downstairs, the Club Room brings it together: strong drinks, low lighting, and a setting that feels just right.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Broadmoor in Colorado Springs
ld.description: The legendary Broadmoor has stood at the foot of Cheyenne Mountain since 1891 — a near-eternity in the American West. For decades it’s been one of Colorado’s most iconic hotels, a sprawling Italian neoclassical compound against a backdrop of dramatic skies and purple mountain majesty. This is a destination resort, to be sure; it’s the rare Broadmoor guest who just happens to have business in sleepy Colorado Springs. They’re here for the golf, for the scenery, and for the award-winning hospitality.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Mining Exchange in Colorado Springs
ld.description: Originally the Colorado Springs Mining Stock Exchange, this hotel occupies four Italian Renaissance buildings with Art Deco flourishes. Authentic steel vaults remain on every floor, a relic from its financial heyday, alongside tin ceilings, brass railings, and brick walls. The lobby leans into Victorian grandeur with gold-toned furnishings that acknowledge the city's mining past, an antique Franz Wirth piano, and a marble fireplace. Rooms vary in layout but share granite desktops, high ceilings, and stone showers with dual heads. It is now managed by Wyndham, though the property retains its historic character.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Las Alamandas in Costalegre / Pacific Coast
ld.description: The backstory seems too fantastic to be true, like something from a Roger Moore-era James Bond movie. Don Antenor Patino, the Bolivian tin magnate, plans a beachfront mega-resort, but doesn’t live to complete it — so his granddaughter Isabel Goldsmith (English financier father, long story) takes over. In the interest of preserving the land (and the dolphins) so dear to her, she revises her grandfather’s plan and erects a tiny, exclusive resort, where a maximum of 28 guests have at their disposal 2,000 acres of pristine beachfront land and close to 100 staff members.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: No.10 Río Amacuzac, Col. Vista Hermosa

ld.name: Anticavilla Hotel in Cuernavaca
ld.description: Mexico’s got its share of ultra-modern design hotels, and it’s got its share of splendid old houses turned luxury hotels. And in Anticavilla Hotel it’s got a little bit of both. This stunning colonial-era property in Cuernavaca has been not just lovingly restored, but positively reconfigured by the efforts of architect Bernardo Gómez Pimienta, whose modernist interventions in the old house’s interiors lead to some ultra-modern external spaces, including a new spa and a dazzling open-air restaurant and lounge facing into the hotel’s gardens.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Las Casas B+B Hotel in Cuernavaca
ld.description: Cuernavaca is a destination that’s most popular among residents of Mexico City, which makes sense, given that it’s just two hours’ drive from the capital. But international travelers will find a stop here makes a delighful counterpoint to the Distrito Federal — and for a laid-back, low-key luxury boutique experience you could hardly do better than Las Casas B+B Hotel, an 11-room hideaway right in the heart of Cuernavaca’s pocket-sized downtown.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Casa Duro in Dallas
ld.description: On Lower Greenville Avenue in Dallas is something genuinely surprising: a restaurant, Sister, and a café, Duro, both “Italianish” in concept, and both by the small but highly regarded Duro Hospitality Group. They’re remarkable for their quality and also for their authentically European atmosphere, something that’s not exactly common in this town. And upstairs from both is a hotel that, if we’re honest, might be too small to be properly considered a hotel: Casa Duro, a three-room guest house, or a trio of apartments, by the same owners, where their appetite for Italian culture is allowed to run wild.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed with a deposit of USD 150 per stay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Swexan in Dallas
ld.description: That’s a portmanteau of “Swiss” and “Texan”, if you’re wondering, and it’s a gamble that pays off bigger the longer you stay. Hotel Swexan draws on this dual heritage to conjure the effortless charm of continental service standards plus larger-than-life Texan swagger. It’s a lot of hotel in the Harwood district, itself a walkable oasis in Uptown Dallas, and there’s no shortage of must-try activities without even leaving the grounds. Call it cowboy entrepreneur: spacious, no-expense-spared rooms with commanding views, but also a freewheeling sense of humor and up-for-anything energy in the decor. It looks, feels, and acts like the flagship property it is. Head to the roof at some point every night and drink it in.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel ZaZa Dallas in Dallas
ld.description: Just because you’re going to Dallas doesn’t mean you have to stay at one of the big chain hotels. Hotel ZaZa is, if you can believe it, a bit of the south of France, transplanted to the south-central United States. It’s a conceit that seems difficult to carry off, but in this case it certainly works, resulting in one of Dallas’s most extraordinary hotels.
ld.petsAllowed: Hotel ZaZa is a pet-friendly facility. A one-time, non-refundable deposit of $150 per pet is required at check in.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Mansion on Turtle Creek in Dallas
ld.description: The Rosewood Mansion on Turtle Creek most definitely lives up to its name: it doesn’t seem like a hotel, but an extravagant house. The 143 room structure was built, in 1925, as a residence for cotton baron Sheppard King, and is the ultimate in old-fashioned Dallas opulence. Here, you live it up like the tycoons of the past. A lot of people call it the best hotel in the States.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Triple Creek Ranch in Darby
ld.description: To indulge in such rugged pastimes as fly-fishing and snowmobiling, you’re willing to accept a certain coarseness of accommodations. Here, though, it is possible to experience the spectacular landscape of the heart of Montana while making your home in a luxurious private cabin, complete with the full range of amenities.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Clayton Hotel & Members Club - Cherry Creek, Denver

ld.name: Clayton Hotel & Members Club - Cherry Creek, Denver in Denver
ld.description: A few miles to the south of downtown Denver and the stadium district, in the upscale country club–adjacent enclave of Cherry Creek North, the Clayton Hotel & Members Club aims to thread a very particular needle: to be desirable yet inclusive, chic yet unstuffy, to be a private members’ club without universally drawing from among the already privileged.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed for a charge of USD $150 per stay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Denver in Denver
ld.description: It’s a fine line the Four Seasons walks. On the one hand, luxury guests expect meticulous service and a laundry list of upscale amenities. But if the experience is too consistent, it risks lapsing into sameness. The Four Seasons challenge has been maintaining its high standards while still managing to tailor the experience to the locality. The Four Seasons Denver is a case in point: from this spire-topped skyscraper, with its far-ranging views of the Rockies and the plains, it would be quite a feat if you managed to forget where you were.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Populus Denver in Denver
ld.description: Colorado’s native aspen tree was the inspiration behind the striking and unique look of this modern eco-hotel, which opened in 2024. Its aim is to “bring nature back into our cities” and for this it makes clever use of plenty of natural and recycled materials, as well as local flora. Work from local artists also features and there’s even birdsong played in the elevator. The green credentials might be impressive, but they’ve also created an exceedingly comfortable hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Crawford Hotel in Denver
ld.description: Thanks to a wave of redevelopment, downtown Denver’s once-neglected Union Station finds itself surrounded by action in a way it hasn’t been for more than half a century. LoDo, short for Lower Downtown, has brought life back to the city center, and this Beaux-Arts monument deserved to be more than a footnote in transportation history. Now it’s an authentic downtown gathering place, as well as the home of the Crawford Hotel, a 112-room boutique hotel whose lobby still does double duty as a waiting room for rail passengers.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Shinola Hotel in Detroit
ld.description: Perhaps no city in the United States is as famous for its precipitous decline as Detroit — the decline of the American auto industry hit it like a natural disaster, turning whole neighborhoods into post-apocalyptic ghost towns. But where there’s a low, there’s an opportunity to rise up, and today Detroit is also famous for the urban revitalization that’s currently in full swing. It’s a story that’s intimately bound up with the rise of the Detroit-based Shinola, a retailer selling watches, bicycles, and lifestyle products manufactured largely in America. And to this story we can add another tangible improvement that Shinola has made to downtown Detroit: the Shinola Hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: Dog-friendly accommodations are available for up to two dogs, with no weight or breed restrictions, for a $125 + tax pet fee.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Townsend Hotel in Detroit
ld.description: Much of the buzz about Detroit is focused on its inner-city renewal, but that’s far from the only story in town. There’s plenty worth knowing about in the outlying suburbs as well — and this includes the lovely town of Birmingham, Michigan, home of the Townsend Hotel. The building dates back only to the 1980s, but in hotels, as in so many other areas of life, it’s what’s inside that counts. In the case of the Townsend what’s inside is an absolutely classic luxury hotel, one that you’d swear had existed in its present form for half a century or more.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Dunton Hot Springs in Dolores
ld.description: Mountain hotels come in all shapes and sizes, from rustic lodges to luxurious mega-resorts and everything in between; nowhere, though, is there anything like Dunton Hot Springs. Here, in remote southwestern Colorado, along the banks of the Dolores river, halfway between the ski town of Telluride and the Anasazi ruins of Mesa Verde, is an authentic ghost town, an abandoned century-old gold prospectors’ camp, renovated shack by shack and rehabilitated into a truly unique luxury hotel — a place where roughing it in hand-hewn log cabins (and one teepee) neatly coincides with spa treatments, thermal baths and fine organic dining.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Plaza Hotel Pioneer Park in El Paso
ld.description: This 1930s Art Deco skyscraper would be hard to miss even if it didn’t have “PLAZA” emblazoned on it in glowing red letters. This was a hideout for Hollywood stars in on vacation in West Texas, during the days before jet travel, and today it trades on its combination of historical personality and contemporary style. Rooms are spacious, with far-ranging views over the city and beyond, and all come with marble bathrooms, Le Labo bath products, Nespresso machines, and Tivoli sound systems. Restaurants include the lobby-level Ámbar, a Juarez-style Mexican restaurant and bar, and La Perla, the 17th-floor rooftop bar.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Inns of Aurora in Finger Lakes
ld.description: The village of Aurora, New York lies on the shores of Lake Cayuga, one of upstate’s picturesque Finger Lakes. There’s not much to it, which is sort of the point, but what Aurora does have is a collection of five inns, all of them more than a century old, now restored and renovated to luxury-boutique standard and doing business together as the Inns of Aurora.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Little Palm Island in Florida Keys
ld.description: The most distinctive feature of the Florida Keys might be the Overseas Highway, the stretch of U.S. Route 1 that makes the trip from Miami to Key West into a routine car trip. But Little Palm Island is anything but routine. Guests arrive at the relatively ordinary Little Torch Key and transfer to a yacht named for Harry Truman for the final hop to an island that was one of the former president’s favorite haunts, and is now the only private island resort in North America: Little Palm Island.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: The Marquesa Hotel in Florida Keys
ld.description: In all the noise being made about Miami, it’s easy to forget that the classic Florida holiday destination still lies two hours’ drive from the mainland. Like any travel town in America, Key West has its charmless and overdeveloped side; but Old Town, home to the incomparable Marquesa Hotel, belongs to the locals, and to history—this is the Key West of Hemingway, of Tennessee Williams, an oasis of old-world refinement at the edge of the continent.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Carr Mansion in Galveston
ld.description: There’s no place, in Texas or anywhere else, quite like Galveston — and the same can be said of the Carr Mansion, an 1866 Greek Revival mansion that’s lived several lives before its most recent transformation into an adults-only boutique bed and breakfast. The house is fantastically well-preserved and beautifully updated, thanks to inspired work by the Austin-based designer Shannon Eddings, and while its new proprietors haven’t been shy about furnishing its interiors in a tasteful modern-luxe style, they’ve been careful to keep its unique personality intact — every room is an experience unto itself.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Tu Tu' Tun Lodge in Gold Beach
ld.description: Tu Tu’ Tun Lodge has been a Rogue River retreat since the 1970s, surrounded by dense greenery and just a few miles from Siskiyou National Forest. It’s the kind of place where the most popular activity is listed as “Do Nothing,” though guests also hike to Cape Sebastian, go fishing or take kayaks upriver. Rooms in the main lodge bring the outdoors in with cedar beams, slate hearths, and river rock fireplaces, while larger houses like Osprey Bend offer full kitchens, hot tubs and wraparound decks designed for grilling and gathering. Dinner is is a farm-to-table affair highlighting fresh, seasonal Northwest ingredients.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Blackberry Farm in Great Smoky Mountains
ld.description: The Great Smoky Mountains of Tennessee are home to what is, by any measure, one of the most extraordinary hotels in the United States. Blackberry Farm was a pioneer in the area of farm-to-table dining, and its kitchens show no signs of relinquishing their early lead. Meanwhile, alongside the farm’s three fine restaurants are 68 rooms, suites, cottages, and houses that are the equal of any luxury-hotel lodging in the Southeast, and a good deal more memorable.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Paws Up Montana in Greenough
ld.description: Backcountry living in the Montana Rockies never felt quite so luxe. Deep in the heart of the American West, an easy 40 minutes from Missoula airport (and another 40 minutes from the exact middle of nowhere), Paws Up Montana is for the traveler who wants a wilderness escape to include all the comforts of civilization.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Proximity Hotel in Greensboro
ld.description: Why Greensboro, North Carolina? Because that’s where the Proximity Hotel is — and a hotel like this deserves to get noticed no matter where in the world it’s located. It’s contemporary in design, it’s independently owned, it’s state-of-the-art in function, and it’s manageably small — all qualities we admire. But the central point to be made about the Proximity is that it’s got a genuine shot at being the greenest hotel in North America — and has the LEED Platinum certification to prove it.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Nueve 25 Hotel Boutique in Guanajuato
ld.description: To call Guanajuato an old mining town hardly does it justice. It's perhaps better described as the one-time location of the world’s largest silver extraction site, a town founded and made fabulously wealthy after the Spanish struck gold and silver in the early 16th century. Nueve 25 Hotel Boutique is one of a handful of luxury hotels in the UNESCO-honored historic center, the name a reference to the precious metal — a composition of at least 92.5% pure silver is required for the denomination of sterling silver — that put Guanajuato on the map.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Stillpoint Lodge in Halibut Cove
ld.description: Like many destinations on the Alaskan coast, the fishing village–art colony town of Halibut Cove, on the Kenai Peninsula, can only be reached by air or by sea. Stillpoint Lodge is upscale lodge living, its cabins constructed from local Alaskan timber — anything else, in this environment, would feel far too polished. The interiors, as rustic as their materials may be, are extremely comfortable, with plentiful light, lavish beds and baths, and extraordinary views from their porches, picture windows, or both. The lodge offers space for yoga, massage, or just lounging, as well as a hot tub and sauna. And since you can’t just pop into town for dinner, you’ll take all your meals here, sourced from local Alaskan seafood, meat, and produce.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Missing Hotel in Hill Country
ld.description: It’s an unusual name, but it makes its point: what’s gone missing at Missing Hotel is not the hotel itself, but you, for the duration of your stay. This 11-unit escape is set near the town of Marble Falls, just beyond the outskirts of Austin — close enough for an easy weekend trip, but far enough to feel properly secluded. Call it glamping, if you must, or forest bathing, or just a Hill Country getaway, but the bottom line is the same: a collection of geodesic domes and villas built on platforms amid the treetops, each one with a plunge pool or a hot tub for maximum relaxation. The style is a quirky mix of modern and bohemian, and is nothing if not memorable — and the same goes for the whole experience, which is perfectly comfortable yet delighfully off-the-grid.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Halekulani in Honolulu
ld.description: At 453 rooms it’s not small. But once you’ve settled on Waikiki Beach as a destination it’s clear that you’ve decided to forget about secondary concerns like secrecy, exclusivity, hipness, and the like, and simply focus on pleasure. And at that point you could do a whole lot worse than Halekulani.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Waikiki Beach in Honolulu
ld.description: Just off Kalakaua Avenue rather than on it, this dual-tower high-rise keeps its lobby, restaurants and pools on the eighth floor: no passing foot traffic, no crowded bars, and a calm that most Waikiki addresses can't offer. All 552 units are individually owned residences: even the smallest king room starts at 500 square feet with a kitchenette, living area and laundry. Upper floors scale through one, two and three-bedroom configurations, color palettes shifting by level to reflect the island's landscapes. Solera is the open-air rooftop restaurant; ten-seat omakase counter Sushi Sho requires booking well ahead.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Daphne in Houston
ld.description: Where there’s a boutique hotel in Texas you’re likely to find the Bunkhouse name, and Hotel Daphne in Houston is part of the family. This 49-room escape in Houston Heights embraces the artistic, bohemian side of Houston, an angle that sets it apart from the majority of the city’s lodgings. Hypsi, the hotel’s Italian restaurant, is helmed by a celebrated local chef, and the lobby library doubles as a shop displaying a curated selection of locally produced goods.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Saint Augustine in Houston
ld.description: Tucked into Montrose’s leafy streets, Hotel Saint Augustine is a thoughtfully composed stay with a strong design point of view. Spread across five buildings, it mixes eras and materials like burled walnut, red lacquer, Calacatta Viola, with sculptural furniture and vintage finds. Guest rooms offer a softer counterpoint to the richness of the public spaces, some with screened porches set among the trees. It is smart, well-made, and exactly what this part of Houston was missing.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel ZaZa Museum District in Houston
ld.description: In Texas everything really is a little bit bigger, a little bit bolder. And the boutique hotels are no exception. Downtown Houston’s Hotel ZaZa, the second from the Dallas-based group, puts decadence first, and you won’t confuse it for a business chain anytime soon.
ld.petsAllowed: Hotel ZaZa is a pet-friendly facility. A one-time, non-refundable deposit of $150 per pet is required at check in.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel ZaZa Memorial City in Houston
ld.description: Given Houston’s status as America’s fourth-largest city, it’s perhaps a bit surprising that there isn’t a boutique-hotel scene quite on the scale of those in places like New York, Los Angeles, or Chicago. But it’s certainly not for lack of effort on the part of Texas’s small but faithful contingent of boutique hoteliers. Hotel ZaZa Memorial City is the sequel to the decade-old Museum District installment, and brings the brand’s familiar high-end, high-style experience to the west side of Houston.
ld.petsAllowed: Hotel ZaZa is a pet-friendly facility. A one-time, non-refundable deposit of $150 per pet is required at check in.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Post Oak Hotel at Uptown Houston

ld.name: The Post Oak Hotel at Uptown Houston in Houston
ld.description: Houston has no shortage of high-end hotels from the big luxury chains, but the swankiest hotel in town might just be an independent. The Post Oak Hotel at Uptown Houston’s lobby features an enormous Swarovski crystal chandelier and a number of Frank Stella originals, and this no-expense-spared philosophy extends to the rooms, which start out at 500 square feet and include lavish marble bathrooms with Acqua di Parma bath products and even a small set of in-room dumbbells. There’s an impressive spa as well, with a well-equipped fitness center, and a lovely outdoor pool, plus two restaurants, a cocktail bar, and a patisserie.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bottleworks Hotel Indianapolis in Indianapolis
ld.description: Formerly the local Coca-Cola bottling plant, the Bottleworks dates back to the 1920s, when industrial buildings still benefited from Art Deco styling. Today the old plant is a mixed-use, arts- and culture-focused development whose anchor is the Bottleworks Hotel. The rooms and suites in the old wing combine authentic industrial flourishes with contemporary comforts and modern furniture, while those in the new addition are perhaps less historic but no less stylish. And the Bottleworks development’s dining and drinking options are many, from the hip Blue Collar Coffee Co. to the multitude of local vendors occupying the Garage Food Hall.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Ironworks Hotel Indy in Indianapolis
ld.description: You don’t have to be a hospitality-industry analyst to predict that the Ironworks Hotel, in Indianapolis, Indiana, takes its aesthetic inspiration from the industrial heyday of the Midwest. And though it’s a new build, it’s meant to evoke the kind of heavy industry that’s implied by the name. This means a heavy brick facade broken up by full-height shop windows — and inside, it means visible infrastructure, exposed piping, and what feels like acres of heavily weathered salvaged barn wood.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Casa Las Tortugas Petit Beach Hotel & Spa

ld.name: Casa Las Tortugas Petit Beach Hotel & Spa in Isla Holbox
ld.description: The night before opening in December 2003, thirteen turtles came ashore at Holbox — and that settled the name. Adults-only and barefoot in spirit, the hotel has rooms and suites stepping up from beachfront ground level to rooftop terraces with private pools looking out over the Gulf of Mexico. Yucatan honey toiletries, woven hammocks and Starlink internet make up the in-room picture. Mandarina does Mediterranean-Mexican cooking on the sand, AMA is a Japanese bar with second-floor sunset views, and UMO fires everything from local and organic produce. Complimentary yoga most mornings keeps the pace slow.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Nômade Temple Holbox in Isla Holbox
ld.description: A tourism boom has changed Isla Holbox in recent years, bringing an influx of international visitors to the once-sleepy island just north of the Yucatán Peninsula. It’s still a tropical paradise — blissfully car-free and part of Mexico's largest nature reserve, which is famously a sanctuary for the world’s largest fish — but it’s harder these days to find peace and quiet on the sand. Enter Nômade Temple Holbox, a luxurious and eco-conscious adults-only retreat that’s a 15-minute golf-cart ride from the ferry terminal, pleasantly removed from the busier parts of the island and set right on a secluded beach.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Hualalai in Island of Hawaii
ld.description: With all the action happening on the beaches of Oahu and Maui and in the deep forests of Kauai, it’s easy to overlook the Big Island. And perverse as it may be to claim that any part of Hawaii qualifies as a well-kept secret, it’s nevertheless true that the island of Hawaii, for all its natural beauty, is under-traveled, relative to its neighbors. Thus it’s the perfect site for a resort like the Four Seasons Hualalai. For as luxurious as it may be, this is anything but an ostentatious monument of a hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets up to 25llbs are allowed, however please be aware of Hawaii's four month pet quarantine requirement.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Kona Village, A Rosewood Resort in Island of Hawaii
ld.description: The original Kona Village was a Sixties classic, and in many ways a forerunner of the boutiue-inspired style that is the state of the luxury-resort art today: no vast central complex, but a loose network of traditionally constructed bungalows lining the seaside cliffs and the lagoon. Its story was interrupted by the tsunami of 2011, but this Big Island favorite is back, this time as Kona Village, a Rosewood Resort.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Mauna Lani, Auberge Collection in Island of Hawaii
ld.description: When we were young, Hawaii was somewhat out of fashion as a travel destination — cheap airfares had put farther-flung destinations within reach, and the mid-century style of many of the islands’ hotels had fallen into a sort of uncanny valley, too recent to be retro but definitively out of style. It’s hard to imagine now. Fresh off a huge interior renovation, the Mauna Lani Bay Hotel and Bungalows, on the Kohala Coast of the Big Island, is looking better than ever.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: 1 Hotel Hanalei Bay in Island of Kauai
ld.description: The 1 Hotels are verdant enough in Midtown Manhattan and West Hollywood; the brand’s Kaua’i outpost is on another level. 1 Hotel Hanalei Bay does its best to blend in with the vegetation on the bluff in Princeville, just across the river (but 15 minutes’ drive) from Hanalei Beach. It’s as sustainable as they come, but it’s also outrageously luxurious — not in an outdated country-club way, but in the new style: the rooms and suites are comfortable and subtly high-tech, while the spa, fitness, and outdoor recreation offerings are the absolute state of the art.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Timbers Kauai Ocean Club & Residences in Island of Kauai
ld.description: The Garden Island of Kaua‘i is wild enough to have featured as a filming location for TV’s Lost and various Jurassic Park films, but what’s perhaps most appealing about it is that its unspoiled landscapes and seascapes aren’t all that hard to reach. Timbers Kaua‘i is a case in point; here you’re surrounded by impossible vistas, pressed right up against the water’s edge, and yet you’re minutes from Lihue, the island’s largest settlement (and, crucially, the home of its commercial airport).
ld.petsAllowed: This is a smoke free and pet free property

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Lana'i in Island of Lanai
ld.description: In contrast with the more famous and more heavily traveled Hawaiian islands Lanai remains delightfully wild — most roads are unpaved, and there’s famously not a single traffic light on the island. This means a resort like the Four Seasons Resort Lanai feels properly secluded. And while the landscape may be rugged, life here is plush indeed — the resort’s 35-acre estate stands on a bluff above Hulopo’e Beach, and its grounds are thick with palm trees, gardens, and pools, a real-life Eden on the island’s south coast. Among the attractions are the Hawanawana Spa and the spectacular Jack Nicklaus Manele Golf Course; excursions include Jeep rides, catamaran tours, horseback outings, and much more.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets up to 25llbs are allowed, however please be aware of Hawaii's four month pet quarantine requirement.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea in Island of Maui
ld.description: Safe to say Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea doesn’t exactly fly under the radar. With 380 rooms and suites divided among multiple buildings spread across its 15 acres, it’s a substantial resort by any standard. And its spaces, both interior and exterior, are perhaps more familiar to the general public than is typical for a resort of its caliber — this was, after all, the filming location for the first season of The White Lotus.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets up to 25llbs are allowed, however please be aware of Hawaii's four month pet quarantine requirement.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Resort at Kapalua Bay, Maui

ld.name: The Resort at Kapalua Bay, Maui in Island of Maui
ld.description: Despite its relatively modest capacity — just 56 units — The Resort at Kapalua Bay, Maui has all the facilities of a much larger resort, as well as a privileged location that’s flanked by a pair of golf courses, a nature reserve, and a marine reserve with some phenomenal diving and snorkeling. Safe to say you’ll be hard pressed to think of anything that’s missing.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Inn at Thorn Hill in Jackson
ld.description: The Inn at Thorn Hill, a luxury hotel and spa in the woods of northern New Hampshire, is nothing if not relaxing. Each of the suites and rooms of the main building has its own unique style and layout, but all feature two-person whirlpool bathtubs and gas fireplaces. Guests in need of more space and privacy may also choose from a pair of charming independent cottages, while a larger group may prefer the historic carriage house, adjacent to the main building, whose six rooms can accommodate up to twelve guests. The spa provides a sauna as well as a generous menu of beauty treatments, while the hotel’s Dining Room serves upscale American cuisine, alongside a tavern with a fantastic selection of classic cocktails, wines, and draft beers.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Caldera House in Jackson Hole
ld.description: Some American ski lodges prize physical comfort above all else, and strive to be as inoffensive as possible in their aesthetics. Others focus most of their efforts on atmosphere and design, and go light on the kinds of extravagances that make a hotel a luxury hotel. What’s rare is a hotel that does both — but Caldera House, in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, is exceptional in exactly this way.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Jackson in Jackson Hole
ld.description: If there’s one town in America that most thoroughly combines Rocky Mountain ruggedness with top-shelf luxury, it’s Jackson, Wyoming. And it’s this precise pairing that is embodied in the Hotel Jackson: the textured wood and rough stone, visible both inside and out, pay tribute to the natural spectacle that is Jackson Hole, while the clean, geometric lines of the hotel’s modernist-inspired architecture — and the luxurious finishes, in leather and fur — demonstrate its upscale aspirations.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Cloudveil, Autograph Collection in Jackson Hole
ld.description: Jackson Hole is no stranger to high-end hospitality, nor to the high-design influence of the boutique-hotel world; the Cloudveil connects these two threads. Set right on the old town square, it’s an unmistakably modern hotel, though its silhouette complements the old Western architecture of its surroundings, and its materials pay tribute to the Rockies themselves. Its interiors mix mountain-lodge coziness with contemporary crispness, and the details are state-of-the-art, right down to the high-tech fitness center. The Bistro occupies two spaces: the lobby-adjacent dining room and the open-air rooftop deck.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Crossroads Hotel in Kansas City
ld.description: Kansas City’s Crossroads Hotel is a beacon of hospitality amidst a collection of low-rise, historically protected brick buildings that comprise the Crossroads arts district from which it takes its name. Its 131 luxuriously appointed guest rooms are decorated in an industrial-chic style, with exposed brick walls and occasional exposed timber beams; a billiards table and a wet bar are the feathers in the caps of the adjoining Pendergast Suite and H.S. Truman Parlor. A rooftop bar, Percheron, offers skyline views, craft cocktails and bocce, while XR Cafe serves coffee, spirits, and casual bites. Prime cuts sizzle and unctuous burrata sits atop fresh greens at Lazia, the hotel’s Italian restaurant.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: AWOL Kennebunkport in Kennebunkport
ld.description: The second installment in Lark Hotels’ AWOL series finds itself in the classic coastal destination of Kennebunkport, Maine, most famously the site of the Bush dynasty’s compound and other upper-crust vacation homes. But AWOL Kennebunkport, designed by the Massachusetts-based Elder & Ash, is much more stylish than the setting might suggest. It’s centered around the historic Captain Walker house, right on the edge of the compact town center, no more than a few minutes’ walk from anything else in town. And to the six-bedroom main house they’ve added a further eleven suites in a more modern style, in cabins spread across the grounds.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pet-friendly accommodations are available in select units. Please contact customer service prior to arrival for arrangements.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Kennebunkport Captains Collection in Kennebunkport
ld.description: Kennebunkport may be most widely known as a summertime haunt for the likes of the Bush dynasty, but the reasons it became a presidential getaway are good reasons for just about anyone to visit: the town itself is a typically welcoming New England seaport, with all the pleasures and perks of a small maritime village. In short, it’s a healthy environment for a top-shelf bed-and-breakfast like the Kennebunkport Captains Collection. Housed in a renovated Federal mansion dating back to 1813, this hotel is situated on a quiet tree-lined street within easy walking distance of galleries and antique shops.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Belvedere Hotel - Kingston in Kingston ON
ld.description: Built as a private residence in 1880, the hotel once known as Chateau Belvedere was, by the middle of the 20th century, the most glamorous lodging in town. Today, as the Hotel Belvedere, it’s no less impressive — just a touch more low-key. After a thorough restoration, its decades-spanning historical charms are on full display, complemented by a touch of era-appropriate contemporary design; the result is a first-rate luxury boutique hotel on a modest, local scale.
ld.petsAllowed: \n No pets are allowed. Exceptions may be made under special circumstances, such as service animals, and must be arranged in advance. A pet deposit may apply if approved.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Smith Hotel in Kingston ON
ld.description: Kingston, Ontario’s Smith Hotel is an unusual one on both the large and the small scale — the former because it’s made not from a historical residence but from a 19th-century church, and the latter because its units are less like typical hotel rooms and more like loft apartments, split across two levels and full of contrast between modern design and antique ecclesiastical architecture.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Tennessean Hotel in Knoxville
ld.description: We told you we wouldn’t rest until there’s a properly stylish and inventive boutique hotel in every city in America. And while we’re not yet ready to declare our mission accomplished, the advent of the Tennessean Hotel, in Knoxville, Tennessee, brings us one step closer to our goal. The location, bordering on World’s Fair Park, is central, convenient to both the convention center and the best restaurants and breweries in downtown Knoxville. And the hotel itself offers a first-rate luxury boutique experience: stylish, memorable, and lacking for nothing when it comes to comfort.
ld.petsAllowed: Pet Policy: Dogs only with a weight restriction of 50lbs. Pet charge is $100.00 per stay. Dog bed provided. Dogs must be kenneled if left alone in the room. Guests must inform hotel prior to arrival if pet will be accompany them. Dog park is available by parking garage. Guests responsible for any damage, interruption of other guests or failure to clean up after dog.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Charmant Hotel in La Crosse
ld.description: A taste of France in the Midwest? No, it’s not a questionable new theme park attraction: La Crosse, Wisconsin was actually settled by French fur traders. It was French people who named this small city on the Mississippi River, and referred to the region’s high ridges as coulées, a term that’s still used today (sans acute accent). La Crosse comes by its French heritage honestly, so it’s no wonder that the cool new hotel in town is called the Charmant Hotel — that’s “charming hotel,” in case you took Spanish in high school.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Post Hotel & Spa in Lake Louise
ld.description: Alberta may be flyover country to the urban leisure traveler, and coastal folk who ski are apt to check out Whistler or Tahoe, even Park City or Vail before venturing this far into Western Canada. That’s their loss, though, and that many more available rooms around Lake Louise, the jewel of the Canadian Rockies, in the heart of the picturesque Banff National Park.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise in Lake Louise
ld.description: The railway hotels of the Canadian Rockies are famous for their grand scale, improbable luxury, and their stunning natural surroundings — and among them perhaps none is so well-known as the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise. Two hours west of Calgary may seem an unlikely setting for a world-class luxury hotel, but this one has been an institution for decades, the likes of Douglas Fairbanks and Alfred Hitchcock gracing its halls, living the high life against the backdrop of the snow-capped Rockies, overlooking the steep majesty of the glacial lake and escaping into the wilderness at every opportunity.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Lodge at Bow Lake in Lake Louise
ld.description: Half an hour to the north of Lake Louise, the Lodge at Bow Lake feels somehow both remote and convenient — this rustic red-roofed landmark is surrounded by a vast expanse of Rocky Mountain wilderness, and is an ideal home base for a mountain-park adventure. Its log construction belies the fact that the Lodge has been substantially modernized, and its rooms are luxurious, though still rugged and unpretentious in style. The top-of-the-line Num-Ti-Jah Suite has the finest views, along with a Japanese soaking tub; all guests gather at 6:30 for a four-course set-menu dinner in the Elkhorn Dining Room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Amangiri in Lake Powell
ld.description: Our preference for quirky little independent hotels goes right out the window when the chain we’re talking about is one of Aman's caliber — which, if we’re honest, can only mean Aman itself. It’s hard to think of a less predictable setting than southern Utah for their outpost, Amangiri, but the otherworldly landscape is inspiring indeed, and serves as the ideal canvas for what is by any reasonable standard an architecturally distinguished property.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Fontainebleau Las Vegas in Las Vegas
ld.description: They’ve got Venice and ancient Egypt on the Vegas Strip, why not Miami Beach too? The Fontainebleau Las Vegas is inspired by the Floridian icon with which it shares its name, but as it’s 70 years younger and more than twice the size — to say nothing of its vast casino — it’s definitely its own beast. The accommodations are suitably lavish, and the amenities are correspondingly over-the-top, including the vast Lapis Spa, the six-acre pool deck, and the 3,800-seat theatre. Meanwhile the Fontainebleau’s multitude of restaurants features concepts from a who’s-who of well-known restaurateurs.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Las Vegas in Las Vegas
ld.description: Only in a city like Vegas could the Four Seasons' trademark elegance seem new and daring. Everyone's talking about the Vegas Renaissance. Yes, you can still get comped rooms, a six-dollar all-you-can-eat steak buffet (iceberg lettuce and Jell-O included) and sell your soul to the slots — but that's all downtown.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets 25 lbs and under are allowed. Maximum 2 pets per room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas in Las Vegas
ld.description: There aren’t many cities where a luxury hotel as relentlessly high-end as a Waldorf Astoria would feel bracingly, refreshingly understated, but the desert-bound theme park that is Las Vegas is one of them. The brand’s clean-lined modernist design and discreetly professional service is appealing enough anywhere, but here it’s a breath of life — and frankly, for a lot of guests, it will transform Vegas from deliciously, ironically kitsch to just plain delicious.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Burg in Leesburg
ld.description: An 1885 estate in Leesburg, Virginia, a town that sheltered the National Archives during the Civil War and later became a retreat for Washington D.C.'s political class. Hotel Burg opened here in 2025, and the interiors match the setting: rich textures, bespoke furnishings, fireplaces in multiple suites. The Dogwood Suite has a clawfoot soaking tub and two fireplaces; the Rooftop Suite adds a private outdoor terrace with its own fireplace above the town roofline. The Huntōn serves a hunt-inspired dinner menu most evenings. Vineyards and equestrian estates fill the surrounding Loudoun County countryside.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Manchester Hotel in Lexington KY
ld.description: The Manchester distills — pun very much intended — the quintessential Kentucky high life into one mid-century maximalist property. Every facet of the hotel feels — from the loft-style brick façade to the warm, convivial public spaces, decorated in stained wood, leather, and brass. Rooms emanate a sense of prestige with well-chosen textiles, wainscoting, and oversize headboards. The rooftop tiki bar is a hit with the locals, and doesn’t hold back on campy Sixties vibes.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Inn at Hastings Park in Lexington
ld.description: A revolution kicked off more than 200 years ago in this quiet corner of Massachusetts. The first shots of the Revolutionary War — at Lexington and Concord, as you’ll remember from history class — were fired steps from the front door of the Inn at Hastings Park. The legendary Freedom Trail, in the heart of Boston, is just 15 miles to the east. If revolutions aren’t your thing, how about transcendentalism? Henry David Thoreau’s Walden Pond is in the neighborhood. Not a history buff? This part of Massachusetts showcases New England at its best in any season. Get acquainted with its small towns, hit the local bike trail, and stock up at its nearby farms. In other words, there’s a lot to recommend the Inn at Hastings Park before we even get to the discussing the hotel itself.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Hornibrook Mansion Empress of Little Rock

ld.name: The Hornibrook Mansion Empress of Little Rock in Little Rock
ld.description: Nothing less than a large-looming, exquisitely-appointed late Victorian mansion, the Empress of Little Rock is a truly memorable boutique bed and breakfast. Originally the Hornibrook Mansion, this architectural statement rendered in Gothic Queen Anne style was the dwelling of one of Little Rock’s most successful late 19th-century saloon keepers. Opulent and octagonal, the Empress’s individually decorated rooms are joined by unique design flourishes, such as a divided stairway, a three-and-a-half-story corner tower, and a stained-glass skylight. Each takes its name from some character in the region’s history, and most feature sitting areas, while suites add jacuzzis or balconies.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Beverly Wilshire, Beverly Hills (A Four Seasons Hotel)

ld.name: Beverly Wilshire, Beverly Hills (A Four Seasons Hotel) in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Beverly Wilshire, A Four Seasons Hotel is a bona fide hospitality icon. This grand old Renaissance Revival–style edifice has presided over the end of Rodeo Drive since 1928, and is familiar not only to luxury shoppers but to cinemagoers as well, having appeared in Pretty Woman and countless other Hollywood films. Enter, though, and you’ll be anything but intimidated; the standard of service here is such that every guest immediately assumes VIP status.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Casa Del Mar  in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Casa del Mar shares something more than ownership with its sister hotel, the neighboring Shutters on the Beach — as surprising as it may sound, they’re the only two hotels in the Los Angeles area that open directly onto the beach. But while Shutters is clean-lined and contemporary, Casa del Mar is a period piece, an authentic 1920s Italianate palace that’s played host to Hollywood royalty for as long as there’s been such a thing.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Chamberlain West Hollywood in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Deep in the heart of West Hollywood, on a quiet residential street between Sunset and Santa Monica, the Chamberlain is actually quite a bit cooler than it looks. This is no backhanded compliment — in a reversal of what seems to be the standard procedure in Los Angeles, the Chamberlain presents an unassuming public face, and keeps its surprises to itself.
ld.petsAllowed: Two dogs are allowed per room (50 pounds max) for a fee of $150 per pet per stay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Chateau Marmont in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Of all the haunted hotels, the Chateau Marmont has to be the most glamorous. Located on LA’s Sunset Strip, it’s where Clark Gable and Jean Harlow got sizzling while she was on her honeymoon with another man. Howard Hughes got himself a penthouse and a pair of binoculars and spied on the girls by the pool. If you’re going to misbehave, a young William Holden was told, do it at the Marmont. And needless to say, the ghost at the Marmont is inclined to be naughty. One guest claimed it got into her bed.
ld.petsAllowed: \n The pet fee is $250 per stay.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Downtown L.A. Proper Hotel in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: In recent years L.A.’s once-overlooked downtown district has come roaring back, and its renaissance continues with the advent of the Proper Hotel Downtown L.A., a 148-room luxury boutique hotel by the team that includes star designer Kelly Wearstler among its creative minds. Like the original Proper Hotel in San Francisco, it begins with the rehabilitation of a classic building, in this case a 1926-vintage Renaissance Revival building at the corner of 11th and Broadway.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fairmont Breakers Long Beach in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The century-old Breakers in downtown Long Beach has what decorators call “good bones” — and thanks to a substantial renovation it’s once again the jewel it was always meant to be. Now doing business as Fairmont Breakers Long Beach, it’s the best of two worlds: a Spanish Revival landmark that recalls the glamour of mid-century California, and the sort of highly professional modern luxury hotel implied by the Fairmont name.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fairmont Miramar Hotel & Bungalows in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: This century-old luxury hotel has seen Santa Monica change from bohemian beach town to upscale enclave; and though it’s just a few minutes’ walk from the beach itself, it’s even closer to the mall that is Downtown Santa Monica. No matter — a stay at the Fairmont Miramar Hotel & Bungalows is what you make of it, and can be as private as you want it to be. The grounds themselves are planted with lush gardens overlooking the Pacific; the hotel’s own private beach club is accessible via a shuttle.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel 850 SVB in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Lately Los Angeles has been in the travel news for its edgy, urban offerings in Downtown and points east. But the more traditional luxury that’s particular to Hollywood’s high-end hotels has by no means gone out of style. If you’ve been to the Sunset Tower, then you’ll agree that hotelier Jeff Klein has a track record with this sort of thing, and it’s no surprise that news of his new Hotel 850 SVB West Hollywood at Beverly Hills, a residential-style luxury boutique hotel in West Hollywood, has met with much enthusiasm.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Bel-Air, Dorchester Collection in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Built in 1946 in a style that can only be described as romantic Mediterranean, the Hotel Bel-Air, with its rose-colored mission-style bungalows, is about as elite a hideaway as you can find. Hidden by bougainvillea, ficus, orange blossom, and fern, on eighteen acres right in the middle of LA’s most exclusive suburb, the grounds are mapped by terracotta passageways, and the reception area lies just beyond an arched stone bridge.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Le Petit Pali Brentwood in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Le Petit Pali Brentwood fills a gap in the Los Angeles hotel scene: in short, it’s a great place to stay in one of the city’s most stylish neighborhoods, an area that’s surprisingly short on lodging options. Brentwood is mostly residential, and Le Petit Pali offers a rare chance to live like the locals, including NBA stars and A-list actors. Like others in hotelier Avi Brosh’s California collection, the 25-room boutique hotel is a smart redesign of an old inn — in this case, a historic motor lodge on Sunset Boulevard. With four bungalow-style buildings set around a series of outdoor patios with abundant greenery, stone fountains, and string lights suspended above wooden Adirondack chairs, it’s a fashionable home away from home with space to relax indoors and out.
ld.petsAllowed: There is a one-time pet fee of $125 + taxes per stay. Dogs only. Limit 1 dog per room. 35 lbs and under. Must sign pet waiver at check-in. Pets cannot be left unattended.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: L’Ermitage Beverly Hills in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Its exterior is somewhat discreet by local standards; it’s what’s inside L’Ermitage Beverly Hills that matters. This local legend has returned to its roots as the only independent luxury hotel in town, and it remains the quintessential Hollywood insider’s hotel — and it’s designed to be at its best when you’re inside looking out. This means discretion, this means privacy, and above all, this means the intimate scale of a boutique hotel; with a little over a hundred suites, it’s not the sort of place where you’ll feel overlooked — don’t be surprised if the staff knows your name and your preferences, down to the smallest detail.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Palihouse West Hollywood in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The very first Palisociety hotel was the Palihouse Holloway, a boutique-chic extended-stay concept named for its West Hollywood address. A decade and a half and more than a few Palisociety openings later, the brand has revisited its roots, with what’s less a simple renovation and more a total replacement of its original hotel: the 95-room Palihouse West Hollywood.
ld.petsAllowed: Pet fee - $125/per stay. Dogs under 30lbs accepted via Pawlisociety Program. Limit 1 dog per room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Regent Santa Monica Beach in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: Regent Santa Monica Beach brings a new level of laid-back luxury to Ocean Avenue. Interiors reflect the coastal setting with a soft palette, breezy silhouettes, and thoughtful in-room extras like marble soaking tubs, yoga mats, and Dyson hairdryers. Floor-to-ceiling windows frame sweeping views of the Pacific, while the expansive pool deck and light-filled lobby invite guests to linger. Ideally positioned for exploring Santa Monica and beyond, with direct access to the beach path and the iconic pier just steps away.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Santa Monica Proper Hotel in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The Proper Hotels brand debuted in San Francisco with a classic building, a vibrant contemporary design by Kelly Wearstler, and high-luxury details that elevated it above typical high-end boutique fare. And for the brand’s second installment, it’s a similar story: though the Santa Monica Proper Hotel is a new build, designed by Howard Laks Architects with interiors by the very same Kelly Wearstler, it incorporates a 1920s Spanish Colonial building on Wilshire Boulevard, updating a century-old classic for the boutique-hotel era.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Shutters on the Beach in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: We’re accustomed to viewing the hospitality world through a critical lens, but every now and then a hotel lives up to the fantasy, and then some. Shutters on the Beach is exactly what you would want a Santa Monica luxury hotel to be, if you were designing it from a blank page. And the best part about it is that you don’t have to — it actually exists, and Michael S. Smith has already gone to the trouble of designing it, in a style that combines the barefoot ease of the West Coast with just a bit of Northeast elegance.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Soho House Holloway in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The original Soho House could only have been established in London, a city with a history of members’-only clubs, and a place where the film, theatre, and art worlds are packed shoulder-to-shoulder; the concept translated fairly easily to downtown Manhattan as well. And here in West Hollywood, with a bit of adaptation, is a slightly sunnier version of the Soho House concept, in the form of the 34-room Holloway House.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sunset Tower Hotel in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: In Hollywood the line between history and kitsch is so fine as to be practically non-existent. But one way or another the Sunset Tower manages to land on the right side of the line. In the latter years of the golden age this Art Deco apartment tower was home to the likes of Marilyn Monroe and Frank Sinatra; and while today the mid-century atmosphere is still in place, it’s no museum — there’s nothing faded about the newly renovated Sunset Tower’s sober, earth-toned interiors, and it’s not collectors or autograph hounds but bona fide Hollywood players who frequent its halls today.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request with a $100 non-refundable pet fee.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Aster in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The Aster is, before anything else, a private club, a much-needed oasis at the very public intersection of Hollywood and Vine. The obvious way in is to become a member — but the Aster’s 35 suites are open to overnight guests as well, and it’s perhaps no surprise that they’re up there with the finest suites in town — a bit bohemian, a bit retro, more than a bit warm and welcoming, understated in their luxury and, above all, memorable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Beverly Hills Hotel, Dorchester Collection

ld.name: The Beverly Hills Hotel, Dorchester Collection in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The Pink Palace has, in true Hollywood fashion, had some work done; nothing shocking, just a hundred-million-dollar renovation in an effort to stay competitive with a new generation. It’s a success—this place could have slid gently into self-parody, but it’s every bit as fine as when Marilyn Monroe and Yves Montand stayed here (ostensibly separately) in 1960.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: The Charlie in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: This particular corner of West Hollywood has changed a bit over the years, to say the least, but back when Charlie Chaplin owned it this jumble of English-style bungalows fit right in to the pastoral landscape. Chaplin left LA over sixty years ago, of course, and it’s a minor miracle that these houses still stand — but thanks to an enterprising hotelier, they do, in the form of the Charlie, a truly unusual boutique hotel. (We always mean that as a compliment.)

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Georgian  in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: A rare piece of Old Hollywood glamour in modern Santa Monica, the Georgian is nothing if not distinctive — this turquoise-and-gold Art Deco mini-skyscraper stands prominently on Ocean Avenue. Its history since its Thirties opening is not unbroken, but under new owners — and with the help of some skilled local designers — it’s been restored to an approximation of its former glory, and it immediately established itself as one of Santa Monica’s hippest hotels.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Maybourne Beverly Hills in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The Maybourne is just about as Beverly Hills as they come, eight floors of classic Californian luxury, paying direct homage to Hollywood’s heyday, right in the heart of the Golden Triangle. The property is the namesake of the Maybourne Hotel Group, joining Claridge’s, The Berkeley, and The Connaught, all members in good standing of the top tier of classic London luxury hotels.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Peninsula Beverly Hills in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The Peninsula Beverly Hills is almost impossibly opulent, even by Hollywood standards, a cinematically pristine Renaissance mansion of the sort that takes offense at sparing expense. A favorite of industry bigwigs, the hotel means it when it boasts of executive-level service — from the fleet of Rolls Royces and BMW's to the lavish “programmes” with celebrity stylists and gurus, this is LA at its shiniest.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Prospect Hollywood in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: The idea of Hollywood may be synonymous with glamour, but nearly a hundred years after the so-called Golden Age, the actual place is a bit more complicated. The Prospect Hollywood, however, is a return to form: a 1939 Hollywood Regency building, rescued from an advanced state of disrepair by designer Martyn Lawrence Bullard and transformed into what is, beneath its retro styling and vintage furniture, a thoroughly contemporary boutique hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Sun Rose West Hollywood in Los Angeles Area
ld.description: There’s no one location in Los Angeles that captures the appeal of the whole city, but the Sunset Strip comes close — Hollywood glamour, rock-and-roll decadence, spectacularly set against the backdrop of the hills. The Sun Rose takes up a whole block along Sunset, and it needs every square foot; the hotel contains not just 150 rooms and suites, but a spa, a handful of fine restaurants, a members’ club, a 100-seat music venue, and even a bowling alley.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Chileno Bay Resort & Residences, Auberge Collection

address.streetAddress: Carretera Transpeninsular San Jose-San Lucas Km. 15, Playa Chileno Bay

ld.name: Chileno Bay Resort & Residences, Auberge Collection in Los Cabos
ld.description: Los Cabos is pretty close to paradise already, but there are few locations that wouldn’t be improved by the addition of a top-class hotel. This is where the California-based Auberge Collection comes in. Though they’re best known for their luxury resorts in the Napa and Sonoma valleys, they’ve got history here, having operated the nearby Esperanza for almost two decades — and now, just up the road in the direction of San Jose del Cabo, Chileno Bay Resort & Residences.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: Carretera Transpeninsular Km 7, Manzana 10 Punta Ballena

ld.name: Esperanza, Auberge Collection in Los Cabos
ld.description: Esperanza is located at the tip of the Baja Peninsula, four miles outside of Cabo San Lucas, where the Pacific meets the Sea of Cortez. The setting is spectacular and the resort itself is luxurious and exclusive, the sort of place where you just might spot a vacationing Hollywood star.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Las Ventanas al Paraiso, A Rosewood Resort

ld.name: Las Ventanas al Paraiso, A Rosewood Resort in Los Cabos
ld.description: Among the first of Mexico's high-end luxury hotels is Las Ventanas al Paraíso, A Rosewood Resort. Certainly, Las Ventanas has its location to its advantage. Los Cabos has a bit of everything — lapis waters, mountains, desert, and soft sand. It also gets 350 days of sun a year.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Montage Los Cabos in Los Cabos
ld.description: The Montage resorts were once strictly a Southern California phenomenon, but they’ve since spread to the east and west; to Deer Valley, Utah and the northwest shore of Maui, respectively. And now they’re expanding to the south as well: Montage Los Cabos brings the now-familiar Montage recipe of luxe lodgings and extravagant offerings to the shores of Santa Maria Bay, between San Jose del Cabo and Cabo San Lucas, home to what might be Cabo’s finest beach.
ld.petsAllowed: Domestic pets up to 40 lbs are permitted. There is a pet fee of 65 USD per pet per stay. Pets must be kept on a leash at all times while on property and are not permitted in pool area, spa or restaurants.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: One&Only Palmilla Resort in Los Cabos
ld.description: The original Palmilla Resort, in its incarnation as a 1950s hot spot, played host to the A-listers of the day — people like Bing Crosby, Ernest Hemingway, even Dwight Eisenhower came here for a taste of the still-exotic, still-unspoiled Baja California. Today, after an $80m renovation, the Palmilla is under the wing of Butch Kerzner's One & Only group, owner and operator of other VIP resorts like Mauritius' Le Touessrok and Le Saint Géran.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: Carretera Transpeninsular Km 5, Misiones del Cabo

ld.name: The Cape, a Thompson Hotel in Los Cabos
ld.description: “The Cape, a Thompson Hotel” is the sort of name that pretty well sums the place up — if you know that the cape in question is Cabo San Lucas, and if you’re acquainted with Thompson’s brand of luxury boutique hospitality, then you more or less know what to expect. The first Thompson hotel in Mexico is blessed with a first-rate location, right on Monuments Beach, with views of the famous Arch across the bay. And the design, by the Mexico City–based architect Javier Sanchez, blends a hand-crafted local look with a bit of a SoCal modernist vibe.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Lote 8 P.º Malecon San Jose, Zona Hotelera

ld.name: Viceroy Los Cabos in Los Cabos
ld.description: Located in San José del Cabo, the quieter, more upscale cousin of Mexico’s west-coast party capital, Viceroy Los Cabos is remarkable for its architectural distinction: it’s a dramatic statement by Miguel Ángel Aragonés, a Mexican architect celebrated for his boldly unconventional designs. This is one of the most aggressively stylish of the Viceroy hotels: sleek and otherworldly, all clean lines, cantilevers, deep shadows and stark white cubes — “floating boxes,” to borrow the architect’s apt phrase — mirrored in still blue reflecting pools.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal in Los Cabos
ld.description: To get to the Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal, you must pass through a tunnel blasted through the mountains that abut the beach — an unconventional approach, and the first of many reminders that this isn’t your crazy younger cousin’s spring-break Cabo. Here, you’ll get foot rubs and cool treats by the pool, rather than thumping bass and body shots — or, for privacy, you can hang out in your very own plunge pool, with its views of the Pacific Ocean. The villas and casitas come with even more goodies, including fire pits and private breakfasts, prepared by your own majordomo. For those of you keeping track, the majordomo is in addition to the personal assistant.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Zadun Los Cabos, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve

ld.name: Zadun Los Cabos, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve in Los Cabos
ld.description: Not every Ritz-Carlton is a neoclassical palace — Zadún, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, like the other Reserves, takes its cues from its setting: in this case San Jose del Cabo, on Mexico’s Baja California coast. The architecture is decidedly modern, while the décor in the rooms, suites, and villas incorporates local design motifs in a tasteful way, and everywhere you’re treated to the typically luxe Ritz-Carlton experience, which means top-notch comforts and service. The Sensei spa, naturally, does brisk business, and the restaurants and bars are carefully tailored to Los Cabos’ local culinary culture, albeit with a high-end sheen.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Cataloochee Ranch in Maggie Valley
ld.description: It’s not easy to find a more spectacular corner of the Appalachians than this 825-acre expanse at the edge of the Great Smoky Mountains National Park. And while Cataloochee Ranch has been in operation for close to a century, it’s only in recent years that it’s been upgraded to its current high level of luxury. The property remains crisscrossed with miles of trails for hiking and horseback riding, but it’s also home to a restaurant, Switchback, that serves High Country classics reimagined by a French-trained chef.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Faraway Martha's Vineyard in Martha's Vineyard
ld.description: Edgartown, Massachusetts, on the island of Martha’s Vineyard, is among the most historic places in the United States. Once home to the American whaling industry, it’s now one of the leisure capitals of the Northeast, and many old sea captains’ stately homes have been transformed into guest houses and hotels. Faraway Martha’s Vineyard comprises six of them; and while, with nearly two centuries in business under one name or another, it’s one of the oldest hotels in the country, its new owners have updated it for the 21st century, even as they’ve preserved the atmosphere that makes it so unique.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hob Knob in Martha's Vineyard
ld.description: Martha’s Vineyard is the kind of destination that can feel a bit closed off to outsiders. It’s a place that’s perhaps better known for vacation homes and vacation estates than it is for hotels. But there are some gems to be found, among them Hob Knob, a charming 19th-century house in Edgartown that’s been converted into a small and intimate 17-room boutique-style hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed in specific rooms only (Standard King and Private Suite only).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Nobnocket Boutique Inn in Martha's Vineyard
ld.description: Names like Nobnocket are the surest sign you’re in New England, and the Nobnocket Boutique Inn isn’t about to let you forget it. Located on Martha’s Vineyard, a short walk uphill from the dock on a on a bluff above Vineyard Haven, this 1908 Arts & Crafts-style house was once the home of the island’s doctor. The new owners overhauled the place, knocking down walls to create open living areas, polishing the hardwood floors, installing large picture windows to maximize the sweeping garden views. Floral wallpaper and bric-a-brac, be gone: these days, the Nobnocket is practically a showcase of modern design and art, featuring works by the likes of Marcel Wanders and Philippe Starck.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Cerrada del Museo de la Tortuga No. 1, Playa Mazunte

ld.name: Zoa Hotel in Mazunte
ld.description: While parts of Mexico are famously overdeveloped, the Pacific coastline of Oaxaca is not among them. This stretch of south-facing beach, spanning the villages of Mazunte and San Agustinillo, is spectacular, and the towns are in that sweet spot: lively but not crowded, off-the-radar but not impossible to reach. And while the beginnings of a luxury travel scene are present, they’re tasteful and restrained — a description that suits Zoa perfectly.
ld.petsAllowed: \n The hotel is pet friendly, but only in the following room types: Double Suite, Deluxe Suite, Junior Suite, Terrace Suite and the Residential Suite.
