award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Lodge at Primland, Auberge Collection

ld.name: The Lodge at Primland, Auberge Collection in Meadows of Dan
ld.description: There are country retreats, and there’s The Lodge at Primland. Not only is the hotel surrounded by verdant woodland and Virginia’s Blue Ridge Mountains, but it also sits on its own 12,000-acre estate to fully immerse guests in nature. Most of the rooms are housed in the main lodge, which offers easy access to the majority of the facilities, but for more privacy there’s the option of the chalet-style Pinnacle suites, the cozy Fairway cottages, or the chance to live out childhood dreams by spending the night in the Tree Houses, which sit high up in the treetops with views across the woodland and the Dan River Gorge.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: ARRIVE Memphis in Memphis
ld.description: Palisociety’s Arrive hotels are all different, carefully tailored to their settings in some of America’s most unique neighborhoods. But they share plenty as well: all are vibrant and eclectic in their design sense, and all include dining and drinking venues that connect them to the local flavors and traditions. Arrive Memphis begins with a lovely old industrial building on South Main, in the city’s Arts District, close to Beale Street and Downtown Memphis.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Decu Downtown in Mérida
ld.description: Mérida, the capital of the state of Yucatán, is relatively under-traveled compared to the peninsula’s famous coastal destinations, but the White City is well worth a visit — especially with hotels like the stunning Decu Downtown as a part of the package. The location, next to the cathedral in the heart of the city center, is as central as the name implies, though the inside-out compound-like construction means the experience is a remarkably tranquil one. As does the scale: a mere eight suites.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Carretera Seye - Acancéh, Supermanzana Tablaje Catastral 3096

ld.name: Galopina in Mérida
ld.description: There’s much more to the Yucatán than the Caribbean resort towns. In the inland countryside near Mérida, surrounded by the jungle landscapes of the Cenotes Rings State Reserve, is Galopina, a five-room escape whose architectural distinction and residential atmosphere make it quite unlike anything else in the region.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel CIGNO in Mérida
ld.description: Right in the center of the city of Mérida a 19th-century mansion has been put to new use as a luxury boutique hotel whose design pays the maximum possible tribute to local tradition. Hotel CIGNO is not a strictly historically correct recreation of the grand Yucatecan residential style, but a contemporary interpretation, full of details inspired by both the colonial and indigenous traditions.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Sevilla in Mérida
ld.description: In Mérida’s historic center, Hotel Sevilla reimagines a 16th-century colonial villa with noticeable contrasts: weathered stone walls and arches preserved as ruins sit alongside clean concrete insertions and modern interiors. Its 21 rooms, some with soaring ceilings, are arranged around leafy courtyards where sub-tropical plants frame shaded terraces and a serene pool. The atmosphere balances raw history with a minimalist sensibility, from the spa to the restaurant and bar. Steps from Mérida Cathedral and a short drive from Paseo de Montejo, the hotel places Yucatán’s past and present close at hand.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: 298 C C. 62, C 62 298C entre 33A y 33 Mérida, México

ld.name: Hotel Sureño in Mérida
ld.description: Everyone’s aware of Cancún’s megaresorts and Tulum’s bohemian-chic beachfront hotels; fewer visitors to the Yucatán Peninsula consider staying in the state capital of Mérida. But the city is full of colonial buildings turned into appealing modern hotels, like Hotel Sureño, which recently opened in the historic center.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: TreeHouse Boutique Hotel in Mérida
ld.description: The capital of the Mexican state of Yucatán is Mérida, and if all you know about the Yucatán peninsula is the Caribbean coast, you’re in for a surprise: a stunning colonial city, established nearly 500 years ago, right on top of an existing Maya one. The result, needless to say, is a place that’s chock full of historical resonance, and the same can be said for the astonishingly lovely (and adults-only!) Treehouse Boutique Hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Pedregal 24 , Colonia Molino Del Rey Alcaldia Miguel Hidalgo

ld.name: Alexander in Mexico City
ld.description: Torre Virreyes, one of the last works of the celebrated architect Teodoro González de León, looks like the tallest building in Mexico City. It isn’t; in fact it’s not even close. But looming high over the Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the Americas, this trapezoid-shaped skyscraper — home to the Alexander Hotel — dwarfs everything around it.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Brick Hotel in Mexico City
ld.description: The upscale residential neighborhood of Roma is home to more than a few century-old mansions, but this one is unique — built from bricks shipped over from England, it was the custom-built residence for the head of the Bank of London & Mexico. It was later owned by one of Mexico’s presidents, and today, after a thorough but sensitive renovation, it’s one of Mexico City’s finest small luxury hotels.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Campos Polanco in Mexico City
ld.description: The vast megalopolis that is Mexico City is no stranger to luxe little enclaves, but this one, even by local standards, is remarkable. An unusual Art Deco building in one of the capital’s poshest districts is now home to Campos Polanco, a 12-suite luxury boutique hotel that aims for nothing less than an authentic residential experience — albeit an extremely high-end one. Its setting is unique, facing the green expanse of the Garden of the Republic of Lebanon. And its design is striking, the result of an all-star team of local creative talent.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed, charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Casa Polanco in Mexico City
ld.description: Casa Polanco is an understated name, but it says all it needs to say. This small and intimate boutique hotel is set in one of Mexico City’s poshest neighborhoods, and it occupies what was once a private house — two of them, actually, a Forties Neocolonial mansion and the unmistakably modernist addition next door. Together they contain just 19 rooms and suites, all unique and all decorated in a style that’s unmistakably luxe but maximally tasteful: soothing neutrals, sleek design furniture, richly figured marble bathrooms, and a curated collection of objects and décor from a multitude of eras.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Casona Roma Norte in Mexico City
ld.description: It’s not easy to stand out in Mexico City’s hippest neighborhood, but Casona Roma Norte is a modern classic that’s as striking from the street as it is inside. This rose-pink Belle Époque mansion dates back to the 1920s, and though its grand interiors have been stripped back and outfitted with minimalist décor and modern art, the place still radiates old-world magic.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Colima 71 - Casa de Arte Hotel in Mexico City
ld.description: Not only is Mexico City one of the cultural capitals of the Western Hemisphere, it’s long been a showcase for inventive homegrown boutique hotels. And a fine example of both of these tendencies is Colima 71 Art Community Hotel, a 16-room boutique hotel in Roma Norte, in a building designed by the celebrated local architect Alberto Kalach, featuring interior design by the local studios Nomah and Karla Celerio Interiorismo.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: 480-2 Cam. a Sta. Teresa, Col. Del Bosque, Tlalpan

ld.name: Hacienda Peña Pobre in Mexico City
ld.description: There are few cities in the world quite as overwhelming as Mexico City, but even here there are green spaces to be found, if you know where to look. Hacienda Peña Pobre lies not in the ultra-urban heart of the city but near its southern edge; more importantly, it’s set just yards from the Bosque de Tlalpan, a sizable urban forest and a popular destination for locals in need of some greenery.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are welcome, with an additional cost of 20 USD + taxes per night.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Ignacia Guest House in Mexico City
ld.description: Some of the most impressive hotels come bearing humble names. Ignacia Guest House certainly doesn’t sound like a big deal, but it’s no ordinary guest house. Set in the upscale Colonia Roma, the mansion that’s stood on this site since 1913 was already impressive enough. Now, thanks to an ultra-modern expansion by architect Fermín Espinosa and designer Andrés Gutiérrez, it’s the kind of house that gets written about in architecture magazines — and for five rooms’ worth of guests, it’s one of the most unique hotel experiences in Mexico City.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: La Valise Mexico City in Mexico City
ld.description: It’s always cool to be contrary — especially in the world of cutting-edge boutique hotels. Let the big chains scramble to outdo each other with bigger spas and better restaurants, sparkling fitness centers and Olympic-sized infinity pools, more pillows on the menu, more of everything. An achingly hip little hotel like La Valise in Mexico City doesn’t need any of that. In fact, the 8-suite property, located above a shop in a 1920s townhouse in the happening Roma neighborhood, makes a virtue of its small size.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Maison Celeste in Mexico City
ld.description: Colonial charm meets retro chic at Maison Celeste, an art-focused boutique hotel and gallery in Mexico City’s hip Roma Norte neighborhood. Many of the mansion’s historic details have been carefully preserved, from the original hardwood flooring and vaulted ceilings to the elegant crown moldings and colorful stained glass panels. But instead of living rooms or lounges, the minimalist ground-level rooms house permanent and rotating exhibitions, pop-up shops, and stylish event spaces. There’s a lot of action here, especially during festivals like Mexico City Art Week, and the rooms upstairs are often booked well in advance.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Nima Local House Hotel & Spa in Mexico City
ld.description: There’s something deliciously ironic about the fact that the biggest city in North America is home to some of the world’s finest small hotels. And by small, we really do mean small: Nima Local House Hotel, with just four rooms, is probably more house than hotel, and, to borrow a catch phrase, it’s the perfect way to live like a local in the Mexican capital’s charming and stylish Roma district.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: OCTAVIA CASA in Mexico City
ld.description: If Mexico City is a whirlwind of colors, sounds, and flavors, Octavia Casa is a calm refuge in which to recover from the sensory overload. Located in Condesa, one of the city’s hippest neighborhoods, this boutique hotel is the passion project of Mexican designer Roberta Maceda, who enlisted architect Pablo Pérez Palacios to create a space in the same spirit as her modern women’s clothing line. The result is stylish yet refreshingly down-to-earth; its interiors are light-filled and minimalist, almost ethereal, characterized by clean, simple lines and natural materials.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pug Seal Allan Poe in Mexico City
ld.description: Located in the hip Mexico City neighborhood of Polanco, Pug Seal Allan Poe has the looks of an intimate design hotel but all the grandeur of a private mansion thanks to its setting in a rather regal 1940s home, set behind wrought-iron gates on an attractive residential block. A double staircase, original stained glass and decorative wall moldings lead to the 20 rooms where the contrasting aesthetic is clean and modern: think marble and glass, modular sofas, sixties-style side tables, walls painted in bold hues, and bathrooms lined with gorgeous tile (and featuring free-standing tubs, if you’re in a suite.) But there’s a whimsical edge to these interiors, one that’s inspired by nature — fitting, given the Pug Seal Allan Poe’s proximity to the urban oasis of Chapultepec Park. Butterflies and insects dot the patterned wallpaper, tree branch sculptures and stag head busts are mounted above beds, even the color palette of beige, aquamarine, and slate calls to mind natural elements from sand and stone to sea and sky.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pug Seal Anatole France in Mexico City
ld.description: Like its sister Pug Seal Allan Poe, Pug Seal Anatole France is also housed in a 1940s private mansion in an upscale part of Polanco, but also like its sibling, it manages to stand out as a truly one-of-a-kind boutique hotel. With 26 suites it’s larger than the other Pug Seals, but it never loses that residential atmosphere — provided, of course, you’re capable of feeling at home in one of the most eclectic residences you’ve ever seen. In the public spaces original features such as arched windows, wrought iron staircases and ornate wall moldings have been paired with equally extravagant accessories such as chandeliers and a grand piano, whilst eclectic guest rooms come dressed in eye-popping colors and a mix of bold stripes and prints. Some have balconies or terraces, some have bathtubs, one even has an outdoor jacuzzi. Safe to say it’s a stay you won’t soon forget.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Av. Paseo de la Reforma 297, Cuauhtémoc

ld.name: Sofitel Mexico City Reforma in Mexico City
ld.description: The distinctive high-rise tower that contains the Sofitel Mexico City Reforma stretches some 40 floors above the city, granting its occupants spectacular views of the Paseo de la Reforma and the rest of this sprawling city. In typical Sofitel style it’s unabashed about its Parisian influence, though it’s no carbon copy of the City of Light — it’s lovingly tailored to its Mexico City setting, and features roughly equal parts New World vigor and Old World glamour.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Wild Oscar in Mexico City
ld.description: Polanco has accrued quite a bit of cultural capital over the decades, initially as a hub for Mexico City’s intelligentsia, then as a frontier for boutique development, and increasingly these days as a hunting ground for club-hoppers and paparazzi. The next step is the Wild Oscar: something a little more businesslike, but no less stylish, globalized exec-chic fluidly transitioning between a series of loose- (or no-) tie environments.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Monte Himalaya 105, Lomas de Chapultepec, Miguel Hidalgo

ld.name: UMA Casa in Mexico City
ld.description: There’s only one hotel in the neighborhood of Lomas de Chapultepec, and fittingly for this upscale residential district, it feels less like a hotel and more like the stylish home of a worldly Mexican friend. Framed by abundant greenery on a quiet block, UMA Casa is a design-forward boutique guesthouse with nine individually decorated suites, all named for native fruits and herbs.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Volga in Mexico City
ld.description: It’s named for the road it’s on, which is in turn named for the most famous river in Russia, and is one block over from the Paseo de la Reforma. And if there’s something a bit Eastern Bloc about this concrete tower, it’s probably down to the associations of Brutalism, or maybe the Tarkovsky-like tableau of its minimalist interior atrium garden. But Volga, the hotel, is a pure expression of today’s Mexico City — a city that’s as cosmopolitan as it is unique.
ld.petsAllowed: Pet frienfly.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: 1 Hotel South Beach in Miami
ld.description: There was a time when the eco-friendly ethos and recycled/reclaimed décor on display at 1 Hotels South Beach would have been a tough sell in ultra-decadent Miami. But as jetsetters increasingly trade conspicuous consumption for conscious consumption, hedonism has taken a wholesome, almost virtuous turn. All of which is to say: the 1 Hotels approach suits modern Miami Beach just fine.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Betsy - South Beach in Miami
ld.description: In Miami the flash hotels arms race has escalated to a point where a hotel like the Betsy — South Beach is almost shocking in its restraint. We’re almost tempted to call it conservative, but with a disclaimer: the Betsy’s pre-deco style means it’s got a personality all its own, and can’t help but stand out from the poolside fashion shoots and celebrity-thronged nightclubs of its more attention-starved neighbors.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Faena Hotel Miami Beach in Miami
ld.description: Alan Faena doesn’t do things halfway. The pioneering Argentinian hotelier didn’t just open a hotel in Buenos Aires — he transformed a piece of abandoned waterfront real estate into a glamorous urban destination, turning a once-derelict neighborhood into a thriving arts district. And now he’s brought the Faena brand to Miami Beach. It’s a place that, of course, doesn’t require the same kind of vision or transformation. This part of Miami is well-developed, to say the least. But in some ways the Faena Hotel Miami Beach is an even more ambitious project. That’s because Faena, just as he did in Buenos Aires, isn’t just opening a hotel: he’s taking over the neighborhood.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Hotel at The Surf Club

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel at The Surf Club in Miami
ld.description: Just a few miles up the road from Miami Beach proper, in the upscale enclave of Surfside, is the legendary Surf Club, an ornate Jazz Age gem whose doors first opened in 1930. Today the original club remains, augmented by modern structures containing residences and the Four Seasons Hotel — a typically luxe and uncommonly stylish luxury hotel, complete with beachside cabanas and a lavish spa, from the venerable hospitality brand. The atmosphere is insular, more luxe hideaway than social nexus, though the restaurants, the Italian-flavored Lido Restaurant and Terrace and Thomas Keller’s Surf Club Restaurant, are destinations unto themselves.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Greystone in Miami
ld.description: The historic 1930s Art Deco façade of the Hotel Greystone looks brand new — and after a vast renovation, what’s inside looks more or less like the last word in contemporary South Beach boutique luxury. The location, right on Collins Avenue, is just about as central as it gets, but the Greystone’s interiors offer immediate relief from the bustle outside; in the lobby, soothing cream tones dominate, accented by living greenery and subtle Deco reverberations.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Up to two pets (cats and dogs)  are welcome for a fee of $100 per pet, per stay. A portion of this fee will be donated to our local no-kill pet shelter.  Pets must be up to date on all vaccinations and pets must be on a leash or in a carrier if they’re outside the guest room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mayfair House Hotel & Garden in Miami
ld.description: Mayfair House Hotel & Garden offers a different perspective on a familiar destination. It’s set neither in glitzy Miami Beach nor in a Downtown Miami skyscraper but in Coconut Grove, the upscale village-like arts and entertainment district along the coast a few minutes to the southwest of downtown. The original Mayfair is an uncommonly stylish 1980s icon by architect Kenneth Treister, and it’s been reverently updated by Goodrich NYC into the hotel you see today: the Mayfair House Hotel & Garden.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mr. C Miami Coconut Grove in Miami
ld.description: The C in Mr. C stands for Cipriani, the famous family of restaurateurs. To their restaurant in Downtown Miami you can add Mr. C Miami Coconut Grove, on Biscayne Bay just to the south of the city proper. Here, a bridge or two from the painstakingly preserved history of Miami Beach, there’s room for something different, and Mr. C Miami – Coconut Grove is certainly that.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Moore in Miami
ld.description: Originally built in 1921 as a neoclassical furniture showroom, The Moore has long been part of Miami’s design DNA. Reimagined as a boutique hotel with serious creative pedigree, its 13 suites play with texture and tone: plaster walls, curved wood, clay and rattan. Below, a Zaha Hadid installation anchors the atrium, while art galleries, concept dining, and a private club animate the rest of the building. It is a discreet, design-forward stay in one of Miami’s most dynamic neighborhoods.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Setai Miami Beach in Miami
ld.description: Miami Beach is a town that’s not exactly hurting for over-the-top luxury accommodations, but the Setai manages to set itself apart by being even more over-the-top than the competition.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Minneapolis in Minneapolis
ld.description: Make no mistake: Four Seasons Hotel Minneapolis is a skyline-defining high rise in the beating heart of a booming Midwestern metropolis. You’ll get a restful night, but you’ll also get thrill-seeking locals in a buzzing lobby scene, especially because it opens onto the Skyway. Height, clearly, is the name of the game — the better to take in the Mississippi or a cosmopolitan sunset, depending on the room. That electricity hits best early in the morning or late at night, when the light through floor-to-ceiling windows works its magic against your soothingly open room layout. Smart of them to eschew sharp edges; it radiates a Deco vibe in keeping with the birth of the skyscraper.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets 35 lbs and under are allowed. Maximum 2 pets per room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: ULUM Moab in Moab
ld.description: Upscale tented camps are one thing, but ULUM Moab is on another level — this is unmistakably a full-on resort experience. The lobby is a permanent brick-and-mortar structure, and each unit is separated from its neighbors by a considerable distance, with plenty of interior space for lounging, as well as comforts you’d normally expect to find only in a proper luxury hotel, including Parachute linens, West Elm furniture, and rain showers stocked with Aēsop bath products.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Montreal in Montreal
ld.description: In just a few short years the once-staid Four Seasons hotel group undertook a significant style makeover, and among the fruits of this effort is the Four Seasons Hotel Montreal. It occupies a modern tower, clad in dark glass, which stands above downtown Montreal’s Golden Square Mile, in the heart of the modern city center. And inside it’s everything you’d expect from a first-class luxury hotel: lavish accommodations, an extravagant Guerlain spa, and a food and beverage program led by celebrity chef Marcus Samuelsson.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets up to 25 pounds are allowed on request. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hôtel Place d’Armes in Montreal
ld.description: Hôtel Place d'Armes is a new addition to the historic district of Old Montréal, a modern boutique hotel within the renovated nineteenth-century Great Scottish Life Insurance building, and an ideal vantage point from which to witness the resurgence of this once-neglected neighborhood.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hôtel William Gray in Montreal
ld.description: There’s no place in North America with more historic character than Old Montreal — which means that a design hotel like the William Gray, made from a pair of 18th-century heritage buildings and a contemporary addition, gets maximum impact from its stylistic contrast. Once you’re inside the modern section, with its soaring glass atrium, it’s clear that you’re in for a 21st-century luxury-boutique experience.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Le Mount Stephen in Montreal
ld.description: Montréal’s hotel scene is unique in North America, largely because of the high concentration of historical atmosphere in Vieux Montréal, the city’s old quarter. But there’s plenty of personality, architectural and otherwise, to be found elsewhere around town. The so-called Golden Square Mile is the historic commercial district, and among its regal old edifices is a stunning neo-Renaissance structure that was originally the home of one the city’s movers and shakers, Lord George Stephen — and it’s for him that the structure, in its new guise as a luxury hotel, is named today: Le Mount Stephen Hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Montreal in Montreal
ld.description: In a city with so many great independent hotels, it’s practically a subversive gesture to stay in a Ritz-Carlton. This hotel, though, like Montréal itself, is steeped in history — opened in 1912, the Ritz-Carlton has played host to everyone from Douglas Fairbanks to John Travolta. It’s not solely an exercise in old-world grandeur, however, as a tasteful modern glass addition expands one side of the historic building.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Brant in Nantucket
ld.description: Discreetly hidden within a trio of 17th-century-style houses in Nantucket’s Brant Point is one of the island’s finest hotels: The Brant. It’s a member of the Provincetown-based Salt Hotels family, and under their guidance it’s been given a chic contemporary-classic look, foregoing the typical whaling-captain inspiration in favor of something more agriculturally inspired. Meanwhile it’s set in one of Nantucket’s most desirable corners, a short walk from the port and the town’s main drag, but just quiet enough for a bit of privacy.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed for a non-refundable $100 fee per pet, per stay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Wauwinet in Nantucket
ld.description: The Wauwinet Inn is remarkable for how near it gets to the Platonic ideal of the perfect Nantucket holiday, an ideal whose earthly incarnations are all too likely to be spoiled by the omnipresent signs of mass market tourism.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Auberge du Soleil, Auberge Collection in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: The original Napa Valley luxury boutique hotel, Auberge du Soleil, three decades on, is still going strong — so strong that, for many repeat guests, there simply isn’t anywhere else. They come for the setting, with views over endless vineyards and olive groves; they come for the hotel, which is effortlessly, unpretentiously luxurious; and they come, most of all, for the restaurant, which stands out as something special even in Napa Valley, a region that’s arguably America’s culinary capital.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Bardessono in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: A decade or two ago, Napa Valley was the place to go for a little slice of Renaissance Tuscany. It made sense at the time, with the California wine industry really hitting its stride, for the architecture to aspire toward a classic European sort of gravity. These days, however, Napa is ground zero for a new green building movement, and its hotels are leading the way — no doubt something greener will come along, but at the time of its opening, Bardessono was pretty much as sustainable as it gets.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Napa Valley in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: The Four Seasons Resort Napa Valley isn’t just in the wine country, it’s set on the grounds of a working winery on the fringe of Calistoga, its 85 rooms and suites divided among several low-slung buildings scattered amid oak trees and vineyards. The accommodations are typically luxe, and the style is modernist with a NorCal farmhouse accent. There’s an expansive spa with an outdoor garden and an adults-only swimming pool, and bikes are available for exploring the countryside. Auro, the hotel’s fine dining restaurant, has been recognized with one MICHELIN Star.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Up to 2 pets (70 pounds combined) are allowed per room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Le Petit Pali St Helena in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: In terms of atmosphere, a quiet lane on the fringes of the Napa Valley town of St. Helena is a long way from Los Angeles, where the Palihotels brand was born. But the quirky European-accented charm of Le Petit Pali St. Helena is a perfect fit for the California wine country — and this setting affords the Petit Pali concept some space to expand to a more resort-like experience.
ld.petsAllowed: There is a one-time pet fee of $125 + taxes per stay. Dogs only. Limit 1 dog per room. 35 lbs and under. Must sign pet waiver at check-in. Pets cannot be left unattended.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Meadowood Napa Valley in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: Several towns in California’s Napa and Sonoma Valleys have a legitimate claim on the title of America’s culinary capital, and St. Helena, home of the West Coast branch of the Culinary Institute of America, is a strong contender. These days it’s also home to one of the California wine country’s most rarefied — and wine-obsessed — hotels. Meadowood Napa Valley has been a local institution for half a century, but far from showing its age, today it remains an absolutely first-rate luxury resort.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Milliken Creek Inn in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: Until recently, the city of Napa was more a rest stop on the way to its eponymous valley. But the past decade has witnessed a flowering of culinary creativity, and the hoteliers have followed suit — it's only in this new Napa that a place like the Milliken Creek Inn could exist.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Montage Healdsburg in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: Where California’s previous generation of wine-country luxury resorts went in for Tuscan or Loire Valley homages, the 2021-vintage Montage Healdsburg is contemporary — and Californian — to the core. It’s set just a few minutes’ drive to the north of Healdsburg proper, amid 250 acres of vineyards and woodland, and its low-slung mid-century modernist–inspired buildings look out over the Sonoma landscape through vast sheets of glass.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: North Block  in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: Yountville, California has what might be the highest concentration of fine restaurants per square mile anywhere in North America; a boutique hotel in this Napa Valley town is virtually guaranteed to combine a strong culinary foundation with a well-thought-out wine program and a wellness-focused approach to luxury. So it is with North Block — the specific keys to its appeal, as always, are in the details.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Rancho Caymus Inn in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: California’s wine country is full of architectural homages to Europe, and this one, built in the 1980s by salt heiress Mary Tilden Morton, is a hacienda-style tribute to the Spanish countryside, built from timber reclaimed from a 19th-century barn, long before that sort of thing became a staple of green construction. It’s also modestly sized, by the standards of villas built by heiresses — with the result that now, in its current life as a luxury boutique hotel, the Rancho Caymus Inn remains somewhat intimate, weighing in at a mere 26 rooms and suites.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: SingleThread Inn in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: Don’t be fooled by the small scale of this downtown Healdsburg hotel — though it weighs in at a mere five rooms and suites, SingleThread Inn offers what might be one of the most luxurious experiences in California. It’s the work of the Los Angeles–born chef Kyle Connaughton, who has worked in celebrated kitchens in Japan and the UK, and his wife Katina, who operates the affiliated SingleThread Farm. The accommodations are anything but an afterthought, with their modern-classic aesthetic and their top-shelf comforts, not to mention their extravagant daily breakfast. But the main attraction is the Japanese-accented SingleThread Restaurant, where Inn guests enjoy preferential booking — advance planning still required.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Solage, Auberge Collection in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: It’s incredible that in 21st-century California a wine-country resort is still half-expected to look like something from 18th-century Tuscany. So it’s to Auberge Collections’ credit that Solage calls on that most Californian of idioms: the bungalow. For though the word itself may come from India, there’s no clearer expression of Napa Valley’s rustic agricultural history than a home-grown architectural style.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Stanly Ranch, Auberge Collection in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: The Auberge Collection now spans a continent, but its roots are in the California wine country — and it’s to these roots that Stanly Ranch returns. True to the name, it’s set on a 712-acre ranch, and on the grounds you’ll find not only the brand’s typically lavish rooms, suites, and villas, but also a truly vast spa complex offering a state-of-the-art wellness program. The look of the accommodations is ranch-inspired but as tasteful as you’d expect; they feel tailored to the place, but without a hint of kitsch. Among the restaurants is Bear, focused on Napa Valley ingredients (and wines).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Cottages at Little Saint in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: California’s wine country has plenty of luxury lodging, but precious little along the lines of the Cottages at Little Saint. Healdsburg’s Little Saint is itself unique, a restaurant, café, bar and events venue that hosts astonishingly high-quality touring acts in its intimate performance space. Against that backdrop, the Cottages are easy enough to understand: four small houses transformed by the designer Ken Fulk into spaces that are both comfortable and creatively inspiring.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Francis House in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: It’s hard to believe that the Francis House, a château-style Napa Valley gem, sat abandoned for half a century. Once a prominent merchant's house and later a hospital — some of Calistoga’s living residents were born here — the place was boarded up and graffiti-covered until the current owners discovered the property and transformed it into an elegant boutique hotel in 2018. All of the building’s interior was unsalvageable, but its original stone walls were beautifully restored making it a stand out feature of the hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Madrona in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: The Madrona may be new, but the Mansion, the hotel’s ornate centerpiece, certainly isn’t — this 1881 mansion was built in Aesthetic Movement style, and stands in stark contrast to the Tuscan and Provençal pretensions of so many other wine-country hotels. It’s set on the west side of Healdsburg, just across Dry Creek from the town center, and its extravagant silhouette isn’t the only surprise for arriving guests; the interiors, by co-owner and designer Jay Jeffers, are eclectic, incorporating period elements as well as modern interventions, a very fine art collection, and a boatload of antiques and curios collected during several lifetimes’ worth of travels.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are welcome for an additional fee of $150 per stay.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Stavrand in Napa / Sonoma Valleys
ld.description: From the outside the Stavrand is quaint almost beyond belief, a Twenties landmark in the storybook locale of Guerneville, California. Inside, though, the fruits of a 2021 renovation are apparent: without sacrificing its historical charm, the Stavrand’s architects have brought it subtly up to date, and the result is a warm, bohemian, slightly utopian vision of Californian life. The original inn was well known for its restaurant, and the Stavrand aims to keep the tradition alive; a quartet of chefs showcase the finest local produce from this remarkably bountiful region.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: 1 Hotel Nashville in Nashville
ld.description: For evidence that Nashville’s hotel scene has grown up fast, look no further. 1 Hotel Nashville follows on the heels of its siblings in New York, Miami, and Los Angeles, and like its sisters, it’s a high-luxury, high-design, ultra-sustainable hospitality experience. The rooms and suites are stylish in a laid-back way, with surfaces in touchably organic materials; the views of downtown Nashville are impressive, and some units come with outdoor terraces. There’s a Bamford spa and a thorough fitness program, and the public spaces include a farm-to-table restaurant, a casual café, and a rooftop cocktail bar and lounge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Nashville in Nashville
ld.description: In downtown Nashville’s SoBro district, Four Seasons claims a front-row seat to the Cumberland River and the city’s most iconic venues. The mood inside is upscale but never too formal, guests arrive in tailored suits or rhinestone boots, weaving through a lobby scented by Mimo’s open kitchen. Rooms are sunlit and sophisticated, with subtle design cues that reference the city’s musical soul: warm woods, soft curves, and a rhythm to the layout itself. With a rooftop pool, serene spa, and seamless service, it’s a stay that hits all the right notes without missing a beat.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pet Policy: Pet must be fully trained and appropriately restrained by the guest. Pet must comply with local legislation requirements. Pet must be kept on a leash when in the hotel or on hotel property unless it is in the guest's room. Pets must not be left unattended. If a guest requires a pet-sitter or pet supplies, they should contact the concierge with advance notice. Pets are not allowed in any food and beverage outlets, health club, and pool areas of the hotel. This exclusion does not apply to guide dogs. Guests are responsible for cleaning up after their pet on hotel property and in the neighborhood. Any disturbances such as barking must be curtailed to ensure other guests are not inconvenienced. Guests must contact the housekeeping department to arrange for a convenient time for servicing their room.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Soho House Nashville in Nashville
ld.description: Born in London, refined in New York, and now expanding across the world, the Soho House concept is a modern twist on the classic London members’ club — instead of Victorian gentlemen it caters to men and women from all walks of life, with a particular preference for the glamorous creative industries. In Nashville, of course, that means the music world — not only is Music City full of clubs and live venues, it’s full of musicians and recording professionals as well.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Southall Farm and Inn in Nashville
ld.description: Nashville is already home to some first-class urban hotels, but in Southall Farm & Inn it’s finally got a country escape to match. 25 miles to the south, on 325 acres of land just outside of the Middle Tennessee city of Franklin, this modern-rustic getaway is not just a lodging, but a working farm as well — lending a farm-to-table aspect to the Inn’s painstakingly local restaurant. The rooms, suites, and cottages vary in size and layout, but all are a handsome mix of modern style and retro playfulness; comfort is assured, both in-room and in Southall’s substantial spa.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Hermitage Hotel in Nashville
ld.description: When the Hermitage Hotel opened in the heart of downtown Nashville in 1910, its rooms were billed at “$2 and up,” a statement which is technically still true today, at least the “up” part. Back then, two dollars is what you could expect to pay for the finest of hotels, at least in this town, admittedly a bit cheaper than New York or Chicago.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Carversville Inn in New Hope
ld.description: An hour outside of Philadelphia and the city slowly gives way to the countryside of Bucks County, Pennsylvania. Here you’ll find the landmark Carversville Inn, an 1813 tavern that was the first one in town, back when Carversville was called Milton (long story). And if the Carversville Inn had simply been preserved for two centuries and change, that would be interesting enough — but in fact it’s been transformed into a stylish contemporary boutique hotel, one that combines historical influence with theatrical modern-retro décor.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Columns in New Orleans
ld.description: This late 19th-century Italianate villa is named for its most distinctive architectural feature. Columns was built in 1883 as a private residence for a tobacco merchant, before serving as a wartime boardinghouse and then, in the Fifties, a hotel. Today it belongs to the owner of the Drifter Hotel, but it’s a very different vibe from the Drifter’s mid-century motel aesthetic; after a thorough renovation it’s a Victorian fantasy world, as ornate and colorful as any hotel in town.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel New Orleans in New Orleans
ld.description: New Orleans is legendary for its rhythmic beat. This Southern city knows how to have a good time—at all times. So where do you stay when you want fun along with a little peace and quiet? Enter the Four Seasons. Set in a landmark tower on the river, it’s in the French Quarter and close enough to the action but also away from the fray. The rooms and suites are elegant escapes with serene design and standout views. A rooftop pool and spa are perfect for unwinding after an eventful evening, and the hotel is also one of the few spots in town that truly caters to families.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed in the outlets unless it's a service animal WRO Approved to exceed weight limit, but not number of dogs per room. Must note details in comments and traces for example, breed, weight and name (pet amenities) and advise callers they will need to sign a waiver.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Henrietta  in New Orleans
ld.description: New Orleans might just have more character than any other city in the United States. Not every hotel in town lives up to the city’s legendary reputation, but the Henrietta has personality to spare. It’s a new build, and a strikingly modern one at that, at least from the outside — but look closer and you’ll see it’s packed with references to classic NOLA architecture, from the arched colonnade on the ground floor to the galleries on the upper floors.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Peter and Paul in New Orleans
ld.description: The last thing you want to see in New Orleans is some kind of minimalistic, modernist-inspired “design” hotel. You’re here because this city, more than any other in America, has a character and an identity that’s uniquely its own. And so does Hotel Peter & Paul, an old Catholic school and a 19th-century church that have been transformed into a stylish and modern — but not at all modernist — boutique hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Saint Vincent in New Orleans
ld.description: This handsome red brick edifice, a 19th-century landmark in New Orleans’ Lower Garden District, would be promising raw material for any hotelier; the owners of the Hotel St. Vincent, however, are hoteliers of unusual talent, and what they’ve made of it is extraordinary. The interiors are full of retro inspiration and historical detail, but they’re anything but old-fashioned. And the comforts are substantial, even luxurious, without feeling the least bit ostentatious. Meanwhile, the Hotel St. Vincent takes food and drink as seriously as you’d expect in this town — Elizabeth Street Café is the French-Vietnamese option, while San Lorenzo showcases Italian flavors, and the the Paradise Lounge lobby bar opens onto the patio.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Maison Metier in New Orleans
ld.description: It’s a rare hotel, in New Orleans or anywhere else, that can so effortlessly combine the youthful good looks of a hipster-brand boutique hotel with the grown-up glamour of something substantially more luxurious. Maison Métier, however, confidently threads this particular needle. The look is unapologetically luxe, right down to the jewel-like colored marble tiles in the bathrooms. But in these hands, luxe doesn’t mean stuffy — the accommodations feel like bedrooms in the home of an eccentric, mysteriously wealthy friend, one who’s careful to make sure you never feel underdressed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Celestine New Orleans in New Orleans
ld.description: The French Quarter doesn’t always live up to its expectations, but a hotel like the Celestine New Orleans is a reminder of what makes this one of the most unique neighborhoods in America. Fourteen rooms and suites decorated in a retro European-inspired style look out over either busy Toulouse Street or the tranquil inner courtyard; while they’re plenty comfortable, they’re more notable for their eclectic and richly detailed style. Peychaud’s, the cocktail bar named for the famous local bitters brand, is the social heart of the Celestine, gathering guests in the courtyard over a glass.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton New Orleans in New Orleans
ld.description: In a city filled with opulent manors and gleaming white columns, the Ritz-Carlton has found the ideal setting for its own tried-and-true formula for classic luxury. Don’t expect any funky twists on the chain’s standards, like the black terrazzo floors at the South Beach branch or the minimalist decor at the downtown Manhattan location — this Ritz-Carlton plays by the book.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Windsor Court in New Orleans
ld.description: Despite its perch on the outskirts of the French Quarter, The Windsor Court isn't exactly full of Creole charm. Forget fluffy beignets and the strains of a saxophone wafting through the humid air; think instead of afternoon tea with blackcurrant scones and smartly dressed maids straightening 300-threadcount cotton sheets. Indeed, as the name suggests, The Windsor Court has a distinctly British feel that matches New Orleans’ old-world appeal, if not its colorful sensuousness.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed for an additional fee.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Chanler at Cliff Walk  in Newport
ld.description: The Gilded Age mansions that line Newport, Rhode Island’s coastal Cliff Walk are an attraction unto themselves; it’s convenient, then, that one of them is open to guests and doing business as the thoroughly luxurious Chanler at Cliff Walk. Not content with a single style, its rooms and villas range across historical periods from Tudor to Georgian and back to the Renaissance. Fireplaces are universal, Jacuzzis nearly so, and some of the views are nothing short of astonishing. Two restaurants, the fine-dining Cara and the slightly more casual Remy’s Loose, gather hotel guests and Newport locals for impressive Mediterranean-accented New England coastal fare.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Cliffside Inn in Newport
ld.description: In Newport, Rhode Island’s historic district, tradition isn’t exactly in short supply. But with the Cliffside Inn, the New England–based Lark Hotels has transformed a beautiful Victorian house into a lovely 16-room boutique hotel. And not just any Newport Victorian — this one happens to have been the home of the painter Beatrice Turner, whose artwork adorns its interiors.
ld.petsAllowed: The hotel has 3 dog-friendly Suites with private exterior entrances—the Cliff, Hydrangea, and Atlantic Suites. Dogs must weigh 30 lbs. and under. A dog bed, bowl and a welcome toy are included in a 50 USD per pet, per day fee.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Vanderbilt, Auberge Collection in Newport
ld.description: Here authenticity means something quite different from museum-grade preservation. The former Vanderbilt Hall, semi-miraculously tucked in to a quiet street in central Newport, has evolved with the times — not in an anxious, trend-chasing way, but tastefully, confidently, so that the character of the place shines through. The building is still as it ever was, and the public spaces retain their historical aspect as well, while the rooms range from classic to contemporary in style — all, though, have been modernized where it counts, bringing them up to today’s luxury-boutique standards.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Menhaden in North Fork Long Island
ld.description: Long Island contains multitudes, from Brooklyn and Queens (technically) to the Hamptons, and beyond. The relatively sleepy North Fork certainly qualifies as beyond — Greenport, once a fishing village, is now an upscale haven for travelers from the city, and the heart of the Long Island wine country. It’s also, as you’ll have noticed, home to the Menhaden, a stylish and self-assured 16-room boutique hotel, set right on Front Street, at one end of Greenport’s compact main drag.
ld.petsAllowed: Small pets are allowed on request, on a case-by-case basis, for an additional fee. Please confirm prior to arrival.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Manoir Hovey in North Hatley
ld.description: While the Eastern Townships of Québec are the French-speaking answer to the rural idylls of northern New England, the Manoir Hovey takes its inspiration from something a little further south — this lakeside retreat was built 125 years ago, in the style of George Washington’s Mount Vernon plantation, and this classic country inn is an escape that’s so refined it borders on the aristocratic.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: 1 Hotel Central Park in New York City
ld.description: Heavily weathered reclaimed wood, industrial-style windows, and dense vegetation climbing green walls — these are not exactly commonplace sights on 58th Street, between Billionaires’ Row and Central Park. It’s a statement of intent from 1 Hotel Central Park, the flagship of the 1 Hotels group, headed by Barry Sternlicht, founder of Starwood and the W hotels — and the intent behind 1 Hotels is to combine quality hospitality with social responsibility.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Aman New York in New York City
ld.description: There was a time when the Aman name was strictly synonymous with secluded resort destinations; Aman Tokyo was proof that the top of a city-center skyscraper could offer its own sense of seclusion. And Aman New York is still another chapter in the evolution of this top-tier hospitality brand: a self-contained world of luxury right in the heart of Manhattan, on 57th Street at 5th Avenue.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Baccarat Hotel & Residences in New York City
ld.description: The flagship hotel from Baccarat Crystal leverages every ounce of its two-and-a-half-century heritage here, just south of Central Park, pulling out all the stops to erect a conspicuous Midtown heavyweight just opposite MoMA. Designers Patrick Gilles and Dorothée Boissier make excellent use of signature crystalware throughout, a memorable counterpoint to midtown’s reigning beige affluence. Take the foyer, for instance: 2,000 LED-embedded Harcourt glasses unite in a 24-hour light installation. Or the Grand Salon, a flamboyant assemblage in pleated-silk wall treatments, silver-leaf paneling, fresh roses in orb bouquets, and terrace topiary with a museum view. Resign yourself to the fact that you’ll likely be out-diva-ed by the décor and you’ll be just fine.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Casa Cipriani New York in New York City
ld.description: Lower Manhattan’s iconic Battery Maritime Building, a 1906 ferry terminal in an ornate Beaux-Arts style, is the venue for Casa Cipriani, a members’ club and luxury boutique hotel by the legendary Italian restaurateurs and hoteliers. Inside is probably the purest dose of contemporary Italian luxury design available this side of Milan; the rooms and suites are remarkably restrained in their opulence, in contrast with the building’s exterior ornament, and those that face the river offer a view unlike any other hotel in town. The Club restaurant is classic Cipriani while the Jazz Café is modeled after a prewar supper club, live music and all.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Crosby Street Hotel, Firmdale Hotels in New York City
ld.description: There was a time when the Firmdale hotels were more or less synonymous with London. The group’s Crosby Street Hotel, however, changed all that. The setting, on the cobbled street for which it’s named, is a perfect one, both in the thick of SoHo and just removed enough from Broadway for a bit of privacy. Meanwhile the style is a fine fit for a neighborhood whose artistic residents transformed an old industrial district into an upscale residential and commercial one; behind those typically Firmdale metal-framed warehouse-style windows is the strong dose of English town-meets-country luxury that New York didn’t know it needed.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Faena New York in New York City
ld.description: Two decades after the original Faena in Buenos Aires and one decade after its Miami Beach sequel, New York has now joined the Faena universe. Faena New York stands alongside the High Line, in Chelsea, on the westernmost block of 18th Street, a location that feels both connected to the city and also, somehow, in a world of its own — fitting for a hotel that aims to create an experience that’s quite unlike anything else.
ld.petsAllowed: Faena New York welcomes dogs up to 25 lbs. A non-refundable $250 pet fee will apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fouquet’s New York in New York City
ld.description: Fouquet’s New York is a combination of two well-loved phrases we never thought we’d see together; the Parisian luxury hotel brand has indeed set up shop in Tribeca, marrying some very French Art Deco–inspired interiors with a post-industrial brick structure that could hardly be more Lower Manhattan. The result, as you might imagine, is a hit in both the fashion and food worlds, and gets to the heart of what people love about both Tribeca and Paris.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Nine Orchard in New York City
ld.description: Whether or not the phrase Dimes Square means anything to you, you’ll appreciate the mini-neighborhood Nine Orchard calls home. Here, at the east end of Canal Street, where the Lower East Side meets Chinatown, there’s a buzz that’s reminiscent of some of Downtown’s earlier golden ages — and, in Nine Orchard itself, there’s a hotel with enough character and personality to become a proper neighborhood institution.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Pendry Manhattan West in New York City
ld.description: For their first hotel in New York, Pendry — the urban luxury-hotel imprint of the Montage Resorts brand — is staking out new territory. Manhattan West is part of the huge Hudson Yards Redevelopment that’s changed the face of Midtown’s west side, and the Pendry Manhattan West, occupying an undulating glass tower by architects Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, shifts the city’s luxury-hospitality center of gravity a bit further towards the Hudson.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed for an additional fee.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Beekman - A Thompson Hotel in New York City
ld.description: Hard to believe an architectural gem of the Beekman’s stature went neglected for so many years, but we’re happy to report that it’s back in business, and it’s been put to the best possible use. The Beekman, a Thompson Hotel, to give it its full name, is an Old New York original, an 1881-vintage skyscraper from the days when a skyscraper meant nine stories of terraced red brick. And if the silhouette doesn’t convince you of its landmark status, a glance upwards surely will, as you walk across the towering central atrium with its pyramidal glass skylight.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets up to 35 pounds are allowed at The Beekman - A Thompson Hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Bowery Hotel in New York City
ld.description: From the outside it’s clear enough that the Bowery Hotel is a relatively recent addition to the neighborhood, but what’s inside is such a faithful homage to classic New York you’d be forgiven for starting to think it’s been here forever. Its eclectic, bohemian look helped usher in a new kind of romance in boutique-hotel style, and the timelessness of its aesthetic means the romance is still fresh long after the glossy minimalism of some of its contemporaries has begun to fade.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel in New York City
ld.description: If it’s not the most famous hotel in all of New York, it’s certainly the most famous hotel on the Upper East Side. The Carlyle Hotel is pure, undiluted essence of old-world Manhattan sophistication, and has been since the days when it was JFK’s “New York White House.” It’s played host to too many famous characters to list; it’s said that Princess Diana, Michael Jackson, and Steve Jobs once shared an elevator here. When you’ve got that reputation for timeless elegance and faultless professionalism, you don’t worry about innovating — you can leave novelty to the downtown boutiques and focus on classic hospitality.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Fifth Avenue Hotel in New York City
ld.description: Named for one of New York’s most iconic thoroughfares, the Fifth Avenue Hotel is more than just one hotel among many in the city’s thriving NoMad neighborhood. Architecturally, it spans more than a century, combining a 1907 Renaissance-style structure by the original Penn Station architects with a modern 24-story glass tower. And inside, the Gilded Age glamour of its public spaces serves as the inspiration for designer Martin Brudnizki’s fantastically colorful and ornate rooms and suites.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. There is a USD 250 charge per per pet stay, with a maximum of 2 pets per room.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Greenwich Hotel in New York City
ld.description: What do we know about the Greenwich Hotel? It’s got a celebrity owner (none other than Robert DeNiro), a prime Tribeca location, impeccable design credentials courtesy of one of New York’s top firms, Grayling Design, and some truly obsessive construction, having something to do with thousands of very expensive handmade bricks. Now there’s no question that all these things make for great press, but do they mean anything to the guests?

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Hotel Chelsea in New York City
ld.description: There was never any question the legendary Hotel Chelsea would eventually face a significant update; it’s good for the Chelsea, and for New York, that it fell to Sean MacPherson to do it, along with partners Ira Drukier and Richard Born. MacPherson’s other hotels around town — the Marlton, the Bowery, the Maritime and more — help usher the romance of old New York into the modern era in a way that’s nostalgic but also authentic. And in the Chelsea, in particular, there’s much to be nostalgic about.
ld.petsAllowed: \n One pet per guest is welcome for no additional fee. A $50 fee will be charged for each additional pet, per night. Both dogs and cats are allowed, but they may not be left alone and unkenneled. Water and food bowls are available upon request. All guests with pets must sign a pet waiver upon arrival.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Lowell in New York City
ld.description: There’s plenty of flashy, ostentatious luxury to be found in New York, if that’s your style, but the Lowell, on Manhattan’s posh Upper East Side, presents an alternative vision. Around here there’s still some affection for an understated sort of luxury, and anyone who’s nonplussed by the Lowell’s lobby — where’s the soaring atrium, the million-dollar art installation? — need only bear this fact in mind.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Ludlow Hotel in New York City
ld.description: A hotel doesn’t need much more than great rooms, inspiring public spaces, and thoughtful, efficient service. Of course it’s not as easy as it sounds. But when you’ve got the kind of pedigree the Ludlow Hotel has — it’s related to the Bowery, the Marlton and the Maritime, among other New York favorites — you’re beginning with a bit of a head start.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed (charges apply).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Mark Hotel in New York City
ld.description: It’s about as far as you can get — both figuratively and literally — from the funky downtown boutique hotels of lower Manhattan. The Mark is the very picture of classic, timeless Upper East Side poshness, in spite of — or maybe even because of — its recent, extremely thorough renovation. And in its present incarnation it’s proof that old money doesn’t necessarily imply old-fashioned.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. There is $100+tx pet fee for dogs under 25lbs.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Mercer in New York City
ld.description: The first SoHo loft hotel is still the definitive entry in the genre. This 19th-century Romanesque Revival building was filled with artists’ lofts during the neighborhood’s postwar heyday, and its late-’90s renovation at the hands of superstar interior designer Christian Liaigre transformed it into one of the best of the first generation of boutique hotels. And while the competition has multiplied, the Mercer’s never lost its sheen — it’s perennially on the radar of some of the world’s most style-conscious travelers.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed complimentary.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Peninsula New York in New York City
ld.description: Behind a century-old Beaux Arts facade right on the poshest stretch of Fifth Avenue lies the New York franchise of the phenomenal Hong Kong-based Peninsula Hotel. And if there’s anywhere in America that’s an appropriate spot for some mega-hospitality, Far East style, it’s this particular corner of midtown Manhattan, a stone’s throw from icons like Rockefeller Center, Radio City Music Hall and Tiffany & Co.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park in New York City
ld.description: We love small, independent hotels, but you’ve got to hand it to the big chains once in a while. It takes a staggering amount of dedicated effort to build a brand up to the point where “Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park” tells you just about everything you could possibly wish to know about a hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad in New York City
ld.description: Purveyors of classic luxury Ritz-Carlton can do contemporary as well — the Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad occupies one of the tallest buildings in this still-developing neighborhood, at 28th and Broadway, and its interiors achieve a perfect balance: swanky enough for old-school customers and stylish enough for the new. The amenities, both in-room and out, are first-rate, as you’d expect from Ritz-Carlton, while the culinary program is overseen by the celebrated chef José Andrés, and includes an Eastern Mediterranean restaurant, a rooftop bar, and a Spanish/Japanese hybrid.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Surrey, A Corinthia Hotel in New York City
ld.description: New York’s Upper East Side is not exactly a boutique-hotel hotbed, at least traditionally, but this revamped century-old classic adds a measure of youthful style to a neighborhood better known for traditional luxury. The Surrey, A Corinthia Hotel still looks conventionally glamorous from the street; this Art Deco edifice was a mid-century celebrity favorite. Inside, though, thanks to designer Martin Brudnizki, it’s been brought gracefully up to date, and is stylish in a way that’s respectful of its history even as it appeals to a new generation.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Twenty Two New York in New York City
ld.description: Despite what the song says, it’s equally true that if you can make it in London, you can make it anywhere. The Twenty Two New York is a London import, named for its sister’s address on Grosvenor Square, and while it’s cut from the same cloth, it’s not an exercise in Anglophilia. Rather, it’s one part Manhattan history, thanks to its home in the restored Margaret Louisa Vanderbilt house, and one part international modern luxury, just like the London-based hotel, restaurant, and private club with which it shares its name.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Wall Street Hotel in New York City
ld.description: Lower Manhattan’s financial district has more to recommend it than you might think, and a hotel like the Wall Street Hotel goes a long way towards illustrating the appeal. The 19th-century Tontine Building stands on the site of a coffee house that was once the home of the stock exchange itself, and after a thorough renovation it’s now home to a 180-room luxury boutique hotel — one that happens to be decorated with Australian Aboriginal art, along with an eclectic range of decorative elements spanning the entire life of this Beaux-Arts classic, from 1855 to the present.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Whitby Hotel, Firmdale Hotels in New York City
ld.description: The Whitby Hotel brings the warmth and coziness of English hospitality to a neighborhood that’s already got plenty of American-style luxury hotels, and proves that Firmdale can compete with anyone in the world on comfort, while looking just that much more stylish and charming while they’re at it.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: W New York - Union Square in New York City
ld.description: In its first incarnation W New York – Union Square was one of the earliest and most visible boutique hotels, and it made a strong impression via the contrast of incongruous elements — specifically, the futuristic-minimalist W interior-design style and the old-money vibe of this handsome 1911 Beaux-Arts building. After a thorough renovation by the same Rockwell Group that was responsible for the 2001 version, it’s looking fresher than ever, and while the interiors remain eye-catching, the new look is a more harmonious blend of a century-plus of influences.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria New York in New York City
ld.description: The Waldorf Astoria’s revival is nothing short of cinematic. After a seven-year restoration by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, this Park Avenue landmark re-emerges with its Art Deco soul fully restored: murals uncovered, silver corridors gleaming, and the Grand Ballroom ready to reclaim its place in the city’s story. Inside, designers Pierre-Yves Rochon and Jean-Louis Deniot created calm, residential-style suites that contrast beautifully with the drama of the public spaces. With Michael Anthony's Lex Yard brasserie and the vast new Guerlain Spa, the Waldorf emerges not as a memory, but as proof that true icons never fade — they simply return, more certain of themselves than ever.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Warren Street Hotel, Firmdale Hotels in New York City
ld.description: Kit Kemp’s Firmdale hotels are practically a genre unto themselves — luxurious yet lively, they combine country and city aesthetics, and feel glamorous and cozy at the same time. Colors, in particular, run rampant, and that’s particularly true of the Warren Street Hotel, whose bright blue façade stands out among its red brick Tribeca neighbors. And though they’re uniformly well-located in some of London and New York’s finest neighborhoods, they feel, in a way, like self-contained worlds apart from their surroundings.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Grana B&B in Oaxaca City
ld.description: A stately 18th-century residence on the west side of Oaxaca City is now Grana B&B, and it’s safe to say that it’s rather more grand than the bed-and-breakfast tag ordinarily implies. Its 15 rooms have been left largely intact — a necessity given the house’s landmark status — but they’ve been updated in an eclectic, contemporary style, mixing traditional craft and modern design in roughly equal measure. Breakfast is served daily at an oversized communal table; among the house’s other common spaces are the tranquil central courtyard and a rooftop with a view of the city and the mountains in the distance.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: 100 Loma de Guajal, San Felipe del Agua

ld.name: Hotel Casa Santo Origen  in Oaxaca City
ld.description: Set where the northern suburbs meet the foothills of the Sierra Madre de Oaxaca mountains, at a comfortable remove from Oaxaca City’s busy center, Hotel Casa Santo Origen aims to create a sense of pleasantly secluded tranquility. It achieves this through a compound-like layout that emphasizes privacy, a location that’s fifteen crucial minutes’ drive from downtown traffic, and through warm and welcoming interiors that display colonial, indigenous, and contemporary influences in more or less equal measure.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Calle Porfirio Díaz 212, Ruta Independencia, Centro

ld.name: Pug Seal Oaxaca in Oaxaca City
ld.description: Pug Seal’s inventive, pocket-sized boutique B&Bs feel like perfect little secrets in the vastness of Mexico City — in the compact historical center of Oaxaca City, however, a 20-suite boutique hotel looms larger, just by comparison with its surroundings. Not to worry: Pug Seal Oaxaca is just as tranquil, just as residential in atmosphere as its cousins in the capital, designed as it is around a central courtyard decorated with colorful murals.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Citizen House Hotel in Oklahoma City
ld.description: This private members' club and boutique hotel occupies three floors of a downtown tower, designed by Michaelis Boyd with electric blues, mismatched patterns, and rich textures. Sixteen apartment-style rooms function as residences rather than typical suites, with the largest spanning nearly 1,000 square feet with a freestanding tub, while Corner Suites capture skyline and National Memorial views through wraparound windows. Chef Miguel Acosta runs the kitchen, turning out seared regional proteins and refined small plates. The Living Room pours seasonal cocktails, and a speakeasy behind an unmarked door handles late-night drinks and karaoke.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Montage Laguna Beach in Orange County
ld.description: Montage Resort & Spa is a throwback to the Laguna Beach of the turn of the twentieth century, a conscious homage to the city’s birth as an artists’ colony. This is the Laguna Beach of the early 1900s, the romantic vision of design in complement with nature. The resort itself, with its winding pathways and classic stone architecture, is surrounded by lush gardens, shaded by tall trees, and sits atop a rugged, rocky bluff, overlooking the white sand beaches below. The interiors are liberally decorated with artworks, some contemporary, some dating back to the heyday of the Arts & Crafts movement, which is Montage’s main inspiration.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: ette hotel in Orlando
ld.description: Luxury boutique hotels are still not exactly the norm in Orlando, but this one is up there with the best of them. Ette is just a few minutes’ drive from the theme parks, but within its walls is a hotel as urban and urbane as its counterparts in Miami or New York. The lobby is resplendent in richly figured Italian marble and the rooms are modern and minimalist, but not without warmth, and the comforts are first-rate. The Michelin-starred chef Akira Black is responsible for Lipa, the rooftop restaurant, as well as Salt & The Cellar, the flagship restaurant and cocktail bar.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Lake Nona Wave Hotel in Orlando
ld.description: Orlando’s Lake Nona Wave Hotel is known for its technology, and we’re not just talking about its gently curving silhouettes; it’s among the first to feature smart windows, which dim automatically in response to bright sunlight, as well as Toto toilets and, in selected rooms, high-tech beds and sleep-quality apps. Just as important, from our perspective, is the fact that its interiors are, if anything, even more distinctive in their design than the hotel’s memorable exterior.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Orlando, Grande Lakes in Orlando
ld.description: At times we’re a bit ambivalent about the big corporate chain hotels, preferring to take our chances with the small and the unique. But how quickly, in a town like Orlando, we go running for the comforting consistency of the Ritz-Carlton.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fairmont Chateau Laurier Gold Experience in Ottawa
ld.description: A private experience within Ottawa’s grandest hotel, Fairmont Gold offers an upgraded stay inside the iconic Château Laurier. Guests enter through a separate check-in and gain access to a private lounge, where breakfast, evening canapés, and soft conversation unfold beneath historic detailing. Rooms are classically styled but thoroughly updated, some with postcard views of Parliament and the canal. The Gold tier delivers what it promises: history, scale, and storybook atmosphere: distilled into something more personal, discreet and entirely worth seeking out in Canada’s capital.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Palm Beach in Palm Beach
ld.description: Pleasures don’t get much simpler than the ones on offer at the Four Seasons Resort Palm Beach. This upscale beach town and this ultra-palatable luxury hotel are a match made in heaven. The rooms and suites are contemporary in style, but gently so — this is a long way, figuratively and literally, from Miami Beach. The beach club, the pools, and the spa are all as tranquil as can be, and the restaurants don’t disappoint — Florie’s, the flagship, is a partnership with Mauro Colagreco, who adapts his Italian and Argentine influences to the climate and produce of South Florida.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palm House in Palm Beach
ld.description: After sitting vacant for nearly two decades on a prime piece of oceanfront real estate, a landmark hotel in Palm Beach underwent extensive renovations and reopened as Palm House. Many of this Mediterranean-style property’s best features were preserved, from the coral-hued facade to the elegant pool deck framed by palm trees in the central courtyard. But as the first property to open in the US as part of the London-based L+R Hotels’ Iconic Luxury Hotels collection, it's been updated accordingly. Refreshed rooms are bright and cheerful with sixties-inspired decor — decorative mirrored wall panels, mod table lamps, king-sized beds with retro-looking upholstered headboards, Juliet balconies, and huge marble bathrooms with soaking tubs. Suites are palatial with curving modular sofas and Art Deco details; one has an Alaskan king bed rumored to be the largest in town.
