The fanciful Palm bar, with glamorous pink Murano glass chandeliers suspended from high vaulting ceilings, is worth the trip on its own.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Breakers Palm Beach in Palm Beach
ld.description: Miami may be where you make yourself seen in a bid to get in the gossip pages; Palm Beach, though, is an altogether different sort of place, and no hotel encapsulates its essence quite like the stately Breakers. More than a century in the making, this hotel takes its style cues from Italian Renaissance villas, spanning an estate of some 140 oceanfront acres. All things considered, though, "hotel" may be too modest a word; facilities include two 18-hole golf courses, a tennis complex, a 20,000-square-foot spa, and a Mediterranean-style beach club, the sort of place where uniformed personal concierges deliver towels and cold drinks to guests lolling in private, poolside bungalows.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Colony Hotel in Palm Beach
ld.description: Since 1947, this pink stucco landmark has been Palm Beach's most recognizable address, hosting royalty, presidents, and movie stars with equal measures of glamor and irreverence. Current owners Sarah and Andrew Wetenhall restored it with Kemble Interiors, preserving the scalloped headboards, patterned wallpapers, and retro-tropical color schemes: green, blue, and pink, that made it iconic in the first place. Swifty's restaurant and the outdoor pool bar keep a lively local crowd coming through year-round, and the fourteen top-floor residences, including a Gwyneth Paltrow-designed villa, are in a category of their own.
ld.petsAllowed: The hotel welcomes pets, charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Vineta Hotel in Palm Beach
ld.description: A classic 1926 Mediterranean Revival building close to the heart of Palm Beach became, a hundred years later, the first American property for the Oetker Hotels group (Hôtel Le Bristol, Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc, etc.). Like its European cousins The Vineta Hotel draws on both classic grand-hotel hospitality and the lessons of the boutique-hotel era, and delivers an experience that feels familiar enough to the traditionally minded but is fresh and forward-looking in its details and implementation.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Please note that we are pup‑friendly for dogs up to 45 lbs (20 kg). There is no pet fee and we allow one dog per room.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The White Elephant Palm Beach in Palm Beach
ld.description: Though it’s a sister to the Nantucket hotel of the same name, the White Elephant Palm Beach is pure South Florida: a century-old Mediterranean Revival structure containing just 32 rooms and suites, all of them renovated in a contemporary-luxe style that’s tailor-made to complement the architecture. There’s an outdoor pool in the charming palm-lined courtyard, and a shuttle service connecting the hotel with the town’s public beach, and the neighborhood, in the historic town center, is impressively walkable. Lola 41 Palm Beach, the restaurant, is another Nantucket import, sister to the highly regarded Northeastern eatery.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Dive Palm Springs in Palm Springs Area
ld.description: You can get pure mid-century Palm Springs just about anywhere in town, but it’s safe to say Dive is the only place you’ll find the spirit of 1960s St. Tropez. In keeping with its inspiration, this 11-room hideaway is glamorous — its adults-only policy certainly helps — and its sunny colors and eccentric, bohemian interiors achieve a uniquely Mediterranean vibe. The pool is a charmer, the garden and orchard are heavenly outdoor spaces, and the atmosphere throughout is nothing short of restorative. Speaking of which — there’s no restaurant per se, beyond breakfast service, but the location is convenient to any number of fine options, and the staff is happy to guide you on your way.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Holiday House Palm Springs in Palm Springs Area
ld.description: At Holiday House, a 28-room boutique hotel in downtown Palm Springs, there’s no messing about with superior, deluxe, and the like: the room categories are Good, Better, and Best. And the good is pretty good, indeed. Good means bright and cheerful, with original artwork, bath hardware by Waterworks, and custom textiles by Mark D. Sikes, the same Hollywood-based designer who reimagined the hotel’s interiors during recent restorations. Better means bigger, in this case, with a wet bar for good measure. And Best means mountain views, plus a private balcony or patio where you can properly enjoy them. (If the Best isn’t quite good enough, look into one of Holiday House’s top-of-the-line options, the aptly named Big Room or The Suite.)
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets under 35 lbs are welcome at 100 USD per stay. Holiday House Palm Springs requests they be on leash when outside of the room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: La Serena Villas in Palm Springs Area
ld.description: Palm Springs may be virtually synonymous with mid-century modernism, but it’s far from the only style in town. La Serena Villas is the latest transformation of a 1933-vintage Spanish-style hotel, and while its new owners have thoroughly updated it for the boutique-hotel era, they’ve kept its stylistic inspiration intact — in fact you’d be hard pressed to find a lovelier example of colonial-contemporary architecture and design.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sparrows Lodge in Palm Springs Area
ld.description: Take a hint from the word-of-mouth publicity, the quiet poolside crowd in retro swimwear, and the understated logo — a minimalist illustration of two little birds perched on a branch. Sparrows Lodge is not aiming for the mainstream. Recycled from the Fifties and refreshed for a style-conscious clientele, this woodsy hideaway is the kind of place where people play horseshoes, swing wooden tennis rackets and read books by their private campfires. At night, the property’s original red barn opens for dinner and drinks. It’s like a dreamy hipster version of the summer camp of your childhood — complete with artisan cocktails and deep, luxurious bathtubs fashioned out of old horse troughs.
ld.petsAllowed: PETS:  We welcome well-behaved dogs under 40 pounds with a one-time fee of $100 per stay, per dog (max two dogs.) Dogs are required to be on a leash at ALL times and not allowed on indoor or outdoor furniture. Please let us know in advance if you plan to bring your pet so we may assign your room accordingly. We have a limited number of rooms available for dogs. Dog policy will be presented at check-in.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Parker Palm Springs in Palm Springs Area
ld.description: This hotel has racked up an impressive number of names in its seventy-year history. Once Gene Autry’s Melody Ranch estate, it was, for a time, the Merv Griffin Resort, then the Givenchy Hotel and Spa — and now, after a substantial rethink by lifestyle designer Jonathan Adler, it’s back; this time as The Parker Palm Springs.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Goldener Hirsch, Auberge Collection in Park City
ld.description: What was once a single California wine country is now one of the most prestigious names in luxury boutique hospitality, and when Auberge Resorts took over the Goldener Hirsch in 2021, the whole Park City hospitality scene got an upgrade. They did more than rename the inn, of course. Star Seattle architects Olson Kundig were brought in for a substantial expansion, and today’s Goldener Hirsch is a double act: the original Bavarian-style chalet is now joined by a striking modern addition.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Montage Deer Valley in Park City
ld.description: Montage Resorts made its name with a pair of Southern California originals, in Laguna Beach and Beverly Hills, and on the face of it, it seems surprising that they chose the ski town of Park City, Utah for their third act, the ski-in, ski-out Montage Deer Valley. But aside from a few technical details — a ski shop replaces surfing lessons, that sort of thing — hospitality is hospitality, whether it’s on the beach or halfway up a mountain.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pendry Park City in Park City
ld.description: It took some time for the boutique-hotel revolution to reach the ski towns of North America, but it’s safe to say it’s officially arrived. The first mountain resort from Montage’s design-oriented Pendry brand is the Pendry Park City, which is at once the most stylish resort in the Park City area and the most luxurious entry in the Canyons Village resort area. Expect the classic timber-lodge paradigm to start looking uncomfortably dated any day now.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Stein Eriksen Lodge in Park City
ld.description: Established in the Eighties by the legendary Norwegian ski champion Stein Eriksen, this luxury lodge has, in spades, what so many ski hotels lack: personality. Studiously avoiding Mountain West clichés, the Stein Eriksen instead opts for a subdued European design, with robust wooden furnishings, massive stone fireplaces, and cool Scandinavian colors.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Lodge at Blue Sky, Auberge Collection

ld.name: The Lodge at Blue Sky, Auberge Collection in Park City
ld.description: Situated on 4,000 acres just outside Park City, The Lodge at Blue Sky offers a remote, design-driven take on the mountain getaway. Accommodations range from creekside cabins to grass-roofed hillside suites and cliffside rooms with wide views of Alexander Canyon. The vibe is peaceful but active with horseback rides, high-alpine hikes, and seasonal meals that pull from the on-site farm. Adults can retreat to the Creek Houses, while families gravitate toward the spacious Sky Lodge suites. Every detail: stone, glass, wood, is placed to keep the landscape front and center.
ld.petsAllowed: Two pets maximum are allowed. The pet fee is $80 per pet and includes dog bed, bowls, amenity, and additional cleaning. The weight limit is 80 pounds and pit bulls are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Washington School House Hotel in Park City
ld.description: The trouble with ski hotels, all too often, is that the majesty of the mountain setting seems to tempt hoteliers into taking the easy way out. You can’t compete with nature, so why even try? Happily it’s an attitude that’s by no means universal these days — the proprietors of Park City’s Washington School House, for one, suffer from no such affliction.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Anna & Bel in Philadelphia
ld.description: Philadelphia’s hip Fishtown neighborhood is the setting for this substantial red brick structure, which was first a women’s home and later a retirement community. It seems the third time’s the charm — Anna & Bel sees this institution (and the neighboring buildings) turned into a stylish and modern boutique hotel. The 50 rooms and suites are decorated in a style that’s both warm and minimalist, memorably mixing modern and antique elements. Add an interior courtyard, complete with a heated pool, as well as a Mediterranean restaurant called Bastia, and this is arguably the neighborhood’s first proper, full-featured boutique hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Hotel Philadelphia at Comcast Center

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Philadelphia at Comcast Center in Philadelphia
ld.description: If you haven’t been to Philadelphia lately you might be caught off guard by the fact that the current Four Seasons is an entirely different hotel a few blocks away from the one you used to know. Four Seasons Hotel Philadelphia at Comcast Center, to give it its full name, is no longer a historical landmark on Logan Square, but a skyscraper-topping refuge in Four Seasons’ new forward-looking contemporary-cool style.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pet Policy: Pet must weigh no more than 25 lbs. Pet must not be left unattended. If guest requires a pet-sitter or pet supplies, they should contact the front office with advance notice. Pets are not allowed in any food and beverage outlets and wellness floor. This exclusion does not apply to guide dogs. Guests are responsible for cleaning up after their pet on hotel property and in the neighborhood. Guests must contact the housekeeping department to arrange for a convenient time for servicing their room. Unless the pet owner is present, no attempt will be made to enter the room. The pet owner must be present when the room is cleaned. Guests are responsible for all property damages and/or personal injuries resulting from their pet.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Guild House Philadelphia in Philadelphia
ld.description: A landmark 1855 rowhome in Philadelphia’s Midtown Village is the setting for the Guild House Hotel, a boutique hotel whose 12 rooms and suites are named for 12 notable women from the house’s earlier incarnation as the proto-feminist New Century Guild. The atmosphere is residential, but this is no mere apartment share — the rooms and suites are notable not only for their eclectic, photogenic interiors, but for their comforts as well. Proper hotel service is ever-present, if unobtrusive, and while there’s no in-house restaurant, the Guild House’s concierge is your guide to the neighborhood and the greater city.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Rittenhouse Hotel in Philadelphia
ld.description: Overlooking Rittenhouse Square in one Philadelphia’s toniest districts, this very modern 33-story high-rise gives away little about the luxurious small hotel that lies within. An elegant and charming classic, the Rittenhouse is one of the city’s most exclusive lodgings, offering not only the largest rooms in Philadelphia—each spanning some 450 to 1,700 square feet—but some of the most lavish as well, decked out in rich mahogany and vibrant fabrics and offering far-ranging views of the Square and the city.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Carretera Federal Chetumal-Puerto, Riviera Maya, Juárez KM 298

ld.name: Banyan Tree Mayakoba in Playa del Carmen
ld.description: The Banyan Tree group must have been looking for a challenge. It’s not that Asian-inflected luxury villas can’t work in the Americas; it’s just that the well-developed and not entirely high-end Riviera Maya isn’t exactly the first place you’d look for a resort that depends on an exclusive, desert-island vibe. But the Banyan Tree Mayakoba succeeds in the face of its own unlikelihood, seemingly oblivious to the challenges of its surroundings.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets: small dogs and cats weighing up to 22 pounds are accepted. An additional fee is required, and we encourage you to get in touch with our hotel team to learn more about our pet policy. You can reach us at experienceconcierge-mayakoba@banyantree.com.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Chablé Maroma in Playa del Carmen
ld.description: The original Chablé Resort & Spa wasn’t lacking anything, strictly speaking — it’s hard to go wrong with a luxe-yet-tasteful luxury resort with a wellness focus and plenty of environmental and cultural sensitivity. But its location deep in the Yucatán jungle necessarily left beachgoing types without an outlet for that particular urge. A single hotel can’t have everything, of course, but the second Chablé hotel goes where the first one couldn’t: namely, Punta Maroma, on the Riviera Maya just to the north of Playa del Carmen.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Etéreo, Auberge Collection in Playa del Carmen
ld.description: The Californian-born boutique-luxe Auberge group is responsible for this spectacular 75-unit hotel, set amid a dense mangrove forest and connected by elevated walkways to a pristine white-sand beach. Etéreo’s studios, suites, and penthouses are extravagant in their comforts and impeccably tasteful in their design, full of the work of local artists and artisans, and all supplied with views out to sea. Some add butler service and outdoor hot tubs, and all guests benefit from the SANA spa and a handful of restaurants, from the Maya-inspired Itzam to the Japanese-accented Che Che and El Changarro, the beachside bar and kitchen.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Esencia in Playa del Carmen
ld.description: A mere forty miles south of the glitz and hustle of Cancún lies a decidedly more relaxed section of the Riviera Maya. But usually wherever there are blinding white sand beaches and water so clear you can discern the precise shade of your toenail polish, the developers are close behind. Even this far down the coast, the discriminating traveler needs to do a little legwork to escape the generic experience of the all-inclusive chain resort. Enter the Hotel Esencia, an intimate beachside escape, an antidote to the tacky high-rise hotels elsewhere on Mexico’s Caribbean coast.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

pages.h1: Palmaïa-The House of AïA: All Inclusive Wellness Resort

address.streetAddress: Paseo Xaman - Ha Manzana1, Fracc Playacar

ld.name: Palmaïa-The House of AïA: All Inclusive Wellness Resort in Playa del Carmen
ld.description: Amid plenty of competition in Playa del Carmen, Palmaïa, the House of AïA, styles itself as no mere hotel, but a “wellness enclave,” and sets itself apart from the crowd with an intense devotion to nature, health, and spiritual well-being. The aim is to deliver all the luxury of a more traditional resort, but in a way that’s both environmentally responsible and spiritually edifying — and in Palmaïa’s capable hands it’s an eminently achievable goal.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: Ctra. Federal Cancun-Playa del Carmen KM. 298

ld.name: Rosewood Mayakoba in Playa del Carmen
ld.description: The Riviera Maya has become increasingly appreciated as the escape hatch from Cancún craziness, and the architecturally bold Rosewood Mayakobá raises the sophistication bar up several notches. In a word, this place is refined. The clean white lines of the resort’s pavilions interplay with the lagoons, lush landscaping, infinity pools and a dramatic coast-side golf course, while modern interiors respectfully nod toward the local aesthetic.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: The St. Regis Kanai Resort, Riviera Maya

ld.name: The St. Regis Kanai Resort, Riviera Maya in Playa del Carmen
ld.description: Perched like a retrofuturist spacecraft over and among mangrove wetlands, St. Regis Kanai Resort, Riviera Maya embraces the ecological abundance for which the region is justly famous. Of course, environmental awareness shouldn’t stop you from taking full advantage of the pristine beachfront and the brand’s renowned butler service — just remember, this isn’t the rowdy part of Playa del Carmen. Everything from the carved-walnut custom beds to the palm-forward landscaping to the shell-strewn strand speaks to this sense of place. And for a more hands-on approach to ecotourism, you’re right next door to the Sian Ka’an Biosphere Reserve.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Viceroy Riviera Maya, a Luxury Villa Resort

ld.name: Viceroy Riviera Maya, a Luxury Villa Resort in Playa del Carmen
ld.description: The name might be more familiar from places like Miami and Santa Monica, but the Viceroy Riviera Maya is proof that the Viceroy group is equally at home in less urban environs. Here, more than most beach hotels, the focus is less on the accommodations themselves than on the setting, a tiny enclave of tasteful, restrained development on a coast that, the rest of the way up and down, is pretty far from unspoiled.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Blind Tiger Portland – Danforth Street in Portland
ld.description: Much more than an apartment share, though certainly not just an ordinary hotel, Blind Tiger Guest House takes its name from the Prohibition-era speakeasy that once occupied the basement of this lovely 19th-century house. Built in 1823, converted into an inn in 1993, it’s fresh off a 2020 renovation by Northeast boutique-hotel specialists Lark Hotels, and the brand’s signature attributes are very much in evidence here: photogenic interiors, luxe comforts, a convivial atmosphere, and a location in a vibrant and walkable corner of town.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Blind Tiger Portland – Carleton Street in Portland
ld.description: A few blocks from its sister on Danforth Street, Blind Tiger Carleton Street carries on in the same style: a six-room guest house in a charming residential neighborhood, decorated with a carefully curated selection of vintage furnishings and local artworks, all within easy walking distance of the best this city has to offer. It’s the work of Lark Hotels, the group responsible for many of New England’s finest boutique hotels — which may be why, in spite of their small size and their private nature, the Blind Tiger houses manage to be such friendly and sociable places.
ld.petsAllowed: No pets allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Portland in Portland
ld.description: At first glance Portland doesn’t seem like the sort of city that’s in need of a hotel of the Ritz-Carlton’s caliber; there’s more to this town, however, than quirky independent boutiques. And this is today’s Ritz-Carlton, not a Neoclassical edifice in white stone but the Broadway Tower, a modern glass skyscraper with spectacular views of the city, the river, and the Cascades. Expect contemporary-classic interiors, thoughtful modern luxuries, a lavish 19th-floor spa, and a restaurant that’s an upscale culinary love letter to the producers and purveyors of the Pacific Northwest.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Woodlark in Portland
ld.description: Portland may be better known in the popular imagination for its hip eccentricity, but it can also do urban elegance with the best of them. Woodlark is a perfect illustration, a pair of historic buildings (one the 1920s-vintage Hotel Cornelius) combined into a single hotel, one that effortlessly embodies Portland’s stylish, cosmopolitan side. The location, between downtown and Burnside, could hardly be more auspicious, close to much of Portland’s best dining and shopping (including the one-of-a-kind Powell’s City of Books).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sundance Resort in Provo
ld.description: Yes, that Sundance. To many minds, this is just another aspect of the multi-faceted house that Robert Redford built, and the fact that it’s a first-class ski getaway is almost secondary. But as many a proud local knows, once you ski Utah, you might never bother with Colorado or California again.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Banyan Tree Puebla in Puebla
ld.description: No isolated resort, the Banyan Tree Puebla is set in a 19th-century building on the edge of the city center, in what used to be the Azul Talavera Hotel. Under the new banner it’s every bit as extravagant a production as we expect from Banyan Tree, marrying historically aware opulence with top-end contemporary comforts and facilities. The rooms and suites bear traces of the building’s past, as does the primary restaurant, Pasquinel Bistrot; it’s joined by several more, including a panoramic rooftop deck with a Thai restaurant and bar, as well as a full-featured Banyan Tree spa.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Casona Sforza in Puerto Escondido
ld.description: There’s nothing on the Oaxacan coast — or anywhere else — quite like Casona Sforza, an 11-room luxury boutique hotel whose unmistakable arched volumes stand mere yards from the beach on the south end of Puerto Escondido. Architect Alberto Kalach designed these distinctive structures, which are placed to maximize their views, their privacy, and their exposure to the breeze; the stylish rough-luxe interiors, meanwhile, are by the Mexico City–based MOB Studio.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: BellView Boutique Hotel in Puerto Vallarta
ld.description: A boutique hotel doesn’t have to be a design hotel, in the modern or contemporary sense — any hotel that’s modestly sized, memorable, and presents a unique point of view on its setting qualifies as a boutique hotel, in our book. Puerto Vallarta’s BellView Boutique Hotel fits the bill, even though its style is antique from top to bottom. For while there are plenty of bigger and more contemporary hotels in this town, there’s nothing else like BellView, whose seven rooms and suites are overflowing with the sort of historical elegance that’s in painfully short supply around here.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Casa Kimberly Hotel Boutique in Puerto Vallarta
ld.description: This lovely pair of adjoining villas in Puerto Vallarta was once home to Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton — and while the connection is part of its charming history, and its most lavish suite bears Ms. Taylor’s name, what’s important about Casa Kimberly is the sheer extravagant romance of the place as it stands today. The suites are all different, but all are exceedingly comfortable and elegant in a way you have to imagine Ms. Taylor would have approved of. There’s a small spa with a pair of treatment rooms, and the Iguana is the open-air restaurant and tequila bar with a view of the city and the bay.
ld.petsAllowed: Only pets allowed are dogs, under 30 pounds. The pet should always be with the owner and never be left in the room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hacienda San Angel in Puerto Vallarta
ld.description: Puerto Vallarta was, at one time, among the most glamorous of Mexican destinations — and though it fell victim to overdevelopment, it’s never completely lost its magic. These days there’s a bit of a resurgence at hand, with a few absolute gems among the big hotels. One of the better examples is the Hacienda San Angel, which makes one little sacrifice — no beach access — in exchange for a measure of privacy and exclusivity that just might be without equal anywhere in town.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Xinalani in Puerto Vallarta
ld.description: Yearning to get away from it all? Puerto Vallarta probably isn’t quite the first place you’ll think of. But then there’s Xinalani, a gloriously secluded eco-resort wedged between the jungle and the water. Technically, it’s in Puerto Vallarta, but it’s actually twelve miles down the coast from the city proper, and only accessible by boat — which makes all the difference. Pick up what you need before boarding, and put an auto-responder on your e-mail: there’s no Starbucks near the hotel, nor a consistently reliable wi-fi connection — no television, no complimentary in-room iPad. The point of coming to Xinalani is to get away from all of that and enjoy the sand, sun, and sea. Well, it’s the bay, technically, the large, crystal-clear Banderas Bay on Mexico’s Pacific coast.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Punta Mita in Punta de Mita
ld.description: Just to the north of Puerto Vallarta, across the Nayarit state border and situated on its own little spit of land, lies Punta Mita — and right in the center of the action lies Four Seasons Resort Punta Mita. At this level you really can’t go wrong; any room, suite, or villa will get you flowy, beach-boho accommodations with to-die-for ocean vistas. And you’ll be spoiled for choice with two private beaches plus a healthy selection of pools to fit your mood. Round it off with an ultra-local experience, ranging from surfing and diving to blending your own tequila to go.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: Lote H-4 Cond. Maestro Ramal, Carretera Federal 200, Km 19.5

ld.name: St. Regis Punta Mita Resort in Punta de Mita
ld.description: Set amongst 22 hectares of lush gardens right next to the beach, The St. Regis Punta Mita Resort occupies an idyllic spot on a Punta de Mita peninsula. Guest rooms and suites open directly onto the gardens or sea views, and inside rooms take their cues from the surrounding nature with layers of natural wood accessorized with Mexican artworks and handcrafted furnishings that celebrate local craftsmanship. Every stay includes the signature St. Regis Butler Service while the facilities include five restaurants and one bar, a spa with a comprehensive list of treatments, an adults-only pool and for families, a children’s pool and kids club.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Desarrollo El Banco Carretera a La Cruz de Huanacaxtle Km 14

ld.name: Susurros del Corazón, Auberge Collection in Punta de Mita
ld.description: The Auberge Collection is best known for its Californian resorts, but its portfolio reaches all the way to the Northeast, to Los Cabos, and now to Punta Mita, just up the coast from Puerto Vallarta. The site, and specifically its stunning expanse of beach, came first; and the evocatively named Susurros del Corazón expertly adapts Auberge’s tastefully luxurious approach to its Pacific Coast setting. The spa is particularly expansive, as are the cascading, terraced swimming pools; opportunities for exploring the coast and the nearby islands are practically endless, as are opportunities for sampling the local culinary traditions via the resort’s multiple restaurants.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Maroma, A Belmond Hotel, Riviera Maya

address.streetAddress: Km 51 Carr. Cancún - Tulum, Riviera Maya

ld.name: Maroma, A Belmond Hotel, Riviera Maya in Punta Maroma
ld.description: Maroma, A Belmond Hotel, Riviera Maya sits on the Riviera Maya, 30 miles south of Cancun on Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, which started as an architect's dream house in the early 80s. Its barrier reef location makes for almost cartoonishly blue crystalline water and one of the world's most highly regarded beaches, featuring a wealth of sea life and water activities.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Auberge Saint-Antoine in Quebec City
ld.description: Auberge Saint-Antoine is half hotel, half museum, a unique blend of a boutique hotel and an old-fashioned bed and breakfast, three centuries-old buildings in the lower Old Port of Québec City, overlooking the stately St. Lawrence river, and just steps from many of this historic city's tourist destinations. The auberge itself occupies an important archaeological site, once home to a cannon battery and a maritime warehouse, and artifacts from various digs are on display in the guest rooms and common areas, including a reception desk built from oak planks two centuries old.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Fairmont Le Château Frontenac in Quebec City
ld.description: The grand dame of the Canadian railway hotels, Fairmont Le Château Frontenac is Québec City’s most famous landmark, a century-old castle high on a bluff over the St. Lawrence river; if you’ve seen a single photo of Québec City, you’ve seen the Château in the background, its green oxidized copper roof and orange Scottish bricks towering above the city’s Vieux Québec historic district. Château Frontenac is a tourist attraction in its own right, and there’s nothing subtle about it — past the sightseers in the lobby is a vast and labyrinthine hotel of some six hundred rooms across six wings, which vary somewhat in age and in relative opulence (though all additions are historically accurate).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fairmont Le Manoir Richelieu in Quebec
ld.description: The magnificent setting of the Fairmont Le Manoir Richelieu, perched high on the Pointe-au-Pic bluffs overlooking the St. Lawrence River, is no coincidence. The location was specifically chosen by a Canadian shipping company that hoped to attract travelers aboard its new passenger vessels from Quèbec City in the late Victorian era. Resembling a grand ivy-clad French château, the luxury hotel is just as striking to behold today, not to mention easier to access. With hundreds of rooms and suites, indoor and outdoor pools, a state-of-the-art spa, an array of upscale dining venues, and easy access to outdoor activities from golf to winter sports, it’s an easy retreat that feels both modern and timeless.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Heights House Hotel in Raleigh
ld.description: Completed in 1860 to designs by British architect William Percival for William Montfort Boylan, this Italianate mansion on the highest point of what is now the Boylan Heights neighborhood is one of the few pre-Civil War houses still standing in Raleigh. The nine ensuite rooms go from standard queens to a sprawling Honeymoon Suite, all fitted out in a "Modern Victorian" register: four-poster beds, working fireplaces, parquet floors, and contemporary furniture that keeps the 20-inch brick walls and ornate plasterwork from tipping into pastiche. The house also functions as a private event venue, with over 10,000 square feet of space across the library, drawing room, dining room, and grounds.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Resort Oahu at Ko Olina

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Oahu at Ko Olina in Rest of Island of Oahu
ld.description: Ko Olina means "place of joy" in Hawaiian, and the Four Seasons here earns that association. Set on the calm, sun-drenched Leeward Coast, a world away from Waikiki's crowds, the resort faces a sheltered lagoon with the Wai'anae Mountains rising behind it. Dolphin pods pass close enough from the oceanfront balconies to make evening plans negotiable. The Naupaka Spa runs fourteen treatment rooms, the kids' club is one of the better ones in the Four Seasons portfolio, and Michael Mina's seafood restaurant alone justifies the flight to Oahu.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets up to 25llbs are allowed, however please be aware of Hawaii's four month pet quarantine requirement.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Boulevard Inn in Richmond
ld.description: The Boulevard Inn occupies a 1914 Colonial Revival townhouse in Richmond’s Fan District, placing guests within easy reach of the neighborhood’s restaurants, galleries, and leafy avenues. Inside, the inn’s handful of rooms balance period character: high ceilings, detailed woodwork, and antique touches, with a straightforward, modern comfort. Owners Mitch and Roni bring hospitality backgrounds from New York and Puerto Rico, and their presence shapes the experience: a personal welcome, a daily European-style breakfast, and an atmosphere that feels genuinely connected to the house’s history.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Emma in San Antonio Area
ld.description: Roman and Williams, the fastidious geniuses behind New York’s High Line and Ace Hotel, nearly carry the entire industrial-chic trend by themselves, curating and exposing and repurposing with no apparent end in sight. And what a lucky find they have here: Pearl’s, a 19th-century brewery and one of the nation’s finest examples of Second Empire architecture. Now it’s the centerpiece of a sprawling, restored riverside gustatory complex with no less than 15 big-name restaurants, a Culinary Institute of America, and two farmers markets a week. Including, of course, Hotel Emma.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Sophie's Gasthaus in San Antonio Area
ld.description: The German enclave of New Braunfels, on the fringes of San Antonio, is the setting for Sophie’s Gasthaus, a 1906 mansion that is now, after a significant restoration at the hands of its new owner, a luxury boutique inn and events venue quite unlike anything in town. At its root, it’s as old-fashioned as hospitality can get: just a lovely house with a character all its own, backed up by service that’s both friendly and professional.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Bo in San Cristóbal de las Casas
ld.description: San Cristóbal de las Casas is nestled in a picturesque valley near Mayan archaeological zones, and its Spanish Colonial heart is bursting with Baroque churches and Neoclassical buildings. Throw in a dash of Moorish influence and, more recently, the Zapatistas, and you’ve got a heady historical brew. Hotel BO distills the cultural elements that have been in flux here for centuries, while at the same time paying tribute to the elements that shape the landscape — water, fire, air and earth.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Orli La Jolla in San Diego
ld.description: Set in the charming seaside town of La Jolla, mere steps from museums, shops, and cafes, Orli offers something different. It’s a respite from the everyday, where guests take their pick from a handful of elegantly designed rooms in a carefully restored historic landmark home designed by architect Irving Gill. There is a distinct residential feel here, where guests feel they have the run of the place (and service is contactless). Borrow a book from the curated collection, pour yourself a brew, and kick back under the olive trees in the courtyard.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The LaFayette Hotel and Club in San Diego
ld.description: San Diego’s iconic Lafayette Hotel hosted the likes of Frank Sinatra and Ava Gardner during its mid-century heyday. And after stints as an office building, radio station, and movie set — a memorable scene from Top Gun was filmed here — it’s experiencing its second golden age. The property was renovated by a local hospitality group that runs some of the city’s most stylish bars and restaurants, and reopened its doors in 2023 as the Lafayette Hotel & Club, an urban resort steeped in retro glamour and celebrated for its gourmet food and drinks.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: 1 Hotel San Francisco in San Francisco Bay Area
ld.description: It wasn’t the first, but there’s perhaps no more natural home for the 1 Hotels group than San Francisco — the waterfront Embarcadero district is the perfect place for such a stylish, sustainable, and luxurious hotel. This specific address is perfect, right by the Ferry Building with easy access to the Financial District and the rest of the compact city center. And the hotel itself is an inspired mix of urban-rustic style and comforts that are luxe without feeling ostentatious. Terrene, the hotel’s versatile restaurant, is a fine introduction to modern Californian farm-to-table cooking (and modern Californian wines).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cavallo Point Lodge in San Francisco Bay Area
ld.description: San Francisco Bay and its environs offer a wealth of swanky lodging options, and there’s a lot of variety, from urban Union Square to pastoral Napa Valley. However, that famous, shimmering bay can act as something of a moat — meaning you’e either in San Francisco or you’re quite a ways out of it. The Lodge at Cavallo Point solves this dilemma by embracing that very juxtaposition.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Up to two dogs are allowed per room. There is a $150 non-refundable pet fee per room per stay.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco at Embarcadero

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco at Embarcadero in San Francisco Bay Area
ld.description: There are still some places in San Francisco where a hoodie doesn’t quite cut it as formal wear. The second Four Seasons hotel in town is the Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco at Embarcadero, and it occupies the top floors of the 345 California Center. It’s satisfyingly high-end and impressively full of modern and contemporary art — and the views of the near skyline and the distant Golden Gate Bridge are spectacular. Many of the iconic sights are close at hand, from North Beach and Jackson Square to the foodie destination that is the Ferry Building; the hotel’s own flagship restaurant, Orafo, is a destination unto itself.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Drisco in San Francisco Bay Area
ld.description: While the area in and around the downtown district is in full-on high-tech boomtown mode, there are fewer and fewer places where you can get in touch with the classic elegance of old Victorian San Francisco. Pacific Heights, however, is still Pacific Heights, a tony hilltop residential district whose streets are lined with century-old mansions with views over the Marina towards Alcatraz and the Golden Gate. This is where you’ll find Hotel Drisco, a longtime local favorite and a fine option for visitors who want to see how the other half of San Francisco lives.
ld.petsAllowed: Pet Policy: We welcome service animals in compliance with federal, state and local laws, however pets are not permitted in the hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Battery in San Francisco Bay Area
ld.description: If you’re expecting a private member’s club in today’s San Francisco to be a sort of ping-pong playground full of app-pitching tech hucksters, then you’ll be very pleasantly surprised by The Battery. And if the vibe, which is dark, moody, and bohemian, is more Hellfire Club than boys’ club, then so much the better. The only way into the club is by nomination and acceptance by the board — or by reservation, which earns you one of 14 stylish, tastefully luxurious suites and rooms (and makes you a Resident Member for the duration of your stay.).
ld.petsAllowed: The Battery warmly welcomes service animals as is required by federal law. We do not allow comfort animals, however. Dogs, pets, and other animals, trained or untrained, whose sole function is to provide comfort, companionship, or emotional support do not qualify as service animals under the law.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel San Luis Obispo in San Luis Obispo
ld.description: Picture the ideal California coastal destination and you might picture a place like San Luis Obispo. Nestled just about midway between Los Angeles and San Francisco, this smallish city offers laid-back, beachy relaxation while also offering plenty to explore and see, at a decidedly non-urban pace. (SLO doesn’t call itself “SloCal” for nothing.) Enter Hotel San Luis Obispo, a boutique hotel that’s equally suited as a home base for exploring or as a sanctuary for a private getaway.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: San Luis Creek Lodge in San Luis Obispo
ld.description: To call it a bed and breakfast would be accurate, but frankly wouldn’t do it justice. San Luis Creek Lodge combines an intimate, low-key residential-style concept with the kind of design you typically only find in a proper luxury boutique hotel. And with 25 rooms divided among three distinct buildings, it’s larger and more varied than the typical B&B. The setting, right in the heart of San Luis Obispo, is as convenient as it gets, but of course this charming town is no great metropolis — here the heart of town is still a perfectly relaxing place to be.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed for a one time fee of $75.00 plus tax.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Salida Real a Querétaro 168, Zona Centro

ld.name: Hotel Amatte in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: The design-centric Amatte is set on a hill overlooking the vibrant artist community of San Miguel de Allende. While the city is beloved for its colonial architecture, this sleek boho-chic resort pivots ever so slightly, blending hints of that legacy (spy the arched columns by the pool) with a textured modern design that evokes the Mediterranean. From the studio rooms to the villas, the design sensibility remains consistent with design details like basket chandeliers and earth tones. Edible and flower gardens complete the serene picture, while the rooftop restaurant and bars liven things up.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Casa 1810 Hotel Boutique in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: Housed in an imposing, historic colonial building, Casa 1810 sets the tone for an idyllic stay in one of Mexico’s most charming towns. Inspired by the Alhambra fortress in Granada, Spain, rooms feature vaulted ceilings, stone parquet floors, loom-woven rugs, antique wooden headboards. And even though it’s got a popular, celebrated restaurant, the hotel achieves a romantic, quiet atmosphere. Guests can take in the sunset from the rooftop bar or enjoy a cooked-to-order breakfast in the peaceful interior courtyard. A location in the center of San Miguel de Allende means the hotel’s street is closed to cars on weekends. Many of the city’s top attractions, including the famous Parroquia de San Miguel Arcangel and San Miguel de Allende Historical Museum, are less than a 5-minute walk away.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Casa de Sierra Nevada, A Belmond Hotel, San Miguel de Allende

ld.name: Casa de Sierra Nevada, A Belmond Hotel, San Miguel de Allende in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: The quietly stylish Mexican town of San Miguel de Allende is the perfect setting for a classic refuge like the Belmond Casa de Sierra Nevada, equal parts 16th-century residence and modern luxury boutique hotel. The level of service is high, as professional as it is warm, and the hotel’s old-world charm is always allowed to shine through.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Casa Hoyos - Hotel Boutique in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: It’s not the only boutique hotel in Mexico that’s fashioned out of a Spanish colonial mansion, complete with an Andalusian-style patio and colorful tilework. But San Miguel de Allende’s Casa Hoyos is delightfully one-of-a-kind. Inspired by Julián Hoyos, a Spaniard who snapped up the property in 1938, the décor is colorful, vibrant, and full of character. Aside from the hand-painted mural of the Virgin Mary that looks solemnly over the archways of the modernist courtyard, the look is whimsical and nostalgic, filled with cheerful greenery and eclectic design pieces.
ld.petsAllowed: Small dogs are allowed but only specific small breeds. If you are traveling with your pet, please contact cs@tablethotels.com to verify if the hotel can accommodate your loved one.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Casa Blanca 7 in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: On the San Miguel de Allende hospitality scene, low-key and residential is the name of the game. The modest size of its finest hotels means there’s always room for one more exquisite example, and Casa Blanca 7 fits the bill. It’s a 300-year-old house in the city’s Spanish Colonial historic center, and as its name might suggest, it’s got a touch of Moroccan atmosphere, recalling in a subtle way the ultra-private riad hotels of cities like Casablanca and Marrakech.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Matilda in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: Located in the central Mexican highlands, the peaceful town of San Miguel de Allende enjoys a well-deserved reputation as a relaxing yet cosmopolitan destination. A longtime home for young artists on the rise and expatriates of all ages, it’s the kind of place that’s full of chic throwbacks to the Spanish Colonial aesthetic. Opened in late 2010, Hotel Matilda bucks the local trend by hewing closer to the design of a big-city boutique while still paying homage to San Miguel’s artistic heritage.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: L'Ôtel - Casa Arca in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: San Miguel de Allende: this once-sleepy colonial masterpiece has become a mecca for foodies and the Instagram set alike (just take one look at the colorful facades and cobblestone streets — we defy you to leave your smartphone or camera at home). Just about 150 miles outside Mexico City, a healthy expat contingent has turned San Miguel de Allende into one of Mexico’s most cosmopolitan cities. And in the very heart of town — a UNESCO World Heritage site, no less — sits the L'Ôtel at Dôce18 Concept House.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Maison Mexique in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: The city of San Miguel de Allende is home to a good number of historic hotels. What makes Maison Mexique special, as the name suggests, is its worldly air; the owners are well-traveled, and the place represents a mélange of cultural influences. Located inside a beautifully restored historic home, this boutique hotel is also grounded in its place, the terracotta walls proudly featuring a collection of paintings and collages by local artists, as well as Mexican graphic prints and black-and-white photographs capturing San Miguel’s history.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood San Miguel de Allende in San Miguel de Allende
ld.description: A luxury resort in one of Mexico’s coastal enclaves would be nothing new, but a hacienda-style hotel in the heart of a historic city center is far from commonplace. The Rosewood San Miguel de Allende is a departure for the Hong Kong–based luxury brand, a detailed reproduction of a grand colonial-style residence, surrounding a lovely central courtyard in the city’s UNESCO-listed old town. And while a lesser hotelier might have been tempted to import their own characteristic aesthetic, here Rosewood wisely opts for a purely local style, leaving its own contributions to the (still essential) areas of comfort, service, and programming.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: El Encanto in Santa Barbara
ld.description: Though physically not all that far from Los Angeles, in terms of atmosphere Santa Barbara could scarcely be more different. Rather than trying to turn it into some Hollywood satellite, smart hoteliers embrace the essential sleepiness of Santa Barbara — and the proprietors of El Encanto, by this definition, certainly qualify as smart.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Miramar Beach in Santa Barbara
ld.description: The Rosewood Miramar Beach refers to this stretch of coastline, just to the east of Santa Barbara, as the “American Riviera,” and from within this sparkling new luxury resort it’s easy to see where they’re coming from — there’s more than a touch of Art Deco in the décor, and the south-facing beach is nothing if not idyllic. Rooms and suites, whether in the gardens or on the beach, are stylish, spacious, and exceedingly well-equipped, and the facilities are exhaustive: a Sense spa, a fitness studio with a variety of classes, a pair of swimming pools, and even some retail shops, including one from Gwyneth Paltrow’s Goop brand. Two restaurants, three bars, and an ice cream shop complete the package; if you can’t find relaxation here, it’s not the Rosewood’s fault.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets allowed for an extra charge of USD 150 per pet, per stay. Service animals are welcome, and are exempt from fees. Food and water bowls are available

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: San Ysidro Ranch in Santa Barbara
ld.description: This spot on the outskirts of Santa Barbara hasn’t been a ranch, strictly speaking, for quite some time, unless one considers rustling up the likes of Audrey Hepburn, Winston Churchill and John and Jackie Kennedy (not all at the same time, mind) to be a traditional ranching activity. San Ysidro Ranch, these days, is more like what might have once been called a health farm, albeit an exceedingly luxurious one.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: La Bahia Hotel & Spa in Santa Cruz
ld.description: Santa Cruz, California’s hospitality scene took a decisive step in an upscale direction with the opening of La Bahia Hotel & Spa. This substantial Spanish Mediterranean structure is set right on the self-explanatory Beach Street, and occupies a sprawling 1926 apartment complex complete with a landmark bell tower. Today, a century later, it’s by a considerable distance the most luxurious hotel in town, and a popular gathering place, as these things ought to be, for Santa Cruz locals as well.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets (Dogs and Cats) are permitted with a $175.00 per pet, per stay fee. Maximum of two (2) pets per room. Learn more

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Inn of the Anasazi in Santa Fe
ld.description: Rosewood Inn of the Anasazi is just about as central as a Santa Fe hotel can get, but that doesn’t mean it feels urban. This town’s compact, low-rise, walkable center never gets all that busy, and the Inn’s traditional pueblo-style construction lends it an extra measure of privacy. From its birth as an independent hotel, the Inn of the Anasazi — named for the ancient civilization that built the region’s distinctive cliff dwellings — was meant to offer an unusually authentic and culturally sensitive New Mexican experience. And now that Rosewood is involved, it’s also a thoroughly first-rate luxury hotel, bringing to bear the brand’s decades of global experience.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Inn at Mattei's Tavern, Auberge Collection

ld.name: The Inn at Mattei's Tavern, Auberge Collection in Santa Ynez Valley
ld.description: The Inn at Mattei’s Tavern has been a fixture in the Santa Ynez Valley wine-country town of Los Olivos since as far back as the 1880s. Safe to say, though, that in its original form it was a shade or two less luxurious than it is now, under the direction of Auberge Collection. It comes by its retro vibe honestly, in other words, but alongside its historic charms you’ll find all the trappings of a modern Californian luxury resort.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bellwether House in Savannah
ld.description: Savannah’s Bellwether House is, strictly speaking, a bed and breakfast, but the lodging that lies within its twin 19th-century Italianate houses exceeds what’s ordinarily expected of a B&B. Its 16 rooms are impressive — they vary widely in size, but all are luxuriously outfitted, and designed in a modern-classic style that adapts antique elements to contemporary use. A unique Indian-accented breakfast is indeed just about the extent of the food and beverage service; it’s followed up by afternoon tea and, around sunset, a full bar whose opening is heralded by a ceremonial bottle of Champagne — opened with a saber, no less.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Bardo Savannah in Savannah
ld.description: Quite a lot of the appeal of the American South lies in its attachment to history and tradition. But there’s room for a little creativity. While other Southern mansion hotels feel dry and airless, preserved in amber, Hotel Bardo Savannah is a fantasy — behind the walls of this treasured 19th-century Victorian mansion is a hotel that’s caught between two worlds: the tranquil seclusion of a resort and the convivial bustle of a private members’ club.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Perry Lane Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Savannah

ld.name: Perry Lane Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Savannah in Savannah
ld.description: Savannah, Georgia is a town that’s incredibly rich in history, and if you arrive expecting to be put up in some grand plantation-style mansion, you’re not completely out of line. You might be surprised by Perry Lane Hotel, however; this Luxury Collection establishment contains plenty of references to Savannah’s aesthetic heritage, but it’s unmistakably contemporary, both in its architecture and in its approach to high-end hospitality.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Douglas in Savannah
ld.description: A beautifully restored 1850s townhouse in the Historic District is now one of the city’s finest small hotels, a 16-room boutique that presents a fresh and eclectic perspective on Savannah’s unique aesthetic character. The restoration took some liberties with historical correctness, to inspired effect — the designers sourced antique furniture and retro decorative elements from multiple eras and geographic sources. The vibe is residential, but more hotel than guest house, featuring a hearty breakfast and a bar and lounge that serves light bites as well as drinks; the location means exploring Savannah on foot is an easy matter.
ld.petsAllowed: \n No pets allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Resort Scottsdale at Troon North

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Scottsdale at Troon North in Scottsdale Phoenix
ld.description: In most of Phoenix, including much of Scottsdale, the desert landscape is a remote abstraction. Not so at the Four Seasons. The location, at the fringe of this sprawling urban area, backs right up against a national forest, which provides the resort with a wild mountain backdrop.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets 30 lbs and under are allowed. Maximum 2 pets per room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mountain Shadows Resort Scottsdale in Scottsdale Phoenix
ld.description: Half a century ago the original Mountain Shadows, in the suburbs of Phoenix, Arizona, was a swanky Rat Pack hideaway, during the heyday of Southwestern glamour, when overseas travel was still rare and stars from Hollywood vacationed in Palm Springs and Scottsdale. The new Mountain Shadows isn’t so much a rehabilitation or a renovation — the original was almost entirely leveled some years ago — as a total reboot, a reimagining of what a contemporary Paradise Valley luxury resort ought to look like.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Royal Palms Resort and Spa in Scottsdale Phoenix
ld.description: Sitting at the foot of Camelback Mountain, with an entrance edged by rows of soaring palm trees, the Royal Palms Resort and Spa creates a striking impression from the moment of arrival. The Spanish colonial mansion, built in 1929 by a nephew of J.P. Morgan, stands in sharp contrast to the bland, corporate architecture that dominates the Phoenix area’s plentiful chain hotels. Here, idiosyncratic touches like Oriental rugs and deep, vibrant colors defy the usual pastel Southwesternisms, making Royal Palms feel as much like a private residence as a resort.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Global Ambassador in Scottsdale Phoenix
ld.description: Hospitality veterans might not expect much from the partnership between an NBA star, a former football player, a country music legend, and a hit-making restaurateur, but in fact the Global Ambassador is a strong entry into the Phoenix luxury-hotel scene. All the details have been carefully considered here, especially in the 141 rooms and suites, whose Art Deco inspiration is enhanced by hand-selected Maison Plage books and distinctive artwork. Five restaurants serve as the heartbeat of the resort, and range across the globe for inspiration, while the spa is both cutting-edge and comprehensive in its fitness and wellness offerings.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: 1 Hotel Seattle in Seattle
ld.description: Upon its advent the 1 Hotels brand quickly established what feels like a whole new category: the sustainable luxury hotel. It’s a good fit for a city as green as Seattle, and 1 Hotel Seattle stands right in the high-tech heart of the city, straddling the border between Downtown and South Lake Union.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Lotte Hotel Seattle in Seattle
ld.description: Lotte Hotels and Resorts is a new name in the United States, but this Korean brand looks perfectly at home in downtown Seattle. Lotte Seattle begins with a local landmark, the 1908 Beaux-Arts Sanctuary, formerly a Methodist church — but the bulk of the hotel is found up above, occupying 16 floors of a modern glass tower that stands over the original church building.
ld.petsAllowed: \n A pet fee of $100 per stay applies for dogs 40 pounds and under.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Populus Seattle in Seattle
ld.description: A 1907 building in Pioneer Square, the city’s oldest and most historic neighborhood, is the setting for Populus Seattle, the second “carbon-positive” hotel in the United States. (The first was Populus Denver.) This means not just conservation measures like adaptive-reuse construction and a pedestrian-friendly location, but active measures like planting a tree for every hotel stay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Lodge at St. Edward Park

ld.name: The Lodge at St. Edward Park in Seattle
ld.description: St. Edward State Park is an unusual thing: more than 300 acres of lakeside forest, feeling for all the world like a far-flung rural escape, yet situated very much within the greater Seattle metropolitan area. And the Lodge at St. Edward State Park is equally unusual: a one-time seminary designed by an eminent local architect, now renovated and transformed into a historically aware and uniquely atmospheric luxury boutique hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Ambiente, A Landscape Hotel in Sedona
ld.description: As desert landscapes go, it’s hard to beat the spectacular red rocks of Sedona. No wonder Ambiente goes out of its way to credit the landscape. Conservation and preservation are at the core of the hotel’s mission, which is to combine unfettered luxury with proximity to nature — it doesn’t get much closer than the 180-degree views afforded by the wrap-around floor-to-ceiling windows.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are welcome, but will require at $250 charge to your credit card for deep cleaning upon your departure.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: El Portal in Sedona
ld.description: Just two hours to the north of Phoenix is an entirely different Arizona, a landscape of pine trees and dramatic red cliffs and the more hospitable climate of the high desert, which at four thousand feet above sea level remains ten degrees cooler than Phoenix at its hottest. This is no sprawling metropolis, either; Sedona is a small town, yet surprisingly cosmopolitan, with a thriving arts scene and some of Arizona’s biggest and best resorts.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Sand Hill in Silicon Valley
ld.description: Silicon Valley, the distributed high-tech capital of the United States has never had the caliber of hotels you’d expect from an actual capital city, but the Rosewood Sand Hill goes a long way toward rectifying the situation. It’s a resort-style hotel with a sprawling pool deck, a high-end Sense spa, and access to a wealth of outdoor recreation in the Santa Cruz mountains. Rooms are stylish, more urbane than rustic, and with their expansive spaces and top-shelf comforts they’re a good match for one of the most expensive neighborhoods in the country; meanwhile the suites are extraordinary, and the villas are the stuff of tech-baron daydreams.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Collector - Luxury Inn & Gardens in St. Augustine
ld.description: You might think the oldest city in America would be somewhere in the vicinity of Plymouth Rock, but you’d be wrong. St. Augustine was the capital of Spanish Florida long before the Mayflower arrived. And by those standards, the lovingly restored homes that make up The Collector Luxury Inn & Gardens are relative newcomers — it’s not every day in the United States that you can sleep in a structure that dates back to the 1790s.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Alpine Falls Ranch in Superior
ld.description: The mountainous western edge of Montana isn’t a place where edgy urban-inspired modern design makes a lot of sense. But fortunately there’s more than one way to design an extraordinary hotel. Alpine Falls Ranch takes the classic mountain-lodge aesthetic that its name implies and simply executes it with commitment, with verve, and with a rare tastefulness. The landscape, after all, is the real star of this show, and the best approach a hotel can take is to complement it rather than distract from it.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Palihouse Hyde Park Village in Tampa
ld.description: The Palisociety hotels may have been born in California, but the brand’s colorful, eclectic, European-influenced style travels remarkably well; while Palihouse Hyde Park Village bears an obvious family resemblance to the other hotels of the same name, it looks perfectly at home on the Gulf Coast of Florida. Hyde Park is an upscale residential district just across the river from downtown Tampa, and Hyde Park Village is an open-air mixed-use development with shops, restaurants, and, thanks to Palisociety, a remarkably stylish boutique hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Lumière by Dunton in Telluride
ld.description: It may still be the most charmingly low-key of Colorado’s major ski resort towns, but that doesn’t mean Telluride hasn’t gone upscale; it’s just that it’s done it in a charmingly low-key way. Lumière with Inspirato combines boutique-hotel good looks with distinctly residential comforts, and its position in the enclave of Mountain Village affords a measure of seclusion from the town, as well as ski-in/ski-out access to the famous slopes.
ld.petsAllowed: A surcharge of $30 per pet, per day will be applied and a $75 departure cleaning fee.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Madeline Hotel & Residences, Auberge Collection in Telluride
ld.description: Telluride, once the quirky cousin of the big-time Colorado resort towns, has now well and truly hit the big time itself — for evidence, look no further than the Hotel Madeline Telluride, a luxury resort that’s very much in the same league as the big five-star hotels of Aspen or Vail. Not to say that Telluride feels like Aspen, not yet — but any thoughts of a rough ride are dispelled immediately upon check-in.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Amomoxtli in Tepoztlán
ld.description: For too long Mexican travel, for overseas visitors, meant nothing but sun, sand, and surf. In the boutique-hotel era, however, there are opportunities for all kinds of destinations to shine. Among them is Tepoztlán, a mountain town near Mexico City that’s known for its significance in Aztec history and culture — as well as the ruins of the nearby El Tepozteco temple, and the national park that surrounds it. And with the advent of Amomoxtli, the region’s first high-end luxury boutique hotel, it’s a destination that’s set to welcome a new crop of international travelers.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Canoe Place Inn & Cottages in The Hamptons / Montauk
ld.description: Canoe Place Inn sprawls across Hampton Bays with historic inn rooms, garden cottages tucked into a hillside, and waterfront residences across the canal. The property balances ancient architecture with contemporary updates: bright spaces, modern amenities, and a layout for both quiet getaways and group gatherings. Good Ground Tavern, operated by Union Square Events in its first Hamptons venture, centers on seasonal American cooking prepared over a Cherrywood grill. The dining room shifts easily between casual happy hours and private celebrations. Hampton Bays gets a proper destination stay, combining history with East End polish.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Faraway Sag Harbor in The Hamptons / Montauk
ld.description: Please note: Faraway Sag Harbor is accepting reservations from June 2026 onward.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Desierto Azul in Todos Santos
ld.description: First came the surfers, then the official distinction as one of Mexico’s Pueblos Mágicos, and finally, a wave of designers, chefs, and hoteliers, turning the once-quiet beach village of Todos Santos into a hip getaway on the Baja California peninsula. Among the numerous style-conscious lodgings on offer is Desierto Azul, a petite boutique hotel on a sun-baked stretch of land a few blocks back from the coastline.
ld.petsAllowed: \n No pets are allowed at the property.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel San Cristóbal in Todos Santos
ld.description: Bunkhouse, the Austin-based hotel group responsible for most of the best hotels in Texas, has finally set its sights beyond the borders of the Lone Star State. Just how far beyond, however, might come as something of a surprise. Hotel San Cristóbal sets up shop in Todos Santos, on the Pacific coast of Mexico’s Baja California. This is a town that’s in the midst of making that familiar transition from fishing village to bohemian getaway to emerging tourist destination — and the San Cristóbal catches it at just the right time, as the first wave is beginning to crest.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Well-behaved pets are always welcome at Hotel San Cristóbal Baja. There is a $25 fee per day per pet (before taxes); please advise the front desk. Dogs must be on a leash at all times.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Degollado, Carretera Todos Santos - Cabo San Lucas, El Pescadero

ld.name: Paradero Todos Santos – Exclusive Experiences in Todos Santos
ld.description: An hour up the west coast of Baja California from the hedonistic holiday hotspot of Cabo San Lucas is a place whose charms are a little more austere, though spectacular in their own right: Paradero Todos Santos, a luxurious all-suite boutique hotel in a highly disciplined Brutalist style which seeks, at least in part, to draw the eye outward, to the landscape architecture and the untouched surrounding ecosystems.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Todos Santos Boutique Hotel in Todos Santos
ld.description: There’s a lot more to Baja California Sur than Cabo excess. Just an hour or so north is the pueblo mágico of Todos Santos, an artsy town that marries a keen visual sense to laid-back Pacific coastal vibes. The Todos Santos Boutique Hotel, as the name implies, distills the locale’s timeless Jesuit heritage down to an intimate, ten-room affair just off the main drag. Ivy-wreathed brickwork defines the public spaces, giving way in the rooms to an ornate vision in dark wood and gilt-framed mirrors. Each of them even boasts a unique, full-wall mural of a frozen-in-time colonial scene.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa Santa Cruz in Todos Santos
ld.description: There aren’t many places more conducive to getting away from it all than Todos Santos, in Baja California Sur, just an hour up the Pacific coast from Cabo San Lucas. And the primary aim of Villa Santa Cruz is to provide guests with an opportunity to unwind in a style that’s both luxurious and as casual as can be. Its owners, two Calfornia-born couples, started with a single villa, and slowly expanded the hotel’s offerings into what you see today: a second villa, a handful of bungalows and poolside mini-villas, and four tented suites, for maximum communion with the beachfront setting.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: 1 Hotel Toronto in Toronto
ld.description: The same 1 Hotels group responsible for eco-friendly, high-design luxury boutique offerings in New York and Miami have arrived in the upscale neighborhood of King West Village. 1 Hotel Toronto features cutting-edge sustainability measures, ultra-stylish interiors, and a handful of popular restaurants and bars, from the farm-to-table 1 Kitchen to the self-explanatory Harriet’s Rooftop bar. The rooms are surprisingly sunny, and their crisp contemporary design is warmed by plenty of organic textures and living houseplants. Like its sister hotels it’s proof that in boutique hospitality, virtue and pleasure don’t have to be mutually exclusive.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Ace Hotel Toronto in Toronto
ld.description: Ace’s first hotel in Canada is set in Toronto’s Garment District, close to the downtown core and innumerable local attractions. It’s a new build, but one with plenty of vintage inspiration, designed by Shim-Sutcliffe Architects and Atelier Ace. The curvaceous brick, concrete, and wooden forms feel retro-futuristic, and the lobby’s floor, if you look carefully, seems to hover in the air, suspended from the ceiling’s concrete arches by judiciously placed metal rods.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bisha Hotel Toronto in Toronto
ld.description: Tucked between the Fashion District and Old Toronto, the Bisha Hotel is a lively option in one of North America’s most cosmopolitan cities. Each of the hotel’s 96 rooms and suites is thoughtfully designed by either Studio Munge — the renowned Toronto-based firm known for its opulent interior designs — or Kravitz Design, brainchild of Grammy-winning artist Lenny Kravtiz and notable for its elegant interiors with a rock-and-roll edge. Four distinct bars and restaurants range from French Made, a casual take on the Parisian café experience, to KŌST, which offers flavours from the California coastline and the Baja Peninsula, and entices guests to dine at the “top of the world” on the hotel’s 44th floor.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Toronto in Toronto
ld.description: The Four Seasons brand is headquartered in Toronto, so it stands to reason that its Yorkville franchise should be something special. This gleaming glass tower is set in an ideal location, surrounded by many of the best restaurants and shops in this cosmopolitan city. It’s also home to some first-rate French cooking at Café Boulud, as well as a stunning spa and wellness center. Rooms and suites are sunny and quietly stylish, and their substantial luxuries are subtle and tasteful, in classic Four Seasons style. Its real strength, however, is probably its service — as the flagship, it sets the tone for the entire brand.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Up to 2 pets weighing less than 25 pounds are allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Park Hyatt Toronto in Toronto
ld.description: Toronto’s hotel scene may be a bit on the conservative side, with relatively few hip, grungy little boutiques. This isn’t necessarily a bad thing, though. One must be prepared, when in Rome, to do as the Romans do — which, in Toronto’s case, quite probably means trading edginess for luxury, at a place like the Park Hyatt.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Shangri-La Hotel, Toronto in Toronto
ld.description: Toronto is a surprisingly global city, and as such it’s no surprise that it counts a Shangri-La among its best hotels. Asia’s luxury hotels, after all, are the envy of the hospitality world. And despite its location in the center of the financial district, the Shangri-La Toronto feels like a place of refuge from the city outside.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Hazelton Hotel Toronto in Toronto
ld.description: Possibly the most luxe of Toronto’s collection of luxury boutiques, the Hazelton is a sign of the times: both high-design, with interiors by the ubiquitous Canadian firm Yabu Pushelberg, and unashamedly high-end, with suites averaging six hundred square feet and outfitted with all the latest luxury trimmings, from iPod docking stations to heated bathroom floors and flush mirror-mounted television screens. It’s meant to be a modern grand hotel, a contemporary version of what places like the Savoy in London or the Waldorf-Astoria in New York must have once been. And with a little luck that’s exactly what it’ll be.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Toronto in Toronto
ld.description: Though we hesitate to wade into any regional rivalries, we’re comfortable declaring that Toronto is Canada’s biggest, busiest, most cosmopolitan city. It’s only fitting, then, that its top-end luxury hotels should be absolutely first-rate. Among the usual suspects when it comes to this sort of thing is Ritz-Carlton, but the Ritz-Carlton Toronto is an unusual one — the design is rather more modern than you’ll find in more typical examples of this venerable luxury brand, while the top-flight service and faultless comforts you expect are all exactly as they ought to be.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Quintessence in Tremblant
ld.description: The age of the boutique ski hotel is upon us. While the typical North American mountain resort counts rooms by the hundreds, Quintessence, on the shores of Quebec’s Lake Tremblant, numbers just thirty suites — though surely they had space for more, as each spans at least 700 square feet, they went for the ultra-luxury approach.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Canyon Ranch Tucson in Tucson
ld.description: To say that Canyon Ranch Tucson is an all-inclusive spa and wellness resort is a bit like saying the Beatles were a rock band from Liverpool — it’s certainly accurate, but it leaves out both of their central roles in defining their genres, as well as the significance of their continued influence on the form. Founder Mel Zuckerman opened Canyon Ranch Tucson at the tail end of the seventies, seeking to replace the somewhat punitive approach of the health spas of the day with something more positive, more empowering, and more spiritually transformative.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: BE Destination Tulum in Tulum
ld.description: Mexico’s prodigious natural gifts are, in some ways, a mixed blessing.
