So stunning are its miles and miles of raw, idyllic coastline that its hotels have historically found themselves quite able to get by on little more than location alone. That’s changing now, of course; a new generation of impeccably conceived and designed boutique hotels is changing the face of the Mexican hospitality scene — hotels like Be Tulum, to take a not entirely random example. The location, you may have guessed, is Tulum, a small town at the southern end of the Mayan Riviera, on the shores of the Caribbean near Cancún. It’s as heavenly as you’d expect it to be, and Be Tulum knows better than to try to outshine the setting.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Carretera Tulum a Boca Paila Km 8.2, Ejido Pino Suarez, 77780 Tulum

ld.name: La Zebra in Tulum
ld.description: Barefoot beach living underpins the laidback style of La Zebra Tulum, where all the suites and casitas sit right on the sands for waking up to a sweeping sea view. The relaxed restaurant and beach bar serve up Mexican flavors and fresh seasonal ingredients, complemented by signature cocktails and local artisanal beers and wines. And whilst the beach is a natural playground for kids, La Zebra has plenty of activities planned to keep them entertained, including learning about Mexican corn to make tortillas and guacamole, craft workshops and piñata parties.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: MILAM in Tulum
ld.description: Unusually for these parts, MILAM sits not in the beachfront resort district but more or less on the edge of the city, where, presumably, such a high-concept, high-design hotel village feels right at home. The name — a reference to tantric “dream yoga” — says it all, channeled via the sinuous organic forms, whimsical lighting, and dramatic design gestures in full flower throughout the property. The rooms are dreamier still, each an indoor-outdoor exercise in psychedelic plaster with local clay and macrame accents. The rest is up to you, dreamwalker: yoga under a traditional palapa roof? Self-care at the spa? Swim-up drinks? Or all three?

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: NABOA Hotel Tulum in Tulum
ld.description: At this late date it takes something special to stand out in boutique-hotel-saturated Tulum, but NABOA Hotel Tulum has what it takes. While many local lodgings have luxe aspirations, the experience here is authentically high-end. It’s also authentically local — architects Jaque Studio combined traditional materials and craftsmanship with contemporary clean lines and modernist-inspired simplicity.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Carretera Tulum - Boca Paila Km. 10, 77780 Tulum Beach

ld.name: Sana Tulum in Tulum
ld.description: You’d think you were in Morocco rather than Mexico upon stepping inside Sana Tulum. The adults-only, riad-style hotel places beach view rooms around a central leafy courtyard, and each space is decorated with Moroccan-inspired wooden arches, motifs, and golden lanterns. The restaurant takes you to the Mediterranean with Greek and Italian dishes married with Mexican produce, and drinks and snacks are also served up on the rooftop by the Moroccan-tiled swimming pool, and at Layla Beach Club, right outside the hotel. The wellness offering comprises a varied mix of beach yoga sessions, jiu-jitsu classes, ice baths, and sound healing, as well as relaxing massages.
ld.petsAllowed: No pets allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Wakax Hacienda - Cenote & Boutique Hotel in Tulum
ld.description: Lots of travelers choose Tulum for its beautiful beaches and festive nightlife. Slightly inland, set apart from the hip village center, Wakax Hacienda taps into some of the region’s other assets — namely its Mayan history, its lush jungle setting, and a network of cenotes, or limestone sinkholes fed by underground rivers. The hotel is strategically positioned right beside a trio of cenotes, and easy access to these ethereal, turquoise-hued, all-natural swimming pools is reason enough to stay.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Vail in Vail
ld.description: When the Four Seasons Vail opened its doors, the greatest surprise was the fact that it hadn’t been there all along. So perfect a summation is it of this upscale Colorado ski town that it’s fair to say now that it’s here, Vail is just as it was before, only more so.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sonnenalp Hotel in Vail
ld.description: The idea of Bavaria in the Rockies may raise eyebrows, but it’s no gimmick — this remarkably authentic Alpine-style resort is owned by the same Faessler family that opened the original Sonnenalp hotel in Ofterschwang in the years immediately following the First World War. It’s the sort of personality that no contemporary designer could possibly fake: almost more European than its counterparts in the Alps, it’s the perfect antidote to the commercial luxury on offer elsewhere in Vail.
ld.petsAllowed: The Sonnenalp Hotel is a pet free and smoke free environment.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Clayoquot Wilderness Lodge in Vancouver Island
ld.description: Set on the rugged Pacific coast of Vancouver Island, reachable only by boat or seaplane, Clayoquot Wilderness Lodge is certainly secluded. But life here is far from primitive. Guests come to Clayoquot to immerse themselves in nature while also treating themselves to more than a little bit of unpretentious luxury.
ld.petsAllowed: Due to the surrounding wildlife guests are asked to leave their pets at home. There are many dogs onsite to keep you company, who have been trained to be comfortable and not disturb the bears and other wildlife.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Fairmont Empress Hotel in Vancouver Island
ld.description: Despite its island location, Victoria has its own version of the railway-style grand hotels that span Canada from coast to coast. It’s patterned after the French-style Chateau Frontenac in Quebec City, but in this most English of Canadian cities it’s got an identity all its own — after all these years (and after a thorough 2017 renovation) it’s still the most luxurious hotel in town, and its position facing the Inner Harbour makes it an unmissable landmark and a fixture in Victoria’s downtown city life. Make time for afternoon tea, served on china given to the Empress by the Queen herself in 1939.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Magnolia Hotel & Spa in Vancouver Island
ld.description: It’s only a century and a half old, but this town goes out of its way to show its age. Fans of modern architecture and towers in green glass will feel more at home in mainland Vancouver — Victoria, on Vancouver Island, is something of a throwback to the era with which it shares its name, the sort of place that puts the British back in British Columbia. And a block from the scenic Inner Harbour is the Magnolia Hotel & Spa, a lodging that, for all its newness, is equally at home in the 21st century and the 19th — which means that, for this timeless town, it’s perfectly contemporary.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Wickaninnish Inn in Vancouver Island
ld.description: By now the staggering natural beauty of British Columbia’s Pacific coast is something of an open secret — and it’s hard to think of a place more spectacular than the west coast of Vancouver Island, where the Wickaninnish Inn sits between a lush old-growth forest and a mile-long beach, just minutes from the township of Tofino yet remote enough to feel like the edge of the world.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Loden Hotel in Vancouver
ld.description: Many hotels in Vancouver can boast breathtaking views — this town is nothing if not topographically gifted. However, the district of Coal Harbour on the north edge of downtown has a slight edge on the rest. Think of it as stadium seating for the panorama that unfolds across the Burrard Inlet. Coal Harbour itself is a tony spot well worth an evening stroll; recently redeveloped with parks and a marina, the neighborhood boasts a sophisticated collection of towers with a level of design not commonly found in North American cities, and in one of these sleek glass towers you’ll find the Loden Hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Hotel Georgia in Vancouver
ld.description: The film business in Vancouver is booming. Which is why it’s surprising, and a delight, to realize that a landmark hotel like the Rosewood Hotel Georgia — then simply the Hotel Georgia — hosted the likes of Laurence Olivier and John Wayne. Marlene Dietrich showed up at reception with an entourage and forty suitcases. Bing Crosby slept here, as did Elvis, and Nat King Cole, and Frank Sinatra, and the Rolling Stones. Katharine Hepburn, who dined in the privacy of her room and, of course, only wore pants, reportedly introduced the very concept of “room service” to the hotel, and singlehandedly modified the ladies’ dress code.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Wedgewood in Vancouver
ld.description: Unlike many of Vancouver’s hotels, the Wedgewood is a privately owned boutique, decorated and still overseen by the daughters of its original founder, a Greek-born Vancouver businesswoman. And in contrast to the city’s modern business hotels, this place is all European-style pomp and old-world elegance, beginning with the antique furnishings, Persian rugs, and carved stone desk of the reception.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Inn at Little Washington in Washington
ld.description: It may come as something of a surprise to discover that seventy miles to the west of the nation’s capital, in sleepy Washington, Virginia, there’s a small country inn (remarkable enough in its own right) with a restaurant to rival any in America. This is the sort of place where the guest rooms, however splendid, will always get second billing, serving primarily to lodge those diners who have made the culinary pilgrimage to Patrick O’Connell’s award-winning restaurant.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Mayflower Inn & Spa, Auberge Collection in Washington
ld.description: Sure, it’s been a couple of centuries, but every now and then you’re reminded that it’s called New England for a reason. For in spite of its most American of names, the Mayflower Inn & Spa, in the Litchfield Hills of northwestern Connecticut, is as close as you’ll get to an English country-house hotel experience this side of the Atlantic. Set amid wooded grounds and finely cultivated gardens, this gorgeous old house is a remarkably idyllic slice of country life, just two hours from New York City; and once inside, you’ll find the resemblance even more pronounced: this is a hotel that’s perfectly dedicated to the kind of effortless poshness that the best English country hotels make their specialty.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Eaton DC in Washington D.C.
ld.description: We’re finally going to make it all the way through the description of a Washington, D.C. hotel without any wisecracks about the capital’s aesthetic conservatism. The Eaton Hotel is impervious to that line of criticism — this isn’t just the hippest hotel in Washington, but one of the most impressive new boutique hotels in America, and it’s thanks in large part to the fact that its founder, Katharine Lo, isn’t given to half-measures.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: 2401 M Street Northwest, Fairmont Gold Floor

ld.name: Fairmont Washington DC Gold Experience in Washington D.C.
ld.description: Located within easy walking distance of some of Georgetown’s most famous and historic monuments, Fairmont Washington DC makes a comfortable base for exploring the city. Rooms and suites are spacious and there’s a restaurant, lobby lounge and bar to come back to after a day’s sightseeing. But it’s the comprehensive wellbeing offering that really stands out, with a three-floor space filled with gym equipment, fitness classes, a 50-foot saltwater pool, a steam room, sauna and whirlpool. The hotel even has its own dog, Georgie, for guests in need of a mood-boosting cuddle.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pendry Washington DC – The Wharf in Washington D.C.
ld.description: Physically, it’s not all that far from Capitol Hill, but in terms of its aesthetics and its atmosphere, the Pendry Washington DC - The Wharf presents a completely different side of the nation’s capital. It’s clear from a glance at its ultra-modern façade that this is no ordinary luxury hotel, and its setting on the waterfront lends it an escapist aspect as well. This, of course, is the sort of thing you can expect from Pendry’s parent company, Montage, a hotel group that’s practically synonymous with luxe-but-hip destination-driven resorts.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Riggs Washington DC in Washington D.C.
ld.description: It’s not every day a 19th-century Romanesque Revival bank building in Washington’s Penn Quarter district reopens as a hotel, especially one as stylish as Riggs. It’s another sign of a new era for the nation’s capital — there’s more character here than in all of D.C.’s hotels circa 2000 put together. It starts with the well-preserved bones of the stately old bank, but this is no mere restoration — they’ve taken liberties, using the city’s history as their inspiration, and the result adds a welcome note of playfulness to the elegance you expect from a Washington D.C. luxury hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed under 35 lbs, charges apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Washington, D.C. in Washington D.C.
ld.description: For visitors to Washington, D.C.’s Georgetown neighborhood, high-end accommodations have long been provided by the usual suspects — namely the Four Seasons, the Ritz-Carlton, and a few other reliable luxury brands. For an experience that’s smaller in scale, but similarly high in standards, there’s a newer option: Rosewood Washington D.C., on the banks of the C&O Canal, whose 37 rooms, 12 suites, and eight townhouses show the influence of modern boutique-hotel hospitality, adapted for a luxury-hotel clientele.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. A 100 USD deposit is taken upon check-in for potential deep cleaning or damage.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Hay-Adams in Washington D.C.
ld.description: Though today’s White House may not be the universally respected institution that it was in less partisan times, just across the street is another Washington D.C. fixture that’s lost none of its luster. The Hay-Adams is a 1928 Italian Renaissance monument, one whose privacy and discretion are near-legendary, and whose location, with the White House and the National Mall as a backdrop, is one-of-a-kind. Constant attention has kept it looking as opulent as can be, while constant technological improvements mean that, beneath its old-world elegance, The Hay-Adams is a thoroughly modern luxury hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Jefferson in Washington D.C.
ld.description: As the capital city of the United States it’s only natural that Washington D.C. should be home to a fair number of grand, historic luxury hotels. Not all of them are quite as old-world as they seem, though. The Jefferson certainly has all the opulence and historical atmosphere you’d expect from one of the original grand dames, and the fact that it’s mostly the result of a 2009 renovation is neither here nor there.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The Swag in Waynesville
ld.description: Right on the edge of the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, nearly a mile above sea level, is one of the region’s best-kept secrets. The Swag started its life as a private home, but gradually evolved into an inn; now, after the addition of a second lodge and a handful of outlying cabins, it’s something more akin to a luxury boutique resort.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Resort and Residences Whistler

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort and Residences Whistler in Whistler
ld.description: The Coast Mountains are famously wild and untamed. But that doesn’t mean their hotels have to be. In fact, there’s an opportunity there for the sort of inspiring contrast that some of the best hotels are made of. Take a vibrant and relatively unpretentious British Columbia ski town and add a thoroughly polished contemporary-style luxury resort and you’ve got the makings of some fruitful contradictions. This is the Four Seasons Resort Whistler.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Nita Lake Lodge Resort & Spa in Whistler

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fairmont Chateau Whistler in Whistler
ld.description: We don’t mean to offend anyone in Colorado, California or Vermont when we say Whistler and Blackcomb are home to North America’s best skiing and snowboarding; it’s merely a statement of fact. Blessed with the longest season and the greatest vertical drop of any resort on the continent, in addition to dozens of feet of Pacific Northwest snowfall every year, Whistler is not just the Canadian ski capital, but an international destination as well.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: ARRIVE Wilmington in Wilmington
ld.description: The Arrive hotels are a Palisociety venture, and the concept is simple enough: the same impeccable taste and welcoming vibe familiar from their Californian originals, applied to some of the most unique neighborhoods all across the country. Arrive Wilmington is painstakingly tailored to its setting, a marriage of three historic structures in the waterfront district, and combines a bit of rough-edged post-industrial patina with genteel Southern charm — in typical Palisociety style it’s decorated with whimsical patterned wallpaper and an eclectic array of furnishings, including antiques, mid-century modern pieces, and contemporary additions.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Dreamers BnB in Wilmington
ld.description: An 1895 Queen Anne–style house on the edge of Wilmington’s riverside downtown district provides the setting for a unique guest house. Dreamers Welcome is worthy of its name, its interiors expertly designed, full of contemporary artworks, modern furniture, and one-of-a-kind antiques. Some are soothing in white, cream, and blond wood, others more intense in patterned wallpapers or floor-to-ceiling Klein blue; all are as comfortable as can be. It’s more than just a collection of bedrooms, too — there’s a delightful little reading room, some excellent porches for lounging, and a fine vegan breakfast by Californian chef Anna Masteller.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Woodstock Inn & Resort in Woodstock
ld.description: Vermont may have a reputation for low-frills, homespun charm, as does the word Woodstock, with its hippie-era associations. But this is an entirely different Woodstock, both literally and figuratively. The Woodstock Inn, in the Vermont town of the same name, was founded by Laurance Rockefeller — in 1969, ironically enough — and though it’s recently undergone a thorough renovation, it’s stayed true to its aristocratic spirit: this is one of the most elegantly luxurious hotels, not only in Vermont, but in the whole of the Northeast.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed in our Garden Level King rooms and the Morgan House.    There is a $150 (plus tax) pet fee per stay ($250 in the Morgan House).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Cala de Mar Resort & Spa Ixtapa

ld.name: Cala de Mar Resort & Spa Ixtapa in Zihuatanejo
ld.description: Overdevelopment has taught many of us to approach Mexico’s resort towns with some trepidation, but here’s one that just might restore our faith. Cala de Mar Resort & Spa Ixtapa, clinging as it does to a cliff face on Mexico’s pacific coast, its rooms and suites cascading down towards the water.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: La Casa que Canta in Zihuatanejo
ld.description: If the scale of Mexican mass tourism puts you off, you’ve got options — Zihuatanejo, just four miles down the coast from Ixtapa, was until recently little more than a quiet fishing village, and even now is steeped in the kind of small-town charm Ixtapa never had.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Playa Viva in Zihuatanejo
ld.description: Take everything that annoys you about mass tourism on the Mexican coasts and put it out of your mind. Whatever your mental image, Playa Viva is more or less the opposite of that. A mere 20 casitas, for starters, is about as far as it gets from mass tourism in the first place. And this location, on protected land a half hour outside of Zihuatanejo, has a long, long way to go before it could be considered developed, much less overdeveloped.
